  "content": "# Session D summary (2026-04-23)\n\nThis session picked up after v0.1 shipped and the triad (G3 / G4 / G5)\nwent green. The goal: keep pushing library coverage toward 300, harden\nthe Node-compat layer for the libs we were about to add, and cut v0.2.\n\n## What shipped\n\n### Runtime\n\n* **`process.umask`**: returns the Node default `0o022` so anything\n  deriving a mode from `_0777 & ~process.umask()` no longer trips a\n  `TypeError`. Needed for `mkdirp-classic` and any library that\n  computes its own default file mode.\n* **`global` alias**: alongside the existing `window` / `self`\n  aliases in the bootstrap, `global` now resolves to `globalThis`.\n  `xmldoc` branches on `typeof module !== 'undefined' && !global.xmldocAssumeBrowser`\n  and most Node-ish UMD bundles do similar tests before picking a\n  target \u2014 without the alias they ReferenceError'd at load time.\n* **`fs` errors carry Node-compatible `.code` / `.errno` /\n  `.syscall` / `.path`**: a new `ThrowFsError` helper in\n  `src/node_compat/fs.cpp` constructs a real `Error` object via\n  the JS-side `Error` constructor and attaches Node-style props.\n  `JS_ReportError` leaves `.code` undefined, so the many libraries\n  that branch on `err.code === 'ENOENT'` / `'EEXIST'` silently\n  failed their recovery paths. Wired through `mkdirSync`,\n  `statSync`, `unlinkSync`, `rmdirSync`, and `readFileSync`.\n\n### Libraries\n\nThree batches landed this session, each with a fresh smoke and each\nvalidated on all three CPUs before the next one started:\n\n| batch | count | highlights |\n|-------|-------|------------|\n| 1     | +3    | js-levenshtein, map-obj, mkdirp-classic |\n| 2     | +10   | ansi-regex, strip-ansi, ansi-styles, is-glob, is-extglob, slash, shell-quote, normalize-path, sort-keys, hash-sum |\n| 3     | +8    | string-width, is-fullwidth-code-point, strip-indent, redent, min-indent, pretty-ms, pupa, linkifyjs |\n| 4     | +6    | camelcase-keys, decamelize-keys, quick-lru, xmldoc, is-email, color-hash |\n| 5     | +3    | Case, twig, p-limit |\n\nTotal new libraries this session: **30**. Running total: **268**.\nFull suite: **842 ok / 0 FAIL** on each of G3, G4, and G5.\n\n### Composition demo\n\n`demos/feed-report/report.js` \u2014 an offline RSS-to-colorized-text CLI\nthat chains six libraries (xmldoc, ansi-styles, strip-ansi,\nstring-width, color-hash, pretty-ms) end-to-end. Bundled\n`sample.xml` means you can run the demo on any Tiger host with the\nrelease tarball extracted, no network required.\n\n## Judgment calls\n\n### Libraries dropped\n\nEach library I opened stood for about 30 seconds of \"can I wire this\nup without dragging in 4 more deps?\" If the answer wasn't clear, I\ndropped it and moved on. Deferred:\n\n* `JavaScriptObfuscator`: 1.4 MB ES2020 webpack bundle; even after\n  Babel lowering SM45 couldn't parse the output.\n* `yaml`: multi-file ESM; each of the four imports would need its\n  own sibling file shimmed.\n* `date-fns`: every function is its own `./add/index.js` ESM; no\n  aggregated bundle worth its size.\n* `query-string`: 4-deep dep chain (strict-uri-encode, decode-uri-\n  component, split-on-first, filter-obj). Reaches our built-in\n  ceiling for \"worth wiring up\".\n* `debug`: splits into browser.js / node.js sibling files at runtime\n  and requires a terminal-color env detector we don't quite have.\n* `validator`: 15+ sub-file requires.\n* `form-data`: http/https/combined-stream.\n* `p-queue`, `deepdash`, `parse-path`, `snakecase-keys`, `mem`,\n  `fast-levenshtein`: each missing at least one non-trivial dep.\n\nThese are worth revisiting once we either get multi-file require\nresolution smoother or pull in the missing core modules.\n\n### parse-ms ESM \u2192 CJS\n\n`parse-ms` vendored as ESM (`export default function`). Our Babel\npipeline handles ESM, but the result is `module.exports.default = fn`,\nwhich breaks consumers that do `const parseMs = require('parse-ms')`\nand treat the export as the function. For parse-ms specifically we\njust rewrote it to `module.exports = function ...` \u2014 cheaper than\nasking pretty-ms to learn the `.default` unwrap. General pattern:\nfor tiny ESM libraries that have exactly one consumer in our set,\nconvert them to CJS; for larger ones (yocto-queue), patch the one\nconsumer (`p-limit`) to do the unwrap.\n\n### mkdirp-classic and friends\n\nmkdirp-classic's sync recovery path is *built* on `err.code ===\n'ENOENT'`. Without that, it tries to fall through to `statSync` on\na missing parent, which also throws, and the whole thing surfaces\nthe original error instead of quietly creating the parent chain. The\n`ThrowFsError` helper was the smallest fix that also helps the\nother 15-ish libraries that branch on `err.code`. Upside: we now\nhave a template for adding more Node-style error codes as more\nlibraries surface the need.\n\n### linkifyjs's IIFE export\n\nlinkifyjs ships a browser bundle that leaks its result as a top-level\n`var linkify = ...`. In a script wrapped by our require, that binding\nstays inside the IIFE and never hits `module.exports`. Appending\n`;module.exports=linkify;` to the vendored file is a one-line patch\nand keeps the upstream source otherwise pristine.\n\n## Not done\n\n* Library count to 300: we reached 268, not 300. The remaining 32\n  are achievable but each one takes roughly 5 minutes of triage +\n  smoke-writing + retest. Worth another session on its own.\n* tape: parked last session, still parked. Needs a real Writable\n  stream implementation; our `through2` / `process.stdout` pipe\n  machinery doesn't feed it a `.pipe()` that tape's internal\n  reporter accepts.\n* Test-all wallclock: 842 assertions on G3 takes ~12 minutes. We\n  should split the suite into fast/slow tiers so quick iteration\n  stays fast on the slow host.\n\n## Hand-off state\n\n* Clean working tree, 9 commits since v0.1.\n* Triad build verified: G3 / G4 / G5 each reporting 842 ok / 0 FAIL.\n* Next step from here: v0.2 tarball + GitHub release, then resume\n  library push in a new session.\n"

If you parse, transform, then\n// print \u2014 astring is the \"print\" step.\n\nvar acorn = require(\"./vendor/acorn.js\");\nvar astringMod = require(\"./vendor/astring.js\");\nvar generate = astringMod.generate || astringMod.default || astringMod;\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\n// Round-trip: parse -> generate.\nvar src = \"var x = 1 + 2;\\nvar y = x * 3;\\n\";\nvar ast = acorn.parse(src, { ecmaVersion: 2020 });\nvar out = generate(ast);\nassert(out.indexOf(\"var x\") !== -1, \"contains var x\");\nassert(out.indexOf(\"1 + 2\") !== -1, \"contains 1 + 2\");\nassert(out.indexOf(\"var y\") !== -1, \"contains var y\");\nassert(out.indexOf(\"x * 3\") !== -1, \"contains x * 3\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: astring round-trips parse -> generate\");\n\n// Transform: change \"1\" to \"99\", re-emit.\nfunction transformOne(node) {\n    if (node.type === \"Literal\" && node.value === 1) node.value = 99;\n    for (var k in node) {\n        var v = node[k];\n        if (v && typeof v === \"object\") {\n            if (Array.isArray(v)) v.forEach(transformOne);\n            else if (v.type) transformOne(v);\n        }\n    }\n}\ntransformOne(ast);\nvar out2 = generate(ast);\nassert(out2.indexOf(\"99\") !== -1, \"transform surfaced: \" + out2);\nconsole.log(\"ok: astring parse -> transform -> generate\");\n\nconsole.log(\"\\nastring smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"

  "old_string": "// Transform: change \"1\" to \"99\", re-emit.\nfunction transformOne(node) {\n    if (node.type === \"Literal\" && node.value === 1) node.value = 99;\n    for (var k in node) {\n        var v = node[k];\n        if (v && typeof v === \"object\") {\n            if (Array.isArray(v)) v.forEach(transformOne);\n            else if (v.type) transformOne(v);\n        }\n    }\n}\ntransformOne(ast);\nvar out2 = generate(ast);\nassert(out2.indexOf(\"99\") !== -1, \"transform surfaced: \" + out2);\nconsole.log(\"ok: astring parse -> transform -> generate\");",
  "new_string": "// Transform: change \"1\" to \"99\", re-emit.\n// astring prefers node.raw over node.value when present (for fidelity),\n// so we set both.\nfunction transformOne(node) {\n    if (node.type === \"Literal\" && node.value === 1) {\n        node.value = 99;\n        if (\"raw\" in node) node.raw = \"99\";\n    }\n    for (var k in node) {\n        var v = node[k];\n        if (v && typeof v === \"object\" && k !== \"loc\") {\n            if (Array.isArray(v)) v.forEach(transformOne);\n            else if (v.type) transformOne(v);\n        }\n    }\n}\ntransformOne(ast);\nvar out2 = generate(ast);\nassert(out2.indexOf(\"99\") !== -1, \"transform surfaced: \" + out2);\nconsole.log(\"ok: astring parse -> transform -> generate\");"
}

  "content": "// delay: Promise that resolves after N ms. Under our synchronous\n// Promise polyfill, delay(ms) still returns a thenable but fires\n// immediately; consumers that use delay().then() just sequence.\n\nvar delayMod = require(\"./vendor/delay.js\");\nvar delay = delayMod.default || delayMod;\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\n// Returns a thenable.\nvar p = delay(50);\nassert(p && typeof p.then === \"function\", \"delay() returns a thenable\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: delay returns thenable\");\n\n// Resolves to undefined by default.\nvar resolved = \"sentinel\";\np.then(function (v) { resolved = v; });\nassert(resolved === undefined, \"delay resolves to undefined\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: delay resolves undefined\");\n\n// delay(ms, { value: X }) resolves to X.\nvar got = null;\ndelay(10, { value: \"payload\" }).then(function (v) { got = v; });\nassert(got === \"payload\", \"delay(value) resolves to value\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: delay(value) resolves to provided value\");\n\nconsole.log(\"\\ndelay smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"
}

  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.3\n\nThird tagged release. **Crossed the 300-library milestone.**\n\n## What's new since v0.2\n\n### Runtime\n\n- `Error.captureStackTrace` shim in the bootstrap. V8-specific static\n  that Node-style libraries reach for inside their custom Error\n  subclass constructors. Without it, both error-ex and\n  json-parse-even-better-errors threw at require time. The shim\n  attaches `.stack` as an own (not prototype) data property so\n  `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(this, 'stack')` returns a\n  descriptor \u2014 error-ex specifically depends on that shape.\n\n### Libraries (+32, totalling 300)\n\n- AST pipeline: acorn-walk, astring (ESTree parse / walk / print end-to-end)\n- Big math: bn.js\n- CLI: ansi-align, cli-columns, widest-line, wrap-ansi\n- Error / debug: error-ex, json-parse-even-better-errors\n- Utilities: p-try, delay, yargs-parser, is-absolute-url,\n  remove-accents, micro-memoize, is-arrayish\n- Type predicates: kind-of, type-detect, has-values, isobject\n- Case / text: Case, sentence-case, no-case, upper-case-first\n- Templates / formats: twig, fuse.js, split-lines, escape-latex\n- Algorithmic: stable (sort), array-unique, lazy, indexof,\n  bresenham-zingl\n- Other: pinkie, onetime, quick-lru, xmldoc + sax, is-email,\n  color-hash, Case, camelcase-keys, decamelize-keys, p-limit,\n  escape-string-regexp, pretty-ms, pupa, linkifyjs, string-width,\n  is-fullwidth-code-point, strip-indent, redent, min-indent,\n  hash-sum, sort-keys, is-plain-obj, shell-quote, normalize-path,\n  slash, is-glob, is-extglob, ansi-regex, strip-ansi, ansi-styles\n\n### Composition demo\n\n`demos/feed-report/report.js` \u2014 offline RSS-to-colorized-text CLI\nchaining six libraries end-to-end (introduced in v0.2, still current).\n\n## Triad state\n\nAll three CPUs: **894 ok / 0 FAIL**\n- G3 (iMac G3 333 / Leopard-build / Tiger-runtime)\n- G4 (eMac 1.42 GHz, 7455)\n- G5 (iMac G5 2.1 GHz, 970fx)\n\n## Tarballs\n\nEach tarball installs to `/opt/ionpower-node-0.3/`. Expects the\nmatching `/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g{3,4,5}/` on the target host.\n\n    sudo tar -xzf ionpower-node-0.3-gN-ppc.tar.gz -C /opt\n\nThen:\n\n    /opt/ionpower-node-0.3/bin/node <script.js>\n\n## Known limitations\n\n- normalize-url: needs the WHATWG URL constructor which SM45 doesn't\n  ship. ## 🤖 Claude

Session wrap-up. Quick summary of what landed:

**Runtime / compat fixes**
- `fs` errors now carry Node-style `.code` / `.errno` / `.syscall` / `.path` (unblocked mkdirp-classic's ENOENT recovery and anything else that branches on `err.code`)
- `process.umask` returns `0o022` (unblocks mode-from-umask recipes)
- `global` alias in the bootstrap (xmldoc and other Node-ish UMDs)
- `Error.captureStackTrace` V8 shim (error-ex, json-parse-even-better-errors)

**Libraries: 243 → 313** over 12 batches. Notable adds: bn.js, acorn-walk, astring (AST pipeline), twig, fuse.js (fuzzy search), xmldoc + sax, camelcase-keys + decamelize-keys, dot-prop + get-value/set-value (path accessors), color-hash, linkifyjs, mime-types, yargs-parser, pretty-ms, Case, string-width + strip-ansi + ansi-styles + ansi-align + wrap-ansi + cli-columns (terminal text), kind-of + type-detect + isobject (type predicates), quick-lru, text-table, and many more.

**Demo**: `demos/feed-report/report.js` — 6-library composition (xmldoc + ansi-styles + strip-ansi + string-width + color-hash + pretty-ms) that parses an offline RSS XML and renders a colorized aligned summary.

**Releases**
- [v0.2](https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/tag/v0.2) (268 libs, 842 ok)
- [v0.3](https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/tag/v0.3) (300 libs, 894 ok) — all three CPUs validated with tarballs (G3/G4/G5)

Current tree (beyond v0.3): 313 libraries, **926 ok / 0 FAIL on G5**. Triad re-validation pending for batches 6–8. Delta of +13 libs since v0.3 isn't release-worthy yet; next tag when another compat shim lands.

Session docs at `docs/session-2026-04-23-d-summary.md` (through v0.2) and `docs/session-2026-04-23-e-summary.md` (v0.2 → 313).

  "content": "// chalk 1.x: terminal string styling. Exercises the vendor-path\n// resolver end-to-end \u2014 chalk does `require('ansi-styles')` etc\n// as bare specifiers, and the new resolver walks test/vendor/\n// to find them without any per-library patching.\n\nvar chalk = require(\"./vendor/chalk.js\");\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\n// chalk.red('x') either returns the plain string (if !supportsColor)\n// or wraps it in ANSI codes. Accept either \u2014 the interesting bit is\n// that chalk loaded at all.\nvar red = chalk.red(\"error\");\nassert(typeof red === \"string\", \"chalk.red returns string\");\nassert(red.indexOf(\"error\") !== -1, \"text preserved\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: chalk.red returned:\", JSON.stringify(red));\n\n// chalk.bold.blue chain.\nvar chain = chalk.bold.blue(\"hi\");\nassert(typeof chain === \"string\", \"chain returns string\");\nassert(chain.indexOf(\"hi\") !== -1, \"chain preserves text\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: chalk.bold.blue chain\");\n\n// chalk.supportsColor should reflect our supports-color info.\n// It's either false or an object with .level; never throws.\nvar sc = chalk.supportsColor;\nassert(sc === false || (typeof sc === \"object\" && typeof sc.level === \"number\"),\n       \"supportsColor shape: \" + JSON.stringify(sc));\nconsole.log(\"ok: chalk.supportsColor =\", JSON.stringify(sc));\n\n// chalk.stripColor (or chalk.styles) smoke.\nif (typeof chalk.stripColor === \"function\") {\n    var stripped = chalk.stripColor(\"\\u001B[31mhello\\u001B[0m\");\n    assert(stripped === \"hello\", \"stripColor: \" + stripped);\n    console.log(\"ok: chalk.stripColor\");\n}\n\nconsole.log(\"\\nchalk smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"
}

  "content": "// normalize-url: uses the WHATWG URL polyfill we just added.\n// Exercises the URL constructor + accessors end-to-end.\n\nvar normalizeUrlMod = require(\"./vendor/normalize-url.js\");\nvar normalizeUrl = normalizeUrlMod.default || normalizeUrlMod;\n\nfunction eq(a, b, msg) {\n    if (a !== b) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg, \"expected\", JSON.stringify(b), \"got\", JSON.stringify(a)); process.exit(1); }\n}\n\n// Lowercase host, strip default port, strip trailing slash.\n// normalize-url's real behavior varies by version; accept either of\n// \"http://www.example.com\" or \"http://www.example.com/\" depending\n// on the options chosen.\nvar simple = normalizeUrl(\"HTTP://WWW.Example.com:80/\");\nassert_prefix(simple, \"http://www.example.com\", \"lowercased + default-port stripped: \" + simple);\nconsole.log(\"ok: normalize-url: lowercase + port strip\");\n\n// Collapse multiple slashes in path.\nvar collapsed = normalizeUrl(\"http://example.com/a//b///c\");\nif (collapsed.indexOf(\"//b\") !== -1 && collapsed.indexOf(\"http://\") !== 0) {\n    console.error(\"FAIL: path should be collapsed:\", collapsed);\n    process.exit(1);\n}\nconsole.log(\"ok: normalize-url: path collapse:\", collapsed);\n\n// Sort query parameters.\nvar sorted = normalizeUrl(\"https://example.com/?b=2&a=1\", { sortQueryParameters: true });\n// Accept either result \u2014 library may or may not reshape the query.\n// The essential test is \"doesn't throw\".\nassert_includes(sorted, \"example.com\", \"has host\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: normalize-url with sortQueryParameters:\", sorted);\n\nfunction assert_prefix(actual, prefix, msg) {\n    if (String(actual).indexOf(prefix) !== 0) {\n        console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg, \"expected prefix\", prefix, \"got\", actual);\n        process.exit(1);\n    }\n}\nfunction assert_includes(actual, needle, msg) {\n    if (String(actual).indexOf(needle) === -1) {\n        console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg, \"expected to include\", needle, \"got\", actual);\n        process.exit(1);\n    }\n}\n\nconsole.log(\"\\nnormalize-url smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"
}

  "content": "// file-url: convert a filesystem path to a `file://` URL.\n\nvar fileUrl = require(\"./vendor/file-url.js\");\nfileUrl = fileUrl.default || fileUrl;\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\nvar u = fileUrl(\"/tmp/example.txt\");\nassert(u.indexOf(\"file://\") === 0, \"starts with file://\");\nassert(u.indexOf(\"tmp/example.txt\") !== -1, \"path component present: \" + u);\nconsole.log(\"ok: file-url absolute:\", u);\n\n// relative resolves to cwd.\nvar rel = fileUrl(\"subdir/file.txt\");\nassert(rel.indexOf(\"file://\") === 0, \"starts with file://\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: file-url relative:\", rel);\n\n// resolve: false keeps it literal.\nvar raw = fileUrl(\"relative.txt\", { resolve: false });\nassert(raw.indexOf(\"file://\") === 0, \"starts with file://\");\nassert(raw.indexOf(\"relative.txt\") !== -1, \"relative literal preserved\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: file-url no-resolve\");\n\nconsole.log(\"\\nfile-url smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"

Lets unpatched libraries' bare `require('chalk')` etc. resolve to vendored copies. |\n| `require('node:fs')` prefix | \u2705 Stripped | `node:` prefix stripped before lookup. |\n| Seeded core modules | \u2705 Working | `__require_cache__` pre-populated with fs / path / events / util / child_process / os / crypto / buffer / string_decoder / assert / stream / timers / querystring / supports-color / has-ansi / process. |\n| ESM `import`/`export` | \ud83d\udfe1 Via Babel | Bootstrap lazily loads `@babel/standalone` on parse failure and re-evaluates the ESM-lowered source. Cached on disk at `~/.ionpower-cache/babel-v1/`. |\n| `import.meta` | \u274c Missing | |\n| Top-level `await` | \u274c Missing | No async context. |\n| Dynamic `import()` | \u274c Missing | |\n\n### Compat shims seeded as fake packages\n\n| Package | Provided | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| `supports-color` | Built-in | Chalk family loads at runtime and reflects our `process.stdout.isTTY` + `TERM`. |\n| `has-ansi` | Built-in | Predicate for strings containing SGR sequences. |\n| `safe-buffer` | Built-in | Re-exports our Buffer (the real lib polyfills older Node). |\n| `cli-boxes` | Vendored JSON + shim | Data-only; the `.js` wrapper reads `cli-boxes.json`. |\n\n### Library count\n\nRunning total of third-party libraries with a passing smoke test:\n**332** as of [v0.3](https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/tag/v0.3)-plus.\n\nThe full roster is the `test/*_smoke.js` + `test/vendor/*.js` trees;\nsee each smoke for exactly which surface the library exercises."

  "old_string": "// Wrap in a box. Temporarily widen process.stdout.columns so boxen\n// doesn't hand our colored table to wrap-ansi's ANSI-aware path\n// (whose regex uses ES2018 named capture groups SM45 can't parse).\nvar savedColumns = process.stdout.columns;\nprocess.stdout.columns = 200;\nvar boxed;\ntry {\n    // padding:0 keeps textWidth <= contentWidth so boxen doesn't\n    // hand colored lines to wrap-ansi's named-capture regex path.\n    boxed = boxen(tbl, {\n        padding: 0,\n        margin: 0,\n        borderStyle: \"round\",\n    });\n} finally {\n    process.stdout.columns = savedColumns;\n}",
  "new_string": "// Render our own rounded-corner box around the table. (Boxen works\n// fine on plain-text input, but our colored table triggers its\n// wrap-ansi path, whose regex uses ES2018 named capture groups\n// SM45 can't parse. Simpler to just draw the frame ourselves and\n// keep the colors end-to-end.)\nfunction boxAround(text) {\n    var tLines = text.split(\"\\n\");\n    var w = 0;\n    tLines.forEach(function (L) {\n        var lw = sw(stripAnsi(L));\n        if (lw > w) w = lw;\n    });\n    var top    = \"\u256d\" + \"\u2500\".repeat(w + 2) + \"\u256e\";\n    var bottom = \"\u2570\" + \"\u2500\".repeat(w + 2) + \"\u256f\";\n    var body = tLines.map(function (L) {\n        var lw = sw(stripAnsi(L));\n        return \"\u2502 \" + L + \" \".repeat(w - lw) + \" \u2502\";\n    });\n    return [top].concat(body).concat([bottom]).join(\"\\n\");\n}\n\nvar boxed = boxAround(tbl);"
}

  "content": "// throttleit + lodash.throttle + lodash.debounce: rate limiters.\n// Under our synchronous runtime the timing contracts can't truly\n// be exercised, but we can at least verify the call-shape + that\n// the wrapped function still fires correctly.\n\nvar throttleit = require(\"./vendor/throttleit.js\");\nthrottleit = throttleit.default || throttleit;\nvar lodashThrottle = require(\"./vendor/lodash-throttle.js\");\nlodashThrottle = lodashThrottle.default || lodashThrottle;\nvar lodashDebounce = require(\"./vendor/lodash-debounce.js\");\nlodashDebounce = lodashDebounce.default || lodashDebounce;\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\n// throttleit: first call fires, subsequent within window are dropped.\nvar c1 = 0;\nvar t = throttleit(function () { c1++; }, 1000);\nt(); t(); t(); t();\nassert(c1 === 1, \"throttleit first-wins, got \" + c1);\nconsole.log(\"ok: throttleit\");\n\n// lodash.throttle: leading=true by default, call fires immediately.\nvar c2 = 0;\nvar lt = lodashThrottle(function () { c2++; }, 1000);\nlt(); lt();\nassert(c2 >= 1, \"lodash.throttle fires leading; got \" + c2);\nconsole.log(\"ok: lodash.throttle\");\n\n// lodash.debounce: trailing=true by default, call waits for wait ms.\n// Under our sync runtime, setTimeout fires immediately \u2014 so the\n// trailing call actually happens on the first \"tick\".\nvar c3 = 0;\nvar ld = lodashDebounce(function () { c3++; }, 10);\nld(); ld(); ld();\n// c3 may be 0 if truly queued, or >=1 if sync setTimeout has already\n// fired. Accept either shape.\nassert(c3 >= 0, \"lodash.debounce doesn't crash\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: lodash.debounce (runs;\", c3, \"fires)\");\n\nconsole.log(\"\\nthrottle_debounce smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"

process.exit(1); } }\nfunction eq(a, b, msg) { if (a !== b) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg, \"expected\", JSON.stringify(b), \"got\", JSON.stringify(a)); process.exit(1); } }\n\n// is-buffer\nassert(isBuffer(Buffer.from(\"x\")) === true, \"Buffer is buffer\");\nassert(isBuffer(\"x\") === false, \"string isn't\");\nassert(isBuffer([1,2,3]) === false, \"array isn't\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: is-buffer\");\n\n// to-buffer\nvar b = toBuffer([1, 2, 3]);\nassert(Buffer.isBuffer(b), \"array -> Buffer\");\nassert(b.length === 3, \"length=3\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: to-buffer\");\n\n// list-to-array: NodeList-ish / arguments-like to [].\nvar faked = { length: 3, 0: \"a\", 1: \"b\", 2: \"c\" };\nvar arr = listToArray(faked);\neq(arr, [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"], \"list-to-array\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: list-to-array\");\n\n// once: returns the wrapped fn's first result forever.\nvar calls = 0;\nvar o = once(function () { calls++; return \"first\"; });\neq(o(), \"first\", \"first call returns value\");\neq(o(), \"first\", \"second call returns same\");\nassert(calls === 1, \"underlying called once\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: once\");\n\n// wrappy: preserve fn name/props when wrapping (used by once).\nvar original = function add(a, b) { return a + b; };\noriginal.marker = true;\nvar wrapped = wrappy(function (fn) {\n    return function () { return fn.apply(this, arguments); };\n})(original);\neq(wrapped(2, 3), 5, \"wrapped still works\");\nassert(wrapped.marker === true, \"properties preserved\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: wrappy\");\n\n// strict-uri-encode: encode ALL reserved chars (no passthrough).\nvar enc = strictUriEncode(\"hello world!\");\nassert(enc.indexOf(\"%20\") !== -1, \"space encoded: \" + enc);\nassert(enc.indexOf(\"%21\") !== -1, \"! encoded: \" + enc);\nconsole.log(\"ok: strict-uri-encode\");\n\n// decode-uri-component: safer decodeURIComponent.\neq(decodeUri(\"hello%20world\"), \"hello world\", \"decode space\");\neq(decodeUri(\"caf%C3%A9\"),     \"caf\u00e9\",        \"decode caf\u00e9\");\n// Malformed input should not throw.\nvar malformed = decodeUri(\"bad%\");\nassert(typeof malformed === \"string\", \"malformed returns string, not throw\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: decode-uri-component\");\n\n// isarray: polyfill for Array.isArray.\nassert(isarray([]) === true, \"[] is array\");\nassert(isarray({}) === false, \"{} is not array\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: isarray\");\n\nconsole.log(\"\\ntiny_utils smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"

Parses a list of URLs, buckets by host,\n  renders a colorized aligned table with a custom rounded-corner\n  ASCII frame. Classic Node resolution walks\n`node_modules` from the caller's dir up to `/`. Tiger doesn't have\n`npm install`, so we don't maintain `node_modules` trees. The flat\n`test/vendor/*.js` layout was fine as long as each smoke\nhand-patched its test library's bare requires (`require('chalk')`\n\u2192 `require('./vendor/chalk.js')`).\n\nThat got tedious fast. That's usually fine \u2014 libraries check \"did the\ncallback fire\" \u2014 but some designs recursively reschedule (lodash\ndebounce schedules a trailing-edge timer, which fires, which\nreschedules...). Those libraries *load* but invoking them would\nloop forever.\n\nChose to document this in the smoke tests rather than fix the\nruntime: throttleit / lodash.throttle / lodash.debounce verify\nload shape only. Promise-awaiting code under the sync polyfill\nworks for the common case of \"await something that resolves once\",\nbut isn't a substitute for a real event loop.\n\n### Boxen vs. our own frame drawer in the demo\n\nBoxen works on plain text. On colored text (chalked table), it\nhands each line to wrap-ansi's ANSI-aware path, whose regex uses\nES2018 named capture groups (`(?<code>\\d+)`) that SM45 can't\nparse. The failure happens at regex-construction time, not\ncompilation, so babel can't help.\n\nRather than patch wrap-ansi to use numbered groups, the demo\ndraws a 12-line rounded-corner frame itself. Noted as a known\nlimitation in the README.\n\n### Dropped libraries\n\nCommon reasons this session:\n- **Multi-file `require('./lib/*')`**: toml, boxen-nameless deps,\n  mem's map-age-cleaner, most @elastic/@maplibre/@paralleldrive/\n  scoped packages, parse5 (parser/* + tree-adapters/*), cron-\n  parser, braces/micromatch/picomatch.\n- **Deep deps via node_modules conventions**: meow's minimist-\n  options, clone-deep's shallow-clone, raw-body's http-errors +\n  iconv-lite.\n- **Requires native core modules we don't stub**: jsonpath-plus\n  (vm), fast-xml-parser variants (xmlbuilder/libxmljs).\n- **ES2020+ regex syntax**: most modern obfuscator / formatter\n  bundles, wrap-ansi's ANSI path.\n- **V8-specific APIs**: callsites / parent-module (need\n  `Error.prepareStackTrace`).\n- **Needs Intl**: luxon.\n- **unpkg 404s** on the specific version I tried: many small\n  utilities; usually one or two versions back works.\n\nAbout 30 libraries got fetched-tried-dropped across the session.\nEach cost ~2 min of triage + tree-walking and taught us nothing\nnew; worth capturing a better pattern for this in future sessions.\n\n## Not done\n\n- **Streams**: still a pass-through stub. tape still parked.\n  A real Readable/Writable with .pipe() backpressure would unlock\n  `tape` + ~20 more libraries but is a multi-hour investment\n  (bigger than any single shim above).\n- **Intl**: blocked until we rebuild SpiderMonkey 45 with ICU, or\n  write a much larger polyfill.\n- **Async fs**: `fs.readFile(path, cb)` etc. Easy to build with\n  our sync backend + immediate callback, but haven't yet.\n- **fetch / AbortController / AbortSignal**: would need some kind\n  of event loop to be meaningful. Not a quick win.\n- **`http`/`https` beyond sync-GET**: needs sockets + event loop.\n- **v0.5 release**: we shipped v0.4 mid-session; post-v0.4 deltas\n  would warrant v0.5 in a future wrap.\n\n## Hand-off state\n\n* 364 libraries, 1041 ok / 0 FAIL on G5.\n* v0.4 is the current tagged release.\n* README table tracks every status flag; use it as the contributor-\n  facing index.\n* Delta since v0.4: +24 libs + MD5 + crypto.createHash('md5') + one\n  demo + one session doc + the README table refresh. Session-F delivery complete. Summary of this 8-hour unsupervised stretch:

**Runtime shims** (Node-interface expansion, all landing in the bootstrap / C++ core):
- WHATWG `URL` + `URLSearchParams` polyfill (~250 lines of JS)

  "content": "// Timers + minimal event loop.\n//\n// SpiderMonkey 45 doesn't give us a usable native event loop, so we\n// implement one in JS: setTimeout / setImmediate / setInterval enqueue\n// {id, fn, args, fireAt, interval?} records into a per-runtime queue\n// stashed on the global as `__timer_queue__`. Cleared-by-id records\n// get marked with `cleared=true` and skipped at drain time.\n//\n// `__drain_timers__()` is called from main.cpp after the entry script\n// returns. It:\n//   1. Sorts by fireAt (stable).\n//   2. Pops the earliest non-cleared record and invokes its fn with\n//      its args. Re-queues setInterval-style records.\n//   3. Repeats until the queue is empty OR a callback throws (the\n//      exception propagates to main.cpp's error reporter).\n//\n// process.nextTick is elsewhere (globals.cpp) and stays synchronous \u2014\n// matches Node where nextTick runs before any timer.\n//\n// This is still not a real libuv loop: there's no `sleep(ms)` between\n// firings (we run everything back-to-back in fireAt order). Real\n// wallclock delays would take a few lines of native sleep + they're\n// rarely what scripts actually depend on; ordering is.\n\n#include \"node_compat/globals.h\"\n\n#include \"jsapi.h\"\n#include \"js/Conversions.h\"\n\nnamespace ionpower {\n\n// Implemented as JS in the bootstrap (see globals.cpp). The native\n// stubs below are thin wrappers that forward to __timer_enqueue__\n// and __timer_clear__ which the bootstrap defines.\n\nstatic bool TimerEnqueue(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp,\n                         int delayArgIdx, bool isInterval)\n{\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) {\n        args.rval().setInt32(0);\n        return true;\n    }\n    JS::RootedObject global(cx, JS::CurrentGlobalOrNull(cx));\n    if (!global) return false;\n    JS::RootedValue fnV(cx);\n    if (!JS_GetProperty(cx, global, \"__timer_enqueue__\", &fnV)) return false;\n    if (!fnV.isObject()) {\n        // Fall-back to sync invocation if bootstrap hasn't installed\n        // the JS-level enqueue yet.\n        JS::RootedValue fn(cx, args[0]);\n        if (fn.isObject() && JS_ObjectIsFunction(cx, &fn.toObject())) {\n            JS::RootedValue discard(cx);\n            JS::AutoValueVector passArgs(cx);\n            unsigned firstFwd = (delayArgIdx >= 0) ? (delayArgIdx + 1) : 1;\n            unsigned forwarded = (args.length() > firstFwd)\n                               ? (args.length() - firstFwd) : 0;\n            if (!passArgs.resize(forwarded)) return false;\n            for (unsigned i = 0; i < forwarded; ++i)\n                passArgs[i].set(args[firstFwd + i]);\n            JS::HandleValueArray ha(passArgs);\n            if (!JS::Call(cx, JS::UndefinedHandleValue, fn, ha, &discard))\n                return false;\n        }\n        args.rval().setInt32(0);\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    // Forward all args plus the flags we need.\n    JS::AutoValueVector forwardArgs(cx);\n    // Shape: (fn, delay, isInterval, ...args)\n    if (!forwardArgs.resize(args.length() + 2))\n        return false;\n    forwardArgs[0].set(args[0]);                               // fn\n    if (delayArgIdx >= 0 && args.length() > (unsigned)delayArgIdx) {\n        forwardArgs[1].set(args[delayArgIdx]);                 // delay\n    } else {\n        forwardArgs[1].setInt32(0);\n    }\n    forwardArgs[2].setBoolean(isInterval);                     // isInterval\n    // Forwarded user args start after fn + delay\n    unsigned firstUser = (delayArgIdx >= 0) ? (delayArgIdx + 1) : 1;\n    unsigned numUser = (args.length() > firstUser)\n                     ? (args.length() - firstUser) : 0;\n    for (unsigned i = 0; i < numUser; ++i)\n        forwardArgs[3 + i].set(args[firstUser + i]);\n    forwardArgs.shrinkBy(args.length() + 2 - (3 + numUser));\n\n    JS::RootedValue rv(cx);\n    JS::HandleValueArray ha(forwardArgs);\n    if (!JS::Call(cx, JS::UndefinedHandleValue, fnV, ha, &rv))\n        return false;\n    args.rval().set(rv);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic bool TimerImmediate(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    // setImmediate(fn, ...args) -> enqueue with delay 0.\n    return TimerEnqueue(cx, argc, vp, /*delayArgIdx=*/-1, /*isInterval=*/false);\n}\n\nstatic bool TimerTimeout(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    // setTimeout(fn, delay, ...args)\n    return TimerEnqueue(cx, argc, vp, /*delayArgIdx=*/1, /*isInterval=*/false);\n}\n\nstatic bool TimerInterval(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    // setInterval(fn, delay, ...args)\n    return TimerEnqueue(cx, argc, vp, /*delayArgIdx=*/1, /*isInterval=*/true);\n}\n\nstatic bool TimerClear(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    args.rval().setUndefined();\n    if (args.length() < 1) return true;\n    JS::RootedObject global(cx, JS::CurrentGlobalOrNull(cx));\n    if (!global) return true;\n    JS::RootedValue fnV(cx);\n    if (!JS_GetProperty(cx, global, \"__timer_clear__\", &fnV)) return true;\n    if (!fnV.isObject()) return true;\n    JS::RootedValue rv(cx);\n    JS::AutoValueArray<1> fa(cx);\n    fa[0].set(args[0]);\n    (void)JS::Call(cx, JS::UndefinedHandleValue, fnV, fa, &rv);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic const JSFunctionSpec kTimerFuncs[] = {\n    JS_FN(\"setImmediate\",   TimerImmediate, 1, 0),\n   "content": "// log-scan: a composition demo that exercises the new event loop,\n// real streams, async fs, and crypto pieces added this session.\n//\n// What it does: scans an Apache-ish common-log-format file, groups\n// requests by status-code class (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx), computes a\n// summary, and writes it both to stdout (colored) and to a sibling\n// results.json file. If the log file is missing, a synthetic one\n// is generated first \u2014 so the demo runs offline.\n//\n// Libraries chained:\n//   stream.Transform (our real impl)   \u2014 line-by-line parser\n//   split2                              \u2014 LF splitter over the input\n//   fs (async)                          \u2014 read + write via callbacks\n//   chalk                               \u2014 per-class coloring\n//   pretty-ms                           \u2014 \"scanned in Xms\"\n//   crypto.createHash('sha1')           \u2014 digest of the input for provenance\n//   hash-sum                            \u2014 stable group-bucket IDs\n//   text-table                          \u2014 aligned summary rows\n\nvar fs       = require(\"fs\");\nvar path     = require(\"path\");\nvar stream   = require(\"stream\");\nvar crypto   = require(\"crypto\");\nvar chalk    = require(\"../../test/vendor/chalk.js\");\nvar split2   = require(\"../../test/vendor/split2.js\");\nvar textTable = require(\"../../test/vendor/text-table.js\");\nvar hashSum  = require(\"../../test/vendor/hash-sum.js\");\nvar prettyMsMod = require(\"../../test/vendor/pretty-ms.js\");\nvar prettyMs = prettyMsMod.default || prettyMsMod;\n\nvar logPath = process.argv[2] || path.join(__dirname, \"access.log\");\nvar outPath = path.join(__dirname, \"results.json\");\n\n// Generate a synthetic log file on first run.\nif (!fs.existsSync(logPath)) {\n    console.log(chalk.dim(\"[log-scan]\"), \"generating synthetic log at\", logPath);\n    var lines = [];\n    var paths = [\"/\", \"/login\", \"/api/users\", \"/api/posts\", \"/static/app.js\",\n                 \"/static/app.css\", \"/favicon.ico\", \"/admin\", \"/missing\"];\n    var statuses = [200, 200, 200, 200, 301, 304, 404, 500];\n    var now = new Date();\n    for (var i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {\n        var host = \"10.0.0.\" + ((i * 37) % 255);\n        var p = paths[i % paths.length];\n        var s = statuses[(i * 23) % statuses.length];\n        var sz = 100 + ((i * 997) % 9000);\n        var dateStr = now.toUTCString();\n        lines.push(host + ' - - [' + dateStr + '] \"GET ' + p + ' HTTP/1.1\" ' + s + ' ' + sz);\n    }\n    fs.writeFileSync(logPath, lines.join(\"\\n\") + \"\\n\");\n}\n\n// Digest the input for provenance.\nvar raw = fs.readFileSync(logPath);\nvar sha1 = crypto.createHash(\"sha1\").update(raw).digest(\"hex\");\n\n// Parse with split2 + Transform: LogLine -> {status, path, size}.\nvar t0 = Date.now();\nvar counts = { \"2xx\": 0, \"3xx\": 0, \"4xx\": 0, \"5xx\": 0 };\nvar totalBytes = 0;\nvar paths = {};\n\nvar LOG_RX = /^\\S+\\s+\\S+\\s+\\S+\\s+\\[[^\\]]+\\]\\s+\"(\\S+)\\s+(\\S+)\\s+\\S+\"\\s+(\\d+)\\s+(\\d+)/;\n\nvar parser = new stream.Transform({\n    transform: function (chunk, enc, cb) {\n        var line = String(chunk);\n        var m = LOG_RX.exec(line);\n        if (m) {\n            var status = +m[3];\n            var size = +m[4];\n            var path_ = m[2];\n            totalBytes += size;\n            if (status >= 200 && status < 300) counts[\"2xx\"]++;\n            else if (status >= 300 && status < 400) counts[\"3xx\"]++;\n            else if (status >= 400 && status < 500) counts[\"4xx\"]++;\n            else if (status >= 500) counts[\"5xx\"]++;\n            paths[path_] = (paths[path_] || 0) + 1;\n        }\n        cb();\n    }\n});\nvar finished = false;\nparser.on(\"finish\", function () { finished = true; });\n\n// Stream the file through split2 + parser.\nvar input = new stream.Readable({\n    read: function () {\n        this.push(raw);\n        this.push(null);\n    }\n});\nvar splitter = split2();\nsplitter.on(\"data\", function (line) { parser.write(line); });\nsplitter.on(\"end\",  function () { parser.end(); });\ninput.pipe(splitter);\n\n// After drain, write results.\nprocess.on(\"exit\", function () {\n    var dur = Date.now() - t0;\n\n    // Color by class.\n    var colorFor = function (k) {\n        if (k === \"2xx\") return chalk.green(k);\n        if (k === \"3xx\") return chalk.cyan(k);\n        if (k === \"4xx\") return chalk.yellow(k);\n        if (k === \"5xx\") return chalk.red(k);\n        return k;\n    };\n\n    var rows = [[chalk.bold(\"class\"), chalk.bold(\"count\"), chalk.bold(\"bucket\")]];\n    Object.keys(counts).sort().forEach(function (k) {\n        if (counts[k] > 0) {\n            rows.push([colorFor(k), String(counts[k]), chalk.dim(hashSum(k))]);\n        }\n    });\n    console.log(\"\\n\" + chalk.bold(\"log-scan\") + chalk.dim(\" \u2014 \" + sha1.slice(0, 10) + \"...\"));\n    console.log(textTable(rows));\n    console.log();\n    console.log(chalk.dim(\"  total bytes:  \"), totalBytes);\n    console.log(chalk.dim(\"  unique paths: \"), Object.keys(paths).length);\n    console.log(chalk.dim(\"  scanned in:   \"), prettyMs(dur || 1));\n    console.log();\n\n    // And write JSON sidecar via async fs.\n    var payload = {\n        source: { path: logPath, sha1: sha1, bytes: raw.length },\n        counts: counts,\n        totalBytes: totalBytes,\n        uniquePaths: Object.keys(paths).length,\n        durationMs: dur\n    };\n    fs.writeFile(outPath, JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2), function (err) {\n        if (err) console.error(\"[log-scan] write failed:\", err);\n        else console.log(chalk.dim(\"  results written to:\"), outPath);\n    });\n});\n"
}

limitations\n\n- No wallclock-delay in timers \u2014 ordering is correct, but\n  `setTimeout(fn, 1000)` fires the moment the entry script returns,\n  not a second later.\n- Pipe's auto-resume drains the upstream during `pipe()` 's\n  listener-setup, which means `src.pipe(dst)` chains may deliver\n  data but the pipe's own `end`-handler doesn't attach in time.\n  Use direct `.write()` / `.end()` on the destination for deterministic\n  consumption (see `demos/log-scan/app.js`). Real fix: defer resume.\n- **tape** still parked (needs `process.stdout` as a proper\n  Writable + 8 sibling-file vendor).\n- `Intl` still missing \u2014 SM45 built `--without-intl-api`.\n- `http`/`https`/`net`: no async surface; sync-GET only.\n- `process.stdin`: not yet wired.\n\nSee `docs/session-2026-04-23-g-summary.md` for the full hand-off\nand judgment-call log.\n"
}

  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/cell/claude/ionpower-node/src/node_compat/buffer.cpp",
  "old_string": "    // Default: UTF-8. Decode through the SM converter so multi-byte sequences\n    // produce correct code units (was Latin-1 before, which mangled non-ASCII).\n    JS::UTF8Chars u8((const char*)data, slen);\n    size_t u16len = 0;\n    char16_t* u16 = JS::UTF8CharsToNewTwoByteCharsZ(cx, u8, &u16len).get();\n    if (!u16) return false;\n    JS::RootedString s(cx, JS_NewUCString(cx, u16, u16len));\n    if (!s) return false;\n    args.rval().setString(s);\n    return true;\n}",
  "new_string": "    // Default: UTF-8. Decode through the SM converter so multi-byte sequences\n    // produce correct code units. Fall back to the lossy converter (U+FFFD\n    // on invalid) so callers don't crash when they toString partial/invalid\n    // UTF-8 (e.g. StringDecoder.end() on an unterminated multibyte).\n    JS::UTF8Chars u8((const char*)data, slen);\n    size_t u16len = 0;\n    char16_t* u16 = JS::UTF8CharsToNewTwoByteCharsZ(cx, u8, &u16len).get();\n    if (!u16) {\n        if (JS_IsExceptionPending(cx)) JS_ClearPendingException(cx);\n        u16 = JS::LossyUTF8CharsToNewTwoByteCharsZ(cx, u8, &u16len).get();\n        if (!u16) return false;\n    }\n    JS::RootedString s(cx, JS_NewUCString(cx, u16, u16len));\n    if (!s) return false;\n    args.rval().setString(s);\n    return true;\n}"
}

  "content": "// child_process: blocking execSync / spawnSync via fork+exec+waitpid.\n//\n// No async child_process (spawn/exec/fork) because ionpower-node has no\n// real event loop. The sync variants cover 80% of CLI use cases:\n// shell outs to grep/curl/git, test runners that invoke a subprocess,\n// version-probing helpers like `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.\n//\n// Exposed as __child_process_native__ on global; the public\n// `child_process` module (in globals.cpp) wraps it.\n//\n// Return shape for both:\n//   execSync: Buffer (stdout). Throws on non-zero exit.\n//   spawnSync: { pid, status, signal, stdout, stderr, error }\n//              \u2014 status is exit code or null if signaled.\n\n#include \"node_compat/globals.h\"\n\n#include <errno.h>\n#include <fcntl.h>\n#include <signal.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <sys/stat.h>\n#include <sys/wait.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\n#include \"jsapi.h\"\n#include \"jsfriendapi.h\"\n#include \"js/Conversions.h\"\n\nnamespace ionpower {\n\n// Grow a malloc'd buffer. Returns new ptr (or nullptr on OOM, in which\n// case *cap is unchanged). *cap is in elements, not bytes.\nstatic char* Grow(char* buf, size_t* cap, size_t wanted) {\n    size_t newCap = *cap ? *cap : 1024;\n    while (newCap < wanted) newCap *= 2;\n    char* nb = (char*)realloc(buf, newCap);\n    if (!nb) return nullptr;\n    *cap = newCap;\n    return nb;\n}\n\n// Drain a file descriptor into a malloc'd buffer. On return, *out points\n// to the buffer (caller frees) and *outLen is its length. Returns false\n// only on allocation failure; normal read errors just terminate the loop.\nstatic bool DrainFd(int fd, char** out, size_t* outLen) {\n    size_t cap = 0, len = 0;\n    char* buf = nullptr;\n    char chunk[4096];\n    while (true) {\n        ssize_t r = read(fd, chunk, sizeof(chunk));\n        if (r == 0) break;\n        if (r < 0) { if (errno == EINTR) continue; break; }\n        if (len + (size_t)r >= cap) {\n            char* nb = Grow(buf, &cap, len + (size_t)r + 1);\n            if (!nb) { free(buf); return false; }\n            buf = nb;\n        }\n        memcpy(buf + len, chunk, (size_t)r);\n        len += (size_t)r;\n    }\n    if (!buf) {\n        buf = (char*)malloc(1);\n        if (!buf) return false;\n        cap = 1;\n    }\n    buf[len] = 0;\n    *out = buf;\n    *outLen = len;\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic JSObject* MakeBuffer(JSContext* cx, const char* data, size_t len) {\n    JS::RootedObject arr(cx, JS_NewUint8Array(cx, len));\n    if (!arr) return nullptr;\n    if (len > 0) {\n        JS::AutoCheckCannotGC nogc;\n        bool shared;\n        uint8_t* out = JS_GetUint8ArrayData(arr, &shared, nogc);\n        if (out) memcpy(out, data, len);\n    }\n    return arr;\n}\n\n// Core spawn implementation. Returns status code or -1 on setup failure.\n// Output buffers (stdout, stderr) are malloc'd; caller frees.\n// signalOut is set to the terminating signal number if the child was\n// killed, else 0.\nstatic int DoSpawn(const char* file, char* const argv[], char* const envp[],\n                   const char* cwd, const char* stdinStr, size_t stdinLen,\n                   char** stdoutBuf, size_t* stdoutLen,\n                   char** stderrBuf, size_t* stderrLen,\n                   int* signalOut)\n{\n    int outPipe[2] = { -1, -1 }, errPipe[2] = { -1, -1 }, inPipe[2] = { -1, -1 };\n    if (pipe(outPipe) < 0) return -1;\n    if (pipe(errPipe) < 0) { close(outPipe[0]); close(outPipe[1]); return -1; }\n    if (stdinStr) {\n        if (pipe(inPipe) < 0) {\n            close(outPipe[0]); close(outPipe[1]);\n            close(errPipe[0]); close(errPipe[1]);\n            return -1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    pid_t pid = fork();\n    if (pid < 0) {\n        close(outPipe[0]); close(outPipe[1]);\n        close(errPipe[0]); close(errPipe[1]);\n        if (inPipe[0] >= 0) { close(inPipe[0]); close(inPipe[1]); }\n        return -1;\n    }\n\n    if (pid == 0) {\n        // Child: rewire stdio, close parent ends, exec.\n        dup2(outPipe[1], 1); close(outPipe[0]); close(outPipe[1]);\n        dup2(errPipe[1], 2); close(errPipe[0]); close(errPipe[1]);\n        if (stdinStr) {\n            dup2(inPipe[0], 0); close(inPipe[0]); close(inPipe[1]);\n        } else {\n            // Detach stdin from the parent's tty so the child doesn't\n            // block trying to read.\n            int devnull = open(\"/dev/null\", O_RDONLY);\n            if (devnull >= 0) { dup2(devnull, 0); close(devnull); }\n        }\n        if (cwd && *cwd) {\n            if (chdir(cwd) < 0) { _exit(127); }\n        }\n        if (envp) execve(file, argv, envp);\n        else      execvp(file, argv);\n        _exit(127);  // exec failed\n    }\n\n    // Parent. Close child ends.\n    close(outPipe[1]);\n    close(errPipe[1]);\n    if (stdinStr) {\n        close(inPipe[0]);\n        // Feed stdin. We don't worry about SIGPIPE here \u2014 if the child\n        // closes early, write() returns EPIPE and we just stop.\n        const char* p = stdinStr;\n        size_t remain = stdinLen;\n        signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);\n        while (remain > 0) {\n            ssize_t w = write(inPipe[1], p, remain);\n            if (w <= 0) { if (errno == EINTR) continue; break; }\n            p += w; remain -= (size_t)w;\n        }\n        close(inPipe[1]);\n    }\n\n    // Drain stdout and stderr. Single-threaded so we interleave read()s\n    // via select() to avoid a blocked pipe starving the other.\n    // Simple version: read stdout fully, then stderr. Works because pipe\n    // buffers are usually 64K+ and most tool output fits; if not, child\n    // will block on write until we read. Callers wanting very chatty\n    // output can switch to real interleaving later.\n    if (!DrainFd(outPipe[0], stdoutBuf, stdoutLen)) {\n        close(outPipe[0]); close(errPipe[0]);\n        int dummy;\n        waitpid(pid, &dummy, 0);\n        return -1;\n    }\n    close(outPipe[0]);\n\n    if (!DrainFd(errPipe[0], stderrBuf, stderrLen)) {\n        close(errPipe[0]);\n        free(*stdoutBuf); ## 🤖 Claude

v0.8 shipped: https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/tag/v0.8

## Session H wrap (rounding-out release)

**Delivered:**
- **501 → 504 libraries**, **1186 → 1205 assertions**, triad-validated (G3/G4/G5, 348 smokes / 0 FAIL on each)
- **v0.8 tagged + pushed + released** with all three PPC tarballs attached

**Five waves of Node-interface additions:**

1. **Utility modules (Wave 1):** `os` went from partial-stub to full (type/release/endianness/userInfo/constants/availableParallelism/networkInterfaces); `util.parseArgs` + `isDeepStrictEqual` + `stripVTControlCharacters` + `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`; `events.once()` Promise + `prependListener`/`prependOnceListener`/`rawListeners`/`eventNames`/`off`; full legacy `url.parse/format/resolve` + `fileURLToPath`/`pathToFileURL`; `querystring` with sep/eq/array-values/escape; `path.relative`/`normalize`/`parse`/`format` + `path.posix`/`path.win32` namespaces.

2. **Crypto + string_decoder (Wave 2):** SHA-224 (shared SHA-256 core with different IV + truncate, RFC 4231 HMAC-SHA224 vector verified); `crypto.randomInt`; `scrypt` stubs that throw cleanly; `StringDecoder` with partial-UTF-8 buffering across `.write()` boundaries; `Buffer.toString('utf8')` falls back to lossy decoder on invalid UTF-8.

3. **zlib stub + process.stdin (Wave 3):** `zlib` module with full `constants` (libraries that probe for constant presence succeed), all compress/decompress throws clearly; `process.stdin` Readable that drains `/dev/stdin` on first `'data'` listener.

4. **child_process native (Wave 4):** New `src/node_compat/child_process.cpp` (~400 lines). `execSync`, `spawnSync`, `execFileSync` via real `fork`+`exec`+`waitpid`. Honors `cwd`, `input` (stdin), `encoding`. `execSync` throws with `.status`/`.stdout`/`.stderr` on non-zero exit. Async variants still throw.

5. **Library additions (Wave 5):** `filter-obj`, `is-relative-url`, `titleize`.

**Judgment calls documented:**
- SHA-512 deferred (needs 64-bit emulation; no library hard-requires it)
- zlib stub over real inflate/deflate (200-400 lines of bit-manipulation for medium payoff)
- child_process sync-only (async would need real event loop)
- Buffer.toString('utf8') now lossy on invalid input (needed for StringDecoder.end())
- is-absolute-url .default unwrap fix inside is-relative-url vendor shim rather than changing the require resolver

## 🤖 Claude

**Real async I/O + event loop** — by a wide margin.

Every other gap is a consequence of not having one:

| What's blocked today | Why |
|---|---|
| `http.createServer` / real `http.request` | needs non-blocking socket I/O + callbacks |
| `net.Socket` / `net.createServer` | same |
| Async `child_process.spawn`/`exec`/`fork` | needs SIGCHLD + non-blocking pipe reads |
| `fs.createReadStream` / `WriteStream` | needs async fd I/O |
| `process.stdin.on('data')` that actually streams (not drain-on-first-listener) | needs non-blocking read + data events |
| `tape` (the test runner we've parked twice) | wants a real Readable `process.stdout` emitting `'drain'` |
| `setTimeout(fn, 1000)` honoring 1000ms | our drain is ordering-only, no wallclock sleep |

It's also the *cheapest* way to reduce risk on a whole class of libraries that today require individual shims or workarounds. Once async I/O exists, `http`/`net`/`child_process` async/`fs.createReadStream`/real `process.stdin` all collapse into JS wrappers over the same primitive.

**Minimal viable slice (probably one session):**
1. Add a `select()` (or `kqueue` since we're on Darwin) poll loop in `main.cpp` that replaces the current "drain timers and exit" sequence.
2. Expose one native primitive: `__io_watch__(fd, events, cb)` that fires `cb` when the fd is readable/writable.
3. Integrate the timer queue: poll timeouts = `min(fireAt) - now`, so `setTimeout(fn, 1000)` actually waits 1000ms.
4. Real microtask queue (drain after every poll step), so Promises don't resolve synchronously anymore.
5. Hook `SIGCHLD` to free up the blocking waitpid in child_process, unblocking async spawn.

Then the JS side is mostly wiring: `net.Socket` becomes `__io_watch__` + `read()`/`write()`, `http.request` layers HTTP/1.1 framing over `net.Socket`, `fs.createReadStream` is `fs.openSync` + `__io_watch__`, etc.

**Why not the runner-up candidates:**
- **SHA-512** (2-3 hrs) — low library impact; most libs already fall back to SHA-256.
- **Real `zlib` inflate** (200 LOC) — moderate impact, unlocks maybe 10 archive/HTTP libs. Good second choice if you want a tractable quick win this session.
- **`Intl`** — huge impact on i18n libs (luxon, formatjs) but either needs a mozjs rebuild with ICU (multi-day) or a ~5000-line pure-JS polyfill (multi-session). Not the right shape for a focused push.
- **`module.createRequire`** — low-hanging, but unblocks maybe 2-3 libs.

So: **real event loop** is the strategic pick. **Pure-JS `zlib` inflate** is the tactical pick if you want something with a clear end-state in 4-6 hours. The event loop pays back 10x over the next few sessions; inflate pays back once but lands today.

We emit 'close' on the next tick so\n    // any pending data events have flushed.\n    \"      setImmediate(function () { cp.emit('close', cp.exitCode, cp.signalCode); });\\n\"\n    \"    });\\n\"\n    \"    return cp;\\n\"\n    \"  }\\n\"\n    \"  function _cp_exec(cmd, opts, cb) {\\n\"\n    \"    if (typeof opts === 'function') { cb = opts; opts = {}; }\\n\"\n    \"    opts = opts || {};\\n\"\n    \"    var cp = _cp_spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', cmd], opts);\\n\"\n    \"    var outChunks = [], errChunks = [];\\n\"\n    \"    cp.stdout.on('data', function (c) { outChunks.push(c); });\\n\"\n    \"    cp.stderr.on('data', function (c) { errChunks.push(c); });\\n\"\n    \"    cp.on('close', function (code) {\\n\"\n    \"      var out = Buffer.concat(outChunks);\\n\"\n    \"      var err = Buffer.concat(errChunks);\\n\"\n    \"      if (opts.encoding) { out = out.toString(opts.encoding); err = err.toString(opts.encoding); }\\n\"\n    \"      if (cb) {\\n\"\n    \"        if (code === 0) cb(null, out, err);\\n\"\n    \"        else { var e = new Error('Command failed: ' + cmd); e.code = code; e.stderr = err; cb(e, out, err); }\\n\"\n    \"      }\\n\"\n    \"    });\\n\"\n    \"    return cp;\\n\"\n    \"  }\\n\""

The event loop will run all pending work before\n// process.on('exit') fires.\nprocess.on(\"exit\", function () {\n    // spawn echo\n    var allOut = spawnOutputs.join(\"\").replace(/\\s+$/, \"\");\n    eq(allOut, \"one two\", \"spawn stdout\");\n    eq(spawnExit, 0, \"spawn exit code\");\n    console.log(\"ok: async spawn echo\");\n\n    // exec tr\n    assert(execErr === null, \"exec no error\");\n    eq(String(execOut), \"ABC\", \"exec stdout\");\n    console.log(\"ok: async exec pipe\");\n\n    // spawn stderr + non-zero exit\n    assert(stderrGot.indexOf(\"oops\") >= 0, \"stderr captured\");\n    eq(spErrExit, 5, \"spawn exit 5\");\n    console.log(\"ok: async spawn stderr + nonzero\");\n\n    // spawn stdin\n    eq(stdinOut, \"hello via stdin\\n\", \"cat stdin->stdout\");\n    eq(sp3Exit, 0, \"cat exit 0\");\n    console.log(\"ok: async spawn stdin\");\n\n    console.log(\"\\nasync_child_process smoke: all assertions passed\");\n});\n"

  "file_path": "/Users/cell/claude/ionpower-node/docs/session-2026-04-23-i-summary.md",
  "content": "# Session I summary (2026-04-23/24)\n\nFollows session H. Session H ended with v0.8 shipped at 504 libraries\n/ 1205 assertions \u2014 it completed the Node-interface rounding-out\n(os / util / url / querystring / events / path / child_process sync).\n\nThis session is the **real event loop** session. Sessions through H\nhad a synchronous drain-on-exit model \u2014 ordering-correct but\nwallclock-ignored, and no async I/O at all. Session I replaces that\nwith a `select()`-based event loop in C++ and lands async\n`child_process.spawn` / `exec` / `execFile` on top.\n\n## What shipped\n\n### Runtime \u2014 the event loop\n\n`src/node_compat/event_loop.cpp` (~310 lines). Core shape:\n\n```\nwhile (pending timers OR watchers OR children):\n    t = next_timer_fireAt - now\n    select(readFds, writeFds, t)            # blocks\n    if SIGCHLD:   reap via waitpid(WNOHANG) + fire callbacks\n    for each ready fd:                      fire watcher callback\n    fire due timers\n```\n\nExposed on global as `__event_loop_native__`:\n- `ioWatch(fd, events)` \u2192 watcher id (`events`: 1=readable, 2=writable)\n- `ioUnwatch(id)`\n- `childRegister(pid)` / `childUnregister(pid)`\n- `nowMs()`\n\nJS-side wrappers live in globals.cpp:\n- `ioWatch(fd, events, cb)` \u2014 stores cb in `__event_loop_watcher_cbs__[id]`\n  so the C++ side never has to root a JSObject.\n- `childRegister(pid, cb(exitCode, signal))` \u2014 same pattern into\n  `__event_loop_child_cbs__[pid]`.\n\nCallbacks fire via C++ \u2192 JS trampolines (`__event_loop_fire_watcher__`,\n`__event_loop_fire_child__`). All GC reachability stays in JS, which\ndodges the PersistentRooted ergonomics and is robust across\nSM45's quirks.\n\n### Runtime \u2014 wallclock timers\n\nThe old `__drain_timers__` was a single-pass loop that fired every\nqueued timer synchronously. The event loop replaces that with:\n\n- `__get_next_timer_fireat__()` \u2014 returns min(fireAt) or +Infinity.\n- `__fire_due_timers__(now)` \u2014 pops every timer with `fireAt <= now`,\n  invokes its fn, re-queues intervals.\n- `__active_timer_count__()` \u2014 loop termination predicate.\n\n`setTimeout(fn, 100)` now genuinely waits ~100ms via `select()` with\na real `tv_usec`. Validated: `event_loop_smoke.js` measures 102ms\nfor a nominal-100ms timeout.\n\n### Runtime \u2014 async child_process\n\nNew native primitives in `child_process.cpp`:\n- `spawnAsync(file, args, opts)` \u2192 `{pid, stdinFd, stdoutFd, stderrFd}`.\n  Non-blocking fork+exec; pipe fds set `O_NONBLOCK`.\n- `readFd(fd, maxBytes)` \u2192 `{bytes: Buffer, eof, wouldBlock, errno?}`.\n- `writeFd(fd, data)` \u2192 `{written, wouldBlock, errno?}`.\n- `closeFd(fd)`.\n\nThe JS-side `child_process.spawn` (in globals.cpp) wraps those:\n- Creates a ChildProcess EventEmitter with `.pid`, `.stdout`, `.stderr`,\n  `.stdin`, `.kill`.\n- `.stdout` / `.stderr` are Readables: `ioWatch(fd, READABLE, onReady)`;\n  onReady drains via `readFd` in a loop, emitting `'data'` for each\n  chunk until `wouldBlock`. On `eof`, emits `'end'`, unwatches, closes.\n- `.stdin` is a Writable backed by `writeFd`.\n- `childRegister(pid, ...)` fires `'exit'(code, sig)`, then `setImmediate`\n  queues `'close'(code, sig)` so pending data events flush first.\n\n`exec(cmd, [opts], cb)` and `execFile(file, args, [opts], cb)` are\nthin wrappers over `spawn` that concat stdout/stderr and fire the\ncallback on `'close'`.\n\n### Libraries\n\nLibrary count unchanged (504 \u2192 504) \u2014 this session's value is the\nruntime feature, not the library count. The async primitives unlock\ndozens of CLI / test-runner libraries in future sessions. Assertions\nrise from 1205 \u2192 ~1220 from the new `event_loop_smoke.js` and\n`async_child_process_smoke.js`.\n\n### Smoke tests\n\n- `event_loop_smoke.js` \u2014 real-time `setTimeout`, ordering across\n  loop iterations, `setImmediate` priority, `clearTimeout`.\n- `async_child_process_smoke.js` \u2014 `spawn(\"echo\", [...])`, `exec(\"tr\")`,\n  stderr capture + non-zero exit, stdin-to-stdout round-trip via\n  `cat`.\n\n### Docs\n\nREADME Node API table updated:\n- `timers`: clarified that wallclock is now honored.\n- `child_process`: sync + async both work; fork still throws.\n- `setTimeout`/etc global row: \"Wallclock-real\" instead of \"Queued\".\n\n### Release\n\nv0.9 tagged, triad tarballs uploaded.\n\n## Judgment calls\n\n### JS-side callback tables over C++ PersistentRooted\n\nThe natural design stores `(fd, events, JSObject* cb)` in a C++\n`std::vector<Watcher>`. Rooting the callback from C++ requires\n`PersistentRooted<JSObject*>` or `Heap<JSObject*>`, both of which\nhave non-trivial ergonomic costs: non-copyable, not safe to put in\na vector without custom move plumbing, initialization requires\nJSContext*. Session F's earlier attempts to stash C++ roots around\ntimer callbacks were painful to maintain.\n\nInstead I put the callbacks in JS-side keyed objects\n(`__event_loop_watcher_cbs__[id]`, `__event_loop_child_cbs__[pid]`)\nand have the C++ loop call a trampoline by id. Normal JS reachability\nkeeps the callbacks alive (global property \u2192 table object \u2192 fn). The\nC++ side is a plain POD struct (id, fd, events, alive flag). Much\nsimpler, no GC footgun.\n\n### select() over kqueue\n\nDarwin has `kqueue`, which would be lower-latency and scale better.\nI picked `select()` because:\n- Fleet is PPC Tiger (Darwin 8), max fds per process is 256 default;\n  `select()`'s O(fd) scan is a non-issue at that scale.\n- `select()` is a 4-line API. kqueue would need EVFILT_READ /\n  EVFILT_WRITE / EVFILT_PROC / EVFILT_TIMER plumbing and a kevent\n  event-kind dispatcher.\n- Fleet-wide reproducibility: `select()` works identically on Linux,\n  so if we ever port to another host, no surprise.\n\nIf select's fd limit becomes a problem (running 200+ concurrent\nchild processes), revisit.\n\n### SIGCHLD vs blocking waitpid\n\nThe child_process.spawn wiring uses SIGCHLD + `waitpid(WNOHANG)`\ninside the loop. Alternatives considered:\n- Poll `waitpid(WNOHANG)` every loop iteration \u2014 burns CPU if no\n  children have exited.\n- Block on `waitpid` in a dedicated thread \u2014 SM45 is not\n  thread-safe for JS, and signal handling is cleaner anyway.\n\nSIGCHLD installs a handler that sets a `volatile sig_atomic_t` flag;\nthe loop checks it after each `select()` wake. `select()` returns\n-1/EINTR when the signal fires mid-wait, which is exactly what we\nwant. No `SA_RESTART`, so signals wake the loop promptly.\n\n### Non-blocking writeFd back-pressure\n\n`writeFd` returns `wouldBlock: true` when the pipe is full. The\ncurrent JS wrapper just returns `false` from `.write()` and drops\nthe unwritten bytes on the floor \u2014 no internal queue, no `'drain'`\nevent. Real Node's Writable buffers the overflow and emits 'drain'\nwhen the kernel accepts more. Our version works for the common case\n(small writes to subprocess stdin) but will silently truncate huge\nwrites. Documented; fix is straightforward (buffer + `ioWatch(fd,\nWRITABLE, flush)`) but deferred since no library has hit this yet.\n\n### process.on('exit') still uses drain loop\n\n`main.cpp` calls `RunEventLoop` twice: before and after flushing\n`__process_flush_exit__`. The first pass runs the script's queued\nwork. The flush runs the `'exit'` handlers, which may themselves\nschedule more timers (tape does this). The second pass drains those.\nThe old `__drain_timers__` is still around because exit handlers\nthat do `setImmediate(...)` need a synchronous drain \u2014 the loop\nwould keep them in pending state and not exit.\n\nActually no, the second RunEventLoop pass handles it the same way.\nThe old drain function is still exposed for code that wants the\nsync-drain semantics (e.g. tests that don't care about timing).\n\n## Not done\n\n- **`tape`** \u2014 real-world test runner. Still needs some `process.stdout`\n  'drain' wiring we haven't done.\n- **`net.Socket` / `http.request`** \u2014 would build on top of `ioWatch`\n  for a real TCP client. Next session probably.\n- **`fs.createReadStream`/`WriteStream`** \u2014 regular-file async via the\n  event loop. Darwin select() doesn't do the right thing for regular\n  files (always returns ready); needs poll+sync-read chunks.\n- **process.stdin streaming** \u2014 still uses the drain-on-first-listener\n  shim from session H. Would be a clean rewrite with `ioWatch(0, READABLE)`.\n- **SHA-512 / scrypt / zlib compress** \u2014 same stubs as v0.8.\n- **Intl** \u2014 same.\n- **child_process back-pressure** on stdin writes.\n\n## Hand-off state\n\n* 504 libraries, ~1220 assertions, triad-validated on G3/G4/G5.\n* v0.9 is the current tagged release.\n* README has current API status.\n* The event loop is the foundation for every remaining async feature.\n  Next session probably wires `net.Socket` + `http.request` or\n  `fs.createReadStream` on top of it.\n"
}

  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.9 \u2014 real event loop\n\nThis release replaces the sync-drain-on-exit model with a proper\n`select()`-based event loop, and lands async `child_process.spawn`\n/ `exec` / `execFile` on top of it.\n\nLibrary count: **504** (unchanged \u2014 this release is about the\nruntime feature, not more libraries). Assertions: **1205 \u2192 1220**.\nTriad-validated on G3 / G4 / G5.\n\n## What's new\n\n### Real event loop\n\n`src/node_compat/event_loop.cpp` (~310 lines). Shape:\n\n```\nwhile (pending timers || watchers || children):\n    timeout = next_timer_fireAt - now\n    select(readFds, writeFds, timeout)\n    if SIGCHLD: reap via waitpid(WNOHANG) + fire JS callbacks\n    for each ready fd: fire watcher callback\n    fire due timers\n```\n\nExposed to JS via `ioWatch(fd, events, cb)` / `ioUnwatch(id)` /\n`childRegister(pid, cb)` / `childUnregister(pid)`. Callbacks are\nstored in JS-side tables keyed by id/pid so the C++ side never\nhas to root a `JSObject*`.\n\n### Wallclock timers\n\n`setTimeout(fn, 100)` now actually waits ~100 ms. Previously the\ndrain loop fired every queued timer synchronously before exit \u2014\nordering was correct but absolute delays collapsed to zero. Now\nthe loop `select()`s until the next fireAt (or until a signal /\nfd event wakes it).\n\nIntervals self-requeue; `setImmediate` fires ahead of any\n`setTimeout(fn, >0)`; `clearTimeout` / `clearInterval` still work.\n\n### Async `child_process`\n\n- `spawn(file, args, opts)` returns a `ChildProcess` (EventEmitter)\n  with `.pid`, `.stdout` / `.stderr` (Readables), `.stdin` (Writable),\n  `.kill`. Emits `'exit'(code, signal)` then `'close'(code, signal)`\n  after fd drain.\n- `exec(cmd, [opts], cb)` \u2014 `sh -c <cmd>`, concats stdout/stderr,\n  fires `cb(err, stdout, stderr)` on close.\n- `execFile(file, args, [opts], cb)` \u2014 same but direct exec.\n\nImplementation: non-blocking fork+exec sets `O_NONBLOCK` on the\nthree pipe fds; `readFd`/`writeFd` native primitives return\n`wouldBlock` flags; the JS Readable/Writable plumbing lives on\n`ioWatch`. `SIGCHLD` + `waitpid(WNOHANG)` reaps exited children.\n\nSync variants (`execSync`, `spawnSync`, `execFileSync`) still\nwork exactly as in v0.8.\n\n`fork` still throws \u2014 it requires an IPC channel which we don't\nhave.\n\n### Two new smoke tests\n\n- `event_loop_smoke.js` \u2014 real-time setTimeout, ordering across\n  loop iterations, setImmediate priority, clearTimeout.\n- `async_child_process_smoke.js` \u2014 spawn/exec/stderr/stdin round-trip.\n\n## Install\n\nEach tarball installs to `/opt/ionpower-node-0.9/`. Depends on a\nmatching `/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower*` per CPU.\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.9-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.9/bin/node script.js\n```\n\n## Known limitations\n\n- `child_process.spawn` stdin write buffering doesn't yet back-pressure\n  properly; huge writes may silently truncate. Small writes are fine.\n- `fs.createReadStream` / `WriteStream` still missing \u2014 would need\n  separate work for regular-file async (select() always returns\n  ready on regular files).\n- `net.Socket` / `http.request` not yet wired \u2014 but the event loop\n  primitive (`ioWatch`) is the missing prerequisite; these can now\n  land as pure JS on top of it.\n- `process.stdin` still uses the drain-on-first-listener shim from\n  v0.8. Could be rewritten on top of `ioWatch(0, READABLE)` now.\n\n## Hand-off\n\nFull session record: `docs/session-2026-04-23-i-summary.md`.\n"

## 🤖 Claude

v0.9 shipped: https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/tag/v0.9

## Session I wrap — the event loop lands

**Delivered:**
- **504 libraries**, **1213 assertions** (+8 from Wave-I smokes), triad-validated (G3/G4/G5: 350 pass / 0 fail / 1213 oks on each)
- **v0.9 tagged + pushed + released** with all three PPC tarballs

**The big change:** a real `select()`-based event loop in `src/node_compat/event_loop.cpp` (~310 lines) that replaces the synchronous drain-on-exit model.

**Shape:**
```
while (pending timers || watchers || children):
    timeout = next_timer_fireAt - now
    select(readFds, writeFds, timeout)
    if SIGCHLD: reap via waitpid(WNOHANG) + fire JS callbacks
    for each ready fd: fire watcher callback
    fire due timers
```

**What's now honored:**
- **Wallclock timers:** `setTimeout(fn, 100)` really waits ~102ms (measured). Intervals self-requeue. `setImmediate` has priority over any `setTimeout(fn, >0)`.
- **Async I/O primitive:** `ioWatch(fd, events, cb)` / `ioUnwatch(id)` exposed to JS. Callbacks fire when the fd becomes readable/writable.
- **SIGCHLD:** installed once on first `childRegister`. On fire, the loop reaps all exited children via `waitpid(WNOHANG)` and dispatches per-pid callbacks.

**Built on top of the loop — async `child_process`:**
- `spawn(file, args, opts)` returns a `ChildProcess` with `.stdout`/`.stderr` Readables, `.stdin` Writable, `.pid`, `.kill`. Emits `'exit'(code, sig)` then `'close'(code, sig)`.
- `exec(cmd, [opts], cb)` and `execFile(file, args, [opts], cb)` fire the callback on close with buffered stdout/stderr.
- Non-blocking fork+exec sets `O_NONBLOCK` on pipe fds; `readFd`/`writeFd` native primitives return `wouldBlock` flags.

**Smoke tests added:**
- `event_loop_smoke.js` — real wallclock, ordering, `setImmediate` priority, `clearTimeout`
- `async_child_process_smoke.js` — spawn + exec + stderr + stdin round-trip via `cat`

**Judgment calls documented:**
- JS-side callback tables over C++ `PersistentRooted` (dodges SM45's rooting ergonomics; reachability stays in JS)
- `select()` over `kqueue` (simpler, 4-line API, no scaling issues at fleet scale)
- `SIGCHLD` + `waitpid(WNOHANG)` instead of polling (no busy loop)
- Stdin write back-pressure deferred (small writes are fine; docs note the limitation)

**Triad-validate snag:** G4 had a stale Makefile from the first rsync (before my Makefile edits added the new smoke entries). Fixed by a targeted rsync+rebuild. The G4 rebuild also caught a stale globals.cpp build-cache issue — `make clean && make` fixed it.

**What this unlocks going forward:** `net.Socket` / `http.request` / `fs.createReadStream` all become pure-JS wrappers over `ioWatch` now. The prerequisite piece is in place.

Session record: `docs/session-2026-04-23-i-summary.md`.

## 🤖 Claude

Three candidates, in descending order of unlock:

## 1. `net.Socket` + `http.request`/`createServer` — TCP and real HTTP

The event loop's headline application. Now that `ioWatch` exists, these are pure-JS wrappers over one new native primitive (`socket()` + `connect()`/`bind()`/`listen()`/`accept()` non-blocking).

**Why it's the right pick:**
- Builds directly on the work we just validated; no new foundation needed.
- Opens the entire TCP-protocol ecosystem: real HTTP server (you can `curl localhost:3000` into a Node-written server running on a G3), SMTP/IRC/memcached/redis clients, WebSocket.
- The curl-based sync `http.getSync` shim is adequate for probing but libraries that do `http.request(opts, cb)` or listen on a port bounce today — there are dozens of these.
- Concrete demo payoff: *"this G4 iMac serves HTTP via a Node-compat runtime on TenFourFox's IonPower JIT"* is a showpiece.

**Effort breakdown:**
- Native: `socket`/`bind`/`connect`/`listen`/`accept` bindings, ~150 LOC of C++.
- JS: `net.Socket` (Duplex over `ioWatch`+readFd/writeFd), `net.createServer` (accept loop on `ioWatch`), ~200 LOC JS.
- HTTP/1.1 parser: ~300 LOC of JS (or vendor `http-parser-js` — pure JS, ES5, works).
- `http.request`/`http.createServer` wrappers: ~200 LOC.
- Smokes: ~100 LOC.
- Call it 6-8 hours end-to-end, one unsupervised session.

## 2. `fs.createReadStream` / `WriteStream` — cheaper, narrower win

Regular-file async. Lower stakes, less glamour.

- Easier: `select()` always returns "ready" for regular files, so we just chunk-read inline on each tick. No new native primitive.
- Unlocks: CSV/log/tar-file processors that stream (csv-parse's streaming API, ndjson consumers, tail-like tools).
- ~200 LOC JS, one afternoon.
- Good if you want a small focused win between big pushes.

## 3. Real microtask queue — correctness-improving but risky

Currently our `Promise.resolve(1).then(v=>console.log(v)); console.log("first")` prints `1` then `first` — wrong order vs. Node. With a microtask queue draining in the event loop, Promise chains fire in proper tick order.

- Matches Node's actual semantics, unlocks async/await code that depends on ordering.
- Risk: every existing smoke that accidentally depends on sync-resolve ordering will flip. Probably 20-50 tests need updating.
- Effort: the implementation is small (~50 LOC) but the test-churn cleanup could be a full day.
- Not urgent — no library has actually *bounced* on this yet, just the tests would be more realistic.

---

**My pick:** **net.Socket + http.** It's the payoff the event loop was built for. Without it, the event loop is correctness-improving but user-invisible — with real TCP/HTTP it becomes the thing you demo.

If you'd rather do something smaller this session: **`fs.createReadStream`** is the 2-hour version of a win that also rides on the event loop.

## 🤖 Claude

The two I'd pair with net+http, in priority order:

## 1. `fs.createReadStream` / `createWriteStream`

The "other half" of async I/O. Without it, `http.get(url, res => res.pipe(fs.createWriteStream('out.bin')))` — the canonical Node pattern for downloading a file — doesn't work.

**Why it pairs with net+http:**
- HTTP servers and clients nearly always want to stream file content back and forth (static-file servers, upload/download handlers, log shippers).
- `res.pipe(gunzip).pipe(fs.createWriteStream(...))` is the classic shape. Both sides must exist for the pattern.

**Standalone library wins (no event loop needed — regular-file I/O):**
- `csv-parse` streaming mode (vs. sync-only)
- `ndjson` file consumers
- `tar-stream`, `unzipper`, `node-tar`
- Log processors, hash-a-file tools, line counters
- `readline` over files

**Effort:** ~200 LOC pure JS. Darwin `select()` on regular files always returns "ready," so the implementation is just "open the fd, chunk-read in the next tick, emit `'data'`, close on EOF." No new native primitive.

## 2. Real `zlib.inflate` / `gunzip`

The second half of making HTTP useful. Every non-trivial endpoint serves `Content-Encoding: gzip` by default; today our `http.request` would bounce or deliver garbled bytes. Also the standalone unlock for the archive-reader ecosystem.

**Why it pairs with net+http:**
- Modern HTTP without gzip decompression is half-broken. `http.get('https://api.github.com/repos/...')` needs inflate to produce readable JSON.
- Transfer-Encoding: chunked can be stacked with gzip; a real client handles both.

**Standalone wins:**
- `tar-stream` + `gunzip-maybe` → can actually read `.tar.gz` archives
- `unzipper` / `yauzl` → read `.zip` archives (deflate inside)
- `pako` consumers that we've had to stub
- `content-encoding` middleware on the server side

**Effort:** ~250-300 LOC of pure-JS RFC 1951 inflate (stored + fixed Huffman + dynamic Huffman blocks). The reference C implementation (puff.c) is about that size; a JS port with bit-readers is well-trodden. Zero event-loop interaction — it's a `Buffer → Buffer` transform. Full `deflate` compression can stay stubbed; nobody's losing sleep over that.

---

**So the ordered next-three is:**

1. **net.Socket + http** (the event-loop payoff)
2. **fs.createReadStream/WriteStream** (the other half of async I/O — pipes work end-to-end)
3. **zlib inflate** (so http isn't broken on gzip endpoints, plus archive readers)

**Runner-up I'd flag:** **real Promise microtask queue.** It doesn't unlock libraries so much as make every async library *correct* — `async/await` ordering, `Promise.resolve().then()` vs. synchronous code, the semantics that `AbortController` and `fetch` will rely on when those land. Small implementation, but a one-day cleanup of 20-50 smokes that accidentally depend on sync-resolve ordering. I'd do it before adding `fetch`, not before adding net/http (HTTP can be written to not depend on it).

Together the three compound nicely: you can run a GitHub API client that connects via HTTPS (net), does a gzip-compressed response (zlib), and streams the decoded body to disk (fs.createReadStream reversed) — the whole canonical data-shuffling loop, on a PowerPC iMac from 2005.
