  "content": "# Session U summary (2026-04-24)\n\nFollows session T (v0.22 JWK + AES-KW).\n\nTwo releases shipped:\n\n- **v0.22** \u2014 JWK (JSON Web Key) format + AES-KW (RFC 3394) key wrapping\n  in `crypto.subtle`. Already documented in session T's closing notes;\n  tagged and triad-validated in this session.\n\n- **v0.23** \u2014 library hunt wave 4: four more vendored libraries\n  brought under smoke coverage:\n\n  - `tweetnacl` \u2014 surface check (loads, exposes `hash`/`sign`,\n    `randomBytes` returns the right length when present).\n  - `fast-json-stable-stringify` \u2014 deterministic key-sorted JSON,\n    nested case verified.\n  - `stable-sort` \u2014 stable merge sort on a shuffled duplicate-laden\n    numeric array.\n  - `emoji-regex` v10 \u2014 U+1F600 detection inside a mixed string.\n\n  Library count: 580 \u2192 585+. Assertions: 1368 \u2192 1372+ across 372\n  smoke files.\n\n## Judgment calls\n\n### tiger-rsync gremlin generalised on emac\n\nPreviously the gremlin was \"Makefile sometimes doesn't land\"; workaround\nwas an explicit `scp Makefile`. In this session, the full `--delete`\nflag failed against emac's older `rsync 2.6.3` (it doesn't grok\n`--delete-before`, which the host's rsync 3.x sends to the remote).\n\nWorkaround for v0.23: drop `--delete` for the G4 rsync. Since we\nweren't deleting files from our tree (only adding smoke + vendor\nfiles), the remote's leftover files are harmless. Pattern captured in\n`/tmp/triad-v0.23-g4.sh`.\n\n### Per-host Makefile arguments\n\nThe Makefile defaults to G5 (`MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower` +\n`CPU_FLAGS='-mcpu=G5 -D_PPC970_'`). For the G3/G4 triad builds we pass:\n\n- G3: `MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS='-mcpu=750 -mtune=750'`\n- G4: `MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g4 CPU_FLAGS='-mcpu=7450 -mtune=7450'`\n- G5: `MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g5 CPU_FLAGS='-mcpu=G5 -D_PPC970_'`\n\n(The bare `/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower` symlink on imacg3 points to a stale\n`/tmp/copy/...` location \u2014 probably an old bootstrap leftover. Ignored;\nwe always pass `-g3` explicitly.)\n\n### install without sudo\n\n`/opt/` is `drwxrwxr-x root:admin` on all three hosts. `macuser` is an\nadmin member, so `make install PREFIX=/opt/ionpower-node-0.23` works\nwithout sudo. Attempts to use `sudo` on these hosts always prompt for a\npassword \u2014 noted in case a future release needs a path outside\n`/opt`.\n\n## Hand-off state\n\n- v0.23 tagged + tarballs built for G3/G4/G5.\n- 585+ libraries under smoke coverage, 1370+ assertions across 372\n  smokes.\n- Crypto surface: comprehensive for symmetric + hashing + KDF + JWK +\n  AES-KW. Asymmetric (RSA/ECDSA/Ed25519) still absent.\n\n### Next candidates\n\n- **WebStreams** (ReadableStream / WritableStream / TransformStream) \u2014\n  WHATWG spec; pairs naturally with our existing Promise / microtask\n  queue.\n- **Asymmetric crypto** (RSA-PSS / ECDSA / Ed25519) \u2014 pure-JS bignum\n  and curve math; each is nontrivial.\n- **module.createRequire** \u2014 cheap win; useful for dual-mode packages.\n- **dgram** (UDP) \u2014 simpler than TLS; `socket()/sendto()/recvfrom()`.\n- **More library hunt** \u2014 always more small libraries to vendor.\n"

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.24-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.24 \u2014 WHATWG Streams\n\nAdds `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream`, and `TransformStream` as\nglobal constructors. Minimal WHATWG Streams shape \u2014 enough for the\ncommon consumer patterns.\n\n## What's new\n\n### ReadableStream\n\n```js\nconst rs = new ReadableStream({\n    start(controller) { controller.enqueue(\"a\"); controller.close(); },\n    pull(controller)  { \u2026 },\n    cancel(reason)    { \u2026 }\n});\n\nconst reader = rs.getReader();\nconst { value, done } = await reader.read();\n```\n\nSupports: `start`/`pull`/`cancel` sources, `controller.enqueue`/`close`/\n`error`, `getReader().read()/releaseLock()/cancel()`, `locked` flag,\n`cancel()`, `tee()`, `pipeTo()`, `pipeThrough()`.\n\n### WritableStream\n\n```js\nconst ws = new WritableStream({\n    start(controller) { \u2026 },\n    write(chunk, controller) { \u2026 },\n    close() { \u2026 },\n    abort(reason) { \u2026 }\n});\n\nconst w = ws.getWriter();\nawait w.write(\"x\");\nawait w.close();\n```\n\nWrites are serialized to the sink via a per-stream Promise chain \u2014\nthe sink sees chunks in order, next write only starts after the\nprevious settles. Supports `getWriter().write/close/abort/releaseLock`\nplus `stream.abort(reason)`.\n\n### TransformStream\n\n```js\nconst upper = new TransformStream({\n    transform(chunk, controller) { controller.enqueue(chunk.toUpperCase()); }\n});\n\nrs.pipeThrough(upper).pipeTo(ws);\n```\n\nBundles a writable + readable side with `start`/`transform`/`flush`\nhooks.\n\n## Backpressure caveat\n\nNo explicit high-water-mark queuing or `desiredSize` gauge. Readers /\nwriters serialize by waiting on the previous Promise. That's enough\nfor the common consumer patterns (read-all, pipe-through, pipe-to)\nbut under-spec for producer-heavy scenarios where backpressure is the\npoint.\n\n## Verified\n\nAll nine smokes pass on G3/G4/G5:\n- ReadableStream basic read\n- ReadableStream pull\n- ReadableStream error propagation\n- ReadableStream lock/unlock\n- WritableStream in-order write + close\n- TransformStream uppercase\n- pipeTo\n- pipeThrough\n- tee\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **585+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1381+** across **373** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.24-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.24/bin/node script.js\n```\n\nSeparate G3 / G4 / G5 tarballs \u2014 each depends on the matching\n`/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-{g3,g4,g5}/` install from tenfourfox-src.\n"
}

  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.25 \u2014 module core (createRequire + builtinModules)\n\nAdds the Node 12+ `module` core surface. Dual-mode (ESM + CJS)\npackages use this to get a `require()` bound to the current file.\n\n## What's new\n\n### `module.createRequire(filename | file:// URL)`\n\n```js\nconst { createRequire } = require(\"module\");\nconst localRequire = createRequire(__filename);\n// or from an ESM file's import.meta.url equivalent:\nconst r = createRequire(\"file:///absolute/path/to/file.js\");\n\nconst fs = localRequire(\"fs\");\nconst lib = localRequire(\"./vendor/crc32.js\");\nlocalRequire.resolve(\"./vendor/crc32.js\");\n```\n\nAccepts either an absolute path or a `file://`-prefixed URL string.\nThe returned `require` is rooted at the `dirname` of the passed\nfilename, so relative specifiers resolve correctly from the caller's\nlocation.\n\nBuilt on top of the existing `__make_require__(dir)` primitive \u2014 just\npeels the dirname off the filename and hands it over.\n\n### `module.builtinModules`\n\nAn array listing the core module names we seed in `__require_cache__`:\n`['fs', 'path', 'events', 'util', 'child_process', 'os', 'crypto',\n'buffer', 'string_decoder', 'assert', 'stream', 'timers',\n'querystring', 'readable-stream', 'inherits', 'supports-color',\n'has-ansi', 'module']`.\n\n## Verified\n\nAll 5 smokes pass on G3/G4/G5:\n- module core surface\n- createRequire loads a core module\n- createRequire loads a relative path\n- createRequire accepts file:// URL\n- require.resolve on the bound require\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **585+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1386+** across **374** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.25-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.25/bin/node script.js\n```\n"

  "content": "// perf_hooks + globalThis.performance smoke.\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\n// --- require('perf_hooks') surface ---\nvar ph = require(\"perf_hooks\");\nassert(typeof ph === \"object\", \"perf_hooks is an object\");\nassert(typeof ph.performance === \"object\", \"has performance\");\nassert(typeof ph.performance.now === \"function\", \"performance.now is a function\");\nassert(typeof ph.performance.timeOrigin === \"number\", \"performance.timeOrigin is a number\");\nassert(typeof ph.PerformanceObserver === \"function\", \"PerformanceObserver is a ctor\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: perf_hooks surface\");\n\n// --- performance.now() basics ---\nvar a = ph.performance.now();\nvar b = ph.performance.now();\nassert(typeof a === \"number\", \"now() returns a number\");\nassert(b >= a, \"now() is monotonic\");\nassert(a >= 0, \"now() is non-negative (from timeOrigin)\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: performance.now basics\");\n\n// --- global performance is the same ---\nassert(typeof performance === \"object\", \"global performance exists\");\nassert(typeof performance.now === \"function\", \"global performance.now\");\nassert(performance === ph.performance, \"global performance === perf_hooks.performance\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: globalThis.performance === perf_hooks.performance\");\n\n// --- mark / measure / clear are callable (stubs) ---\nph.performance.mark(\"start\");\nph.performance.mark(\"end\");\nph.performance.measure(\"span\", \"start\", \"end\");\nph.performance.clearMarks();\nph.performance.clearMeasures();\nassert(Array.isArray(ph.performance.getEntries()), \"getEntries returns array\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: mark/measure/getEntries (stubs)\");\n\n// --- PerformanceObserver is constructible + has observe/disconnect ---\nvar calls = 0;\nvar obs = new ph.PerformanceObserver(function () { calls++; });\nobs.observe({ entryTypes: [\"measure\"] });\nobs.disconnect();\nassert(Array.isArray(obs.takeRecords()), \"takeRecords returns array\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: PerformanceObserver shape\");\n\n// --- timeOrigin matches Date.now() ballpark ---\nvar clockDiff = Date.now() - ph.performance.timeOrigin;\nassert(clockDiff >= 0, \"timeOrigin <= Date.now()\");\nassert(clockDiff < 60 * 60 * 1000, \"timeOrigin within the last hour\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: timeOrigin reasonable\");\n\n// --- Use now() around a small loop, duration is non-negative ---\nvar t0 = performance.now();\nvar sum = 0;\nfor (var i = 0; i < 100000; i++) sum += i;\nvar t1 = performance.now();\nassert(t1 - t0 >= 0, \"duration non-negative\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: now() around a loop (took \" + (t1 - t0).toFixed(0) + \"ms, sum=\" + sum + \")\");\n\nconsole.log(\"\\nperf_hooks smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"

  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.26 \u2014 perf_hooks + global performance\n\nAdds the Node `perf_hooks` core module and the WHATWG-compatible\n`performance` global.\n\n## What's new\n\n### `globalThis.performance`\n\n```js\nconst t0 = performance.now();\n// ... work ...\nconst t1 = performance.now();\nconsole.log(\"took\", t1 - t0, \"ms\");\n```\n\n`performance.now()` returns monotonic ms since process start.\n`performance.timeOrigin` is `Date.now()` captured at that start.\n\n`mark` / `measure` / `clearMarks` / `clearMeasures` / `getEntries` /\n`getEntriesByName` / `getEntriesByType` are all callable with\nspec-shaped return types (entries are always empty arrays \u2014 we\ndon't retain timing data).\n\n### `require('perf_hooks')`\n\n```js\nconst { performance, PerformanceObserver, constants } = require(\"perf_hooks\");\n\nconst obs = new PerformanceObserver(entries => { /* \u2026 */ });\nobs.observe({ entryTypes: [\"measure\"] });\nobs.disconnect();\n```\n\n`PerformanceObserver` constructs; `observe` / `disconnect` /\n`takeRecords` are no-ops (no entry callbacks fire). `constants`\nexposes the Node GC reason enums.\n\n## Resolution\n\nMillisecond resolution \u2014 we synthesize from `Date.now()`. SM45\ndoesn't expose `clock_gettime` directly, so sub-millisecond precision\nisn't available. Sufficient for per-request timing and coarse\nbenchmarks.\n\n## Verified\n\n7 smoke assertions pass on G3 / G4 / G5:\n- perf_hooks surface\n- performance.now() basics (monotonic, non-negative)\n- `globalThis.performance === perf_hooks.performance`\n- mark / measure / clearMarks / clearMeasures / getEntries (stubs)\n- PerformanceObserver ctor + observe / disconnect / takeRecords\n- timeOrigin is a reasonable value (\u2264 Date.now(), within the hour)\n- performance.now() around a 100k-iter loop returns a non-negative delta\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **585+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1393+** across **375** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.26-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.26/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.28 \u2014 ES2022 / ES2023 small-API polyfills\n\nSpiderMonkey 45 predates most of the \"library authors assume this\nexists\" APIs from the last few years. This release adds trivial\npolyfills for the common missing surface, all gated by `typeof X ===\n'undefined'` so a future mozjs bump brings native impls through\ncleanly.\n\n## What's new\n\n### Object / Array / String additions\n\n- `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` \u2014 more reliable `hasOwnProperty`\n- `Array.prototype.at(i)` \u2014 negative indexing\n- `Array.prototype.findLast(fn)` / `findLastIndex(fn)` \u2014 reverse scan\n- `Array.prototype.toSorted(cmp)` \u2014 returns sorted copy\n- `Array.prototype.toReversed()` \u2014 returns reversed copy\n- `Array.prototype.toSpliced(start, deleteCount, ...items)` \u2014 returns spliced copy\n- `Array.prototype.with(i, v)` \u2014 returns copy with index replaced\n- `String.prototype.at(i)` \u2014 negative indexing\n- `String.prototype.replaceAll(search, replace)` \u2014 global replace (string or `/g` regex)\n\n### Error / Promise\n\n- `AggregateError` \u2014 Error subclass carrying `.errors` array\n- `Promise.any(iter)` \u2014 resolves with first fulfilled; else rejects with `AggregateError`\n\n### structuredClone\n\n```js\nconst copy = structuredClone({ a: 1, b: [2, 3], when: new Date() });\n```\n\nSupports: plain objects, arrays, `Date`, `RegExp`, `Map`, `Set`,\n`Buffer`. Other types (TypedArray, Blob, ArrayBuffer, class instances)\nfall through to plain-object copy. Does **not** detect cycles \u2014 don't\nclone self-referential graphs.\n\n## Verified\n\n13 assertions pass on G3 / G4 / G5 covering every new API plus a\nPromise.any one-winner + all-rejected round-trip.\n\n## Housekeeping\n\nRestored the older CJS `escape-string-regexp.js` (v0.27's Babel-\ntransformed ESM default export broke chalk's `var esr = require(...)`\ncall site).\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **592+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1438+** across **377** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.28-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.28/bin/node script.js\n```\n"

Server's 'message' handler echoes a reply;\n// client's 'message' handler ends the test.\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\nvar dgram = require(\"dgram\");\nassert(typeof dgram.createSocket === \"function\", \"dgram.createSocket exists\");\nassert(typeof dgram.Socket === \"function\", \"dgram.Socket exists\");\n\nvar server = dgram.createSocket(\"udp4\");\nvar client = dgram.createSocket(\"udp4\");\n\nvar clientGot = false;\nvar serverGot = false;\nvar done = false;\n\nfunction finish(err) {\n    if (done) return;\n    done = true;\n    try { client.close(); } catch (e) {}\n    try { server.close(); } catch (e) {}\n    if (err) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", err.message || err); process.exit(1); }\n    console.log(\"ok: dgram round-trip\");\n    console.log(\"\\ndgram smoke: all assertions passed\");\n}\n\nvar watchdog = setTimeout(function () {\n    finish(new Error(\"dgram smoke timed out after 5s\"));\n}, 5000);\n\nserver.on(\"error\", function (err) {\n    finish(new Error(\"server error: \" + err.message));\n});\n\nserver.on(\"message\", function (msg, rinfo) {\n    serverGot = true;\n    assert(Buffer.isBuffer(msg), \"server got Buffer\");\n    assert(msg.toString() === \"ping\", \"server got 'ping'\");\n    assert(typeof rinfo.address === \"string\", \"rinfo.address is string\");\n    assert(typeof rinfo.port === \"number\", \"rinfo.port is number\");\n    assert(rinfo.family === \"IPv4\", \"rinfo.family\");\n    // Reply back\n    server.send(\"pong\", rinfo.port, rinfo.address);\n});\n\nserver.on(\"listening\", function () {\n    var addr = server.address();\n    assert(addr.port > 0, \"server bound to ephemeral port\");\n\n    client.on(\"error\", function (err) {\n        finish(new Error(\"client error: \" + err.message));\n    });\n    client.on(\"message\", function (msg, rinfo) {\n        clientGot = true;\n        assert(msg.toString() === \"pong\", \"client got 'pong'\");\n        clearTimeout(watchdog);\n        finish();\n    });\n\n    client.send(\"ping\", addr.port, \"127.0.0.1\");\n});\n\nserver.bind(0, \"127.0.0.1\");\n"

  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.29 \u2014 dgram (UDP)\n\nAdds the Node `dgram` core module for UDP sockets.\n\n## What's new\n\n### Native primitives on `__net_native__`\n\n- `sendto(fd, bufOrString, host, port)` \u2192 bytes sent (or -1 on\n  EAGAIN).\n- `recvfrom(fd, maxLen=65536)` \u2192 `{ data: Uint8Array, address, port,\n  size }` or `null` on EAGAIN.\n\n### `dgram` module\n\n```js\nconst dgram = require('dgram');\n\nconst server = dgram.createSocket('udp4');\nserver.on('listening', () => console.log('bound', server.address()));\nserver.on('message', (msg, rinfo) => {\n    console.log('got', msg.toString(), 'from', rinfo.address, rinfo.port);\n    server.send('pong', rinfo.port, rinfo.address);\n});\nserver.bind(0, '127.0.0.1');\n\nconst client = dgram.createSocket('udp4');\nclient.on('message', (msg) => {\n    console.log('reply:', msg.toString());\n    client.close();\n});\nclient.send('ping', server.address().port, '127.0.0.1');\n```\n\nSupports:\n- `dgram.createSocket('udp4')` and `new dgram.Socket({ type })`\n- `bind(port, address, cb)` / `bind(opts, cb)` / `bind(cb)` \u2014\n  ephemeral port when omitted.\n- `send(buf, port, address, cb)` and the legacy 6-arg\n  `send(buf, offset, length, port, address, cb)` shape.\n- `address()` returns `{ address, family: 'IPv4', port }`.\n- `close(cb)`.\n- Events: `'listening'`, `'message'`, `'error'`, `'close'`.\n- Buffer + string payloads.\n- Auto-bind to ephemeral port on first `send()` if not yet bound.\n\n## Not yet\n\n- IPv6 (`'udp6'`)\n- Multicast (`addMembership` / `dropMembership`)\n- `setBroadcast` (stubbed)\n- `setTTL` / `setMulticastTTL`\n\n## Verified\n\nA loopback `'ping'`/`'pong'` round-trip smoke passes on G3 / G4 / G5.\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **592+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1446+** across **378** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.29-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.29/bin/node script.js\n```\n"

process.exit(1); } }\n\n// ---- generateKeyPairSync ----\nvar pair = crypto.generateKeyPairSync(\"ed25519\");\nassert(pair && pair.publicKey && pair.privateKey, \"generateKeyPairSync returns a pair\");\nassert(pair.publicKey.type === \"public\", \"public key type\");\nassert(pair.privateKey.type === \"private\", \"private key type\");\nassert(pair.publicKey.asymmetricKeyType === \"ed25519\", \"public asymmetricKeyType\");\nassert(pair.privateKey.asymmetricKeyType === \"ed25519\", \"private asymmetricKeyType\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: crypto.generateKeyPairSync('ed25519')\");\n\n// ---- sign + verify round-trip ----\nvar msg = Buffer.from(\"hello, ed25519!\", \"utf8\");\nvar sig = crypto.sign(null, msg, pair.privateKey);\nassert(Buffer.isBuffer(sig), \"sig is Buffer\");\nassert(sig.length === 64, \"sig length 64\");\n\nvar ok = crypto.verify(null, msg, pair.publicKey, sig);\nassert(ok === true, \"signature verifies\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: sign / verify round-trip\");\n\n// ---- tamper rejects ----\nvar bad = Buffer.from(sig);\nbad[0] ^= 1;\nassert(crypto.verify(null, msg, pair.publicKey, bad) === false,\n       \"tampered signature rejected\");\n\n// ---- different message rejects ----\nvar other = Buffer.from(\"bye, ed25519!\", \"utf8\");\nassert(crypto.verify(null, other, pair.publicKey, sig) === false,\n       \"wrong message rejected\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: tamper detection\");\n\n// ---- createPrivateKey / createPublicKey from raw bytes ----\nvar pkRaw = pair.publicKey.export();        // 32-byte Buffer\nvar skRaw = pair.privateKey.export();       // 64-byte Buffer\nassert(pkRaw.length === 32, \"exported public = 32 bytes\");\nassert(skRaw.length === 64, \"exported private = 64 bytes\");\n\nvar pk2 = crypto.createPublicKey(pkRaw);\nvar sk2 = crypto.createPrivateKey(skRaw);\nvar sig2 = crypto.sign(null, msg, sk2);\nassert(crypto.verify(null, msg, pk2, sig2), \"round-trip through createPrivateKey/createPublicKey\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: createPrivateKey / createPublicKey (raw bytes)\");\n\n// ---- 32-byte seed expansion ----\nvar seed = Buffer.alloc(32);\nfor (var i = 0; Input: {
  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.30-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.30 \u2014 Ed25519 sign/verify\n\n**First asymmetric crypto primitive.** Wires Node-style\n`crypto.sign` / `crypto.verify` / `crypto.generateKeyPair{,Sync}` /\n`crypto.createPrivateKey` / `crypto.createPublicKey` through the\ntweetnacl pure-JS library for Ed25519.\n\nRSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and X25519 still throw not-supported.\n\n## What's new\n\n```js\nconst crypto = require('crypto');\n\nconst { publicKey, privateKey } = crypto.generateKeyPairSync('ed25519');\n\nconst msg = Buffer.from(\"hello, ed25519!\", \"utf8\");\nconst sig = crypto.sign(null, msg, privateKey);   // 64 bytes\n\nif (crypto.verify(null, msg, publicKey, sig)) {\n    console.log(\"verified\");\n}\n```\n\n### Key object surface\n\n`generateKeyPairSync('ed25519')` returns two `KeyObject`s with:\n\n- `.type` \u2014 `'public'` or `'private'`.\n- `.asymmetricKeyType` \u2014 `'ed25519'`.\n- `.export()` \u2014 raw bytes (32 for public, 64 for private).\n- `.export({ format: 'jwk' })` \u2014 OKP JWK:\n  ```js\n  { kty: 'OKP', crv: 'Ed25519', x: '...', d: '...' }\n  ```\n\n### Import\n\n- `createPublicKey(raw32Bytes | OKP_JWK | privateKey)` \u2014 accept raw,\n  a JWK, or project from a `KeyObject` of `type: 'private'`.\n- `createPrivateKey(raw64Bytes | seed32Bytes | OKP_JWK)` \u2014 a 32-byte\n  seed is expanded via `nacl.sign.keyPair.fromSeed` into a full\n  64-byte secret key.\n\n## Mechanics\n\n- `tweetnacl.js` is lazy-loaded via `__make_require__(cwd)` on first\n  call. That path uses the vendor-fallback, so installed binaries\n  pick up `share/ionpower-node/vendor/tweetnacl.js` and dev trees hit\n  `test/vendor/tweetnacl.js`.\n- `tweetnacl.setPRNG(...)` is wired to `crypto.randomBytes` \u2014 key\n  generation is actually random, not the \"no PRNG set\" stub.\n- `make install` now copies `tweetnacl.js` into `share/ionpower-node/\n  vendor/` alongside `babel.js`.\n\n## Verified\n\nSeven smoke assertions on G3 / G4 / G5:\n- generateKeyPairSync\n- sign / verify round-trip\n- tamper detection (bit-flipped sig rejects; wrong message rejects)\n- createPrivateKey / createPublicKey (raw-byte round-trip)\n- 32-byte seed \u2192 private-key expansion (derived public signs correctly)\n- JWK export / import round-trip\n- generateKeyPair (async callback)\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **592+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1453+** across **379** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.30-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.30/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.31-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.31 \u2014 WebCrypto Ed25519 + X25519\n\nExtends SubtleCrypto with the two curve25519-based algorithms. Both\nshare v0.30's tweetnacl lazy-load plumbing.\n\n## What's new\n\n### Ed25519 via `crypto.subtle`\n\n```js\nconst { publicKey, privateKey } = await crypto.subtle.generateKey(\n    { name: 'Ed25519' }, true, ['sign', 'verify']);\n\nconst sig = await crypto.subtle.sign({ name: 'Ed25519' }, privateKey, data);\nconst ok  = await crypto.subtle.verify({ name: 'Ed25519' }, publicKey, sig, data);\n\nconst jwk = await crypto.subtle.exportKey('jwk', publicKey);\n// { kty: 'OKP', crv: 'Ed25519', x: '...', ext: true, key_ops: [...] }\n```\n\n- `sign` returns a 64-byte ArrayBuffer.\n- `importKey('jwk', ...)` accepts OKP JWKs with `x` (public) or `d`\n  (32-byte seed for private \u2014 auto-expanded to the full 64-byte\n  secretKey).\n- `exportKey('jwk', key)` emits OKP JWKs; for private keys, both `d`\n  (seed) and `x` (derived public) are included.\n\n### X25519 ECDH via `crypto.subtle`\n\n```js\nconst alice = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'X25519' }, true, ['deriveBits']);\nconst bob   = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'X25519' }, true, ['deriveBits']);\n\nconst secretA = await crypto.subtle.deriveBits(\n    { name: 'X25519', public: bob.publicKey }, alice.privateKey, 256);\nconst secretB = await crypto.subtle.deriveBits(\n    { name: 'X25519', public: alice.publicKey }, bob.privateKey, 256);\n// secretA === secretB (curve25519 ECDH)\n```\n\nBacked by `nacl.scalarMult(priv, peerPub)`. Length argument truncates\nthe 32-byte shared secret (256-bit gives the full raw secret).\n\n## Still missing\n\n- RSA / ECDSA / NIST ECDH (P-256, P-384, P-521) \u2014 require bignum /\n  curve arithmetic we haven't written.\n- PKCS#8 / SPKI key formats.\n- `deriveKey` (can be composed via `deriveBits` + `importKey`).\n\n## Verified\n\n3 smoke assertions on G3 / G4 / G5:\n- subtle Ed25519 generate + sign + verify.\n- subtle Ed25519 JWK export \u2192 import \u2192 verify round-trip.\n- subtle X25519 ECDH two-party shared-secret match.\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **592+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1460+** across **380** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.31-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.31/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

  "new_string": "    \"  __require_cache__['module']         = module_core;\\n\"\n    // tweetnacl: seed into the require cache at first access. A getter\n    // on __require_cache__ would be spec-cleaner, but JS_GetProperty()\n    // may bypass getters; the wrapped __make_require__ does a hasOwn\n    // check so we have to populate eagerly via a lazy wrapper. Rather\n    // than eager-loading the ~2400-line file here, we leave the cache\n    // unseeded and let crypto.* use _naclLoad() which does the PRNG\n    // wiring. Users who `require('tweetnacl')` directly get the raw\n    // library and must call setPRNG themselves \u2014 but our patch below\n    // installs PRNG as a side effect of ANY _naclLoad() call, so once\n    // any crypto.sign/verify/etc. touches nacl, later requires share\n    // the PRNG-wired instance through the cache.\\n\"\n    // Cache the wired instance after first _naclLoad() so direct\n    // require('tweetnacl') gets the wired copy.\\n\"\n    \"  (function () {\\n\"\n    \"    var origLoad = _naclLoad;\\n\"\n    \"    _naclLoad = function () {\\n\"\n    \"      var out = origLoad();\\n\"\n    \"      if (!__require_cache__['tweetnacl']) __require_cache__['tweetnacl'] = out;\\n\"\n    \"      return out;\\n\"\n    \"    };\\n\"\n    \"  })();\\n\""

  "content": "// tweetnacl box / secretbox authenticated encryption smoke.\n// Relies on our require hook that lazy-loads tweetnacl with the\n// PRNG wired to crypto.getRandomValues.\n\nvar nacl = require(\"tweetnacl\");\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\n// --- nacl.secretbox: symmetric authenticated encryption ---\n(function () {\n    var key   = nacl.randomBytes(32);\n    var nonce = nacl.randomBytes(24);\n    var msg   = new TextEncoder().encode(\"Hello nacl.secretbox\");\n\n    var ct = nacl.secretbox(msg, nonce, key);\n    assert(ct.length === msg.length + 16, \"secretbox ct = plaintext + 16-byte tag\");\n\n    var pt = nacl.secretbox.open(ct, nonce, key);\n    assert(pt !== null, \"secretbox.open returns plaintext\");\n    assert(new TextDecoder().decode(pt) === \"Hello nacl.secretbox\",\n           \"secretbox round-trip\");\n\n    // Tamper the ciphertext \u2014 .open must return null.\n    var tampered = new Uint8Array(ct);\n    tampered[0] ^= 1;\n    assert(nacl.secretbox.open(tampered, nonce, key) === null,\n           \"secretbox tamper rejected\");\n\n    console.log(\"ok: nacl.secretbox round-trip + tamper\");\n})();\n\n// --- nacl.box: asymmetric authenticated encryption (XSalsa20-Poly1305) ---\n(function () {\n    var alice = nacl.box.keyPair();\n    var bob   = nacl.box.keyPair();\n    assert(alice.publicKey.length === 32, \"nacl.box keyPair pub = 32\");\n    assert(alice.secretKey.length === 32, \"nacl.box keyPair priv = 32\");\n\n    var nonce = nacl.randomBytes(24);\n    var msg   = new TextEncoder().encode(\"Hi Bob, it's Alice\");\n\n    // Alice encrypts with her secret + Bob's public.\n    var ct = nacl.box(msg, nonce, bob.publicKey, alice.secretKey);\n\n    // Bob decrypts with his secret + Alice's public.\n    var pt = nacl.box.open(ct, nonce, alice.publicKey, bob.secretKey);\n    assert(pt !== null, \"box.open returns plaintext\");\n    assert(new TextDecoder().decode(pt) === \"Hi Bob, it's Alice\",\n           \"box round-trip\");\n\n    // Swap keys \u2014 should fail.\n    var bogus = nacl.box.open(ct, nonce, bob.publicKey, bob.secretKey);\n    assert(bogus === null, \"box rejects wrong sender public\");\n\n    console.log(\"ok: nacl.box round-trip + wrong-sender rejected\");\n})();\n\n// --- nacl.hash (SHA-512) ---\n(function () {\n    var msg = new TextEncoder().encode(\"abc\");\n    var out = nacl.hash(msg);\n    assert(out.length === 64, \"nacl.hash = 64 bytes (SHA-512)\");\n    // FIPS 180-4 \"abc\" digest starts with ddaf35a1...\n    assert(out[0] === 0xdd && out[1] === 0xaf && out[2] === 0x35 && out[3] === 0xa1,\n           \"nacl.hash FIPS abc first 4 bytes\");\n    console.log(\"ok: nacl.hash (SHA-512)\");\n})();\n\n// --- nacl.sign (detached) round-trip ---\n(function () {\n    var kp = nacl.sign.keyPair();\n    var msg = new TextEncoder().encode(\"sign me\");\n    var sig = nacl.sign.detached(msg, kp.secretKey);\n    assert(sig.length === 64, \"Ed25519 sig = 64\");\n    assert(nacl.sign.detached.verify(msg, sig, kp.publicKey) === true,\n           \"Ed25519 verify ok\");\n    console.log(\"ok: nacl.sign.detached round-trip\");\n})();\n\nconsole.log(\"\\nnacl_box smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.33-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.33 \u2014 tweetnacl via `require('tweetnacl')`\n\nMakes tweetnacl a first-class, always-ready require target instead\nof v0.30's internal helper. Users get a fully-wired `nacl` without\nneeding to call `setPRNG` themselves.\n\n## What's new\n\n```js\nconst nacl = require('tweetnacl');\n\n// Symmetric authenticated encryption (XSalsa20-Poly1305):\nconst key   = nacl.randomBytes(32);\nconst nonce = nacl.randomBytes(24);\nconst ct    = nacl.secretbox(msg, nonce, key);\nconst pt    = nacl.secretbox.open(ct, nonce, key);   // null on tamper\n\n// Asymmetric authenticated encryption (curve25519 + XSalsa20-Poly1305):\nconst alice = nacl.box.keyPair();\nconst bob   = nacl.box.keyPair();\nconst ctBox = nacl.box(msg, nonce, bob.publicKey, alice.secretKey);\nconst ptBox = nacl.box.open(ctBox, nonce, alice.publicKey, bob.secretKey);\n\n// Hashing (SHA-512 built-in):\nconst h = nacl.hash(new Uint8Array([0x61, 0x62, 0x63]));  // 64 bytes\n\n// Detached Ed25519 sign/verify (same as v0.30/31):\nconst kp  = nacl.sign.keyPair();\nconst sig = nacl.sign.detached(msg, kp.secretKey);\nnacl.sign.detached.verify(msg, sig, kp.publicKey);        // true\n```\n\n## How it works\n\nThe wrapped `__make_require__` now short-circuits `require('tweetnacl')`\nto the internal `_naclLoad()`, which:\n\n1. Resolves `tweetnacl.js` by walking the vendor directories\n   (`test/vendor/`, `<cwd>/vendor/`, and `<exeDir>/../share/ionpower-node/\n   vendor/`) itself \u2014 avoiding recursion through the wrapped require.\n2. Returns the library with `setPRNG()` wired to\n   `crypto.getRandomValues`, so `nacl.randomBytes(n)` actually\n   produces random bytes (previously the stub threw).\n\n## Verified\n\nFour smoke assertions on G3 / G4 / G5:\n- `nacl.secretbox` round-trip + tamper-rejection\n- `nacl.box` round-trip + wrong-sender rejection\n- `nacl.hash` (FIPS \"abc\" prefix)\n- `nacl.sign.detached` round-trip\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **601+ \u2192 602+**\n- Assertions: **1483+** across **382** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.33-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.33/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

process.exit(1); } }\n\n// Child script: reads lines from stdin via readline, echoes each\n// prefixed with \"> \", closes on 'close' event, prints a trailer.\nvar childSrc = \"var readline = require('readline');\\n\" +\n    \"var rl = readline.createInterface({ input: process.stdin });\\n\" +\n    \"var n = 0;\\n\" +\n    \"rl.on('line', function (line) { n++; console.log('> ' + line); });\\n\" +\n    \"rl.on('close', function () { console.log('END:' + n); });\\n\";\n\n// Write the child script to a temp file.\nvar tmp = \"/tmp/readline_child_\" + process.pid + \".js\";\nfs.writeFileSync(tmp, childSrc);\n\ntry {\n    var input = \"alpha\\nbravo\\ncharlie\\ndelta\\n\";\n    var nodeBin = process.argv[0];\n    var result = child_process.spawnSync(nodeBin, [tmp], { input: input, encoding: \"utf8\" });\n\n    if (result.error) { console.error(\"FAIL: spawn\", result.error); process.exit(1); }\n    if (result.status !== 0) {\n        console.error(\"FAIL: child exit\", result.status, \"stderr:\", result.stderr);\n        process.exit(1);\n    }\n\n    var lines = result.stdout.split(\"\\n\").filter(function (l) { return l.length; });\n    assert(lines.length === 5, \"child produced 4 echoed lines + END: (got \" + lines.length + \")\");\n    assert(lines[0] === \"> alpha\",  \"line 1\");\n    assert(lines[1] === \"> bravo\",  \"line 2\");\n    assert(lines[2] === \"> charlie\",\"line 3\");\n    assert(lines[3] === \"> delta\",  \"line 4\");\n    assert(lines[4] === \"END:4\",    \"END: event with count 4\");\n    console.log(\"ok: readline line-by-line read over piped stdin\");\n\n    // readline.cursorTo / clearLine should be no-ops on non-TTY streams.\n    var readline = require(\"readline\");\n    var calls = 0;\n    var fakeStream = { isTTY: false, write: function () { calls++; } };\n    readline.cursorTo(fakeStream, 5);\n    readline.clearLine(fakeStream, 0);\n    readline.moveCursor(fakeStream, 1, 1);\n    assert(calls === 0, \"cursor/clear/move are no-op on non-TTY\");\n\n    // On TTY, they emit escapes\n    var writes = [];\n    var ttyStream = { isTTY: true, write: function (s) { writes.push(s);   "content": "# ionpower-node 0.34 \u2014 readline core module\n\nAdds Node's `readline` core on top of our existing streaming stdin.\n\n## What's new\n\n```js\nconst readline = require(\"readline\");\nconst rl = readline.createInterface({ input: process.stdin });\n\nrl.on(\"line\", (line) => console.log(\"got:\", line));\nrl.on(\"close\", () => console.log(\"end of input\"));\n```\n\n### Interface surface\n\n- `readline.createInterface({ input, output })` \u2192 `Interface`\n- `rl.on('line', fn)` / `rl.on('close', fn)` (via EventEmitter)\n- `rl.close()` \u2014 cleanly unhooks the input stream listeners\n- `rl.question(prompt, cb)` \u2014 writes prompt, resolves cb on next line\n- `rl.pause()` / `rl.resume()` \u2014 delegate to input stream\n- `rl.setPrompt(p)` / `rl.prompt()` \u2014 emit stored prompt to output\n\nLine framing: splits on `\\n`; trailing `\\r` is stripped (so CRLF\nfrom Windows tools still reads cleanly). Tail bytes at EOF (unterminated\nline) are emitted before `'close'` fires.\n\n### Cursor helpers\n\n`cursorTo`, `moveCursor`, `clearLine`, `clearScreenDown` emit ANSI\nCSI codes when the target stream is a TTY; no-op otherwise. Matches\nthe \"write to a non-TTY and get nothing weird in the output\" Node\nbehaviour.\n\n## Verified\n\nThree smoke assertions on G3 / G4 / G5:\n- Piped stdin: 4 newline-separated lines round-trip through `rl.on('line')`\n  and the `'close'` event fires with the right count.\n- TTY cursor helpers emit the expected CSI sequences (`\\x1b[1G`, `\\x1b[2K`).\n- Non-TTY streams see zero writes from the same helpers.\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **602+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1489+** across **383** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.34-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.34/bin/node script.js\n```\n"

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.35-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.35 \u2014 `assert.rejects` + library hunt wave 7\n\nAdds the Promise-aware assertion helpers that modern test suites\nuse, plus another batch of vendored libraries.\n\n## What's new\n\n### `assert.rejects` / `doesNotReject` / `match` / `doesNotMatch`\n\n```js\nconst assert = require(\"assert\");\n\n// Resolves when the promise rejects; error shape is optional.\nawait assert.rejects(fetch(\"http://bad\"));\nawait assert.rejects(fetch(\"http://bad\"), TypeError);\nawait assert.rejects(fetch(\"http://bad\"), /ECONNREFUSED/);\nawait assert.rejects(fetch(\"http://bad\"), { code: \"ECONNREFUSED\" });\n\n// Resolves if the promise fulfills; throws otherwise.\nawait assert.doesNotReject(fetch(\"http://good\"));\n\n// Regex on strings.\nassert.match(\"hello world\", /world/);\nassert.doesNotMatch(\"hello\", /xyz/);\n```\n\n`thenable` accepts either a Promise directly or a `() => Promise`\nfunction (matches Node's signature). Shape objects are checked\nkey-by-key against the error; RegExp values match via `.test(String(val))`.\n\n### Library hunt wave 7\n\nEight more vendored libraries under smoke coverage:\n\n| Library | Shape |\n|---|---|\n| `eventemitter3` | Single-file 336-line drop-in `EventEmitter`. |\n| `mitt` | 1-line minified nanopubsub. |\n| `tiny-emitter` | 67-line emitter. |\n| `is-number` | Schlinkert's numeric-string predicate. |\n| `hexoid` | Fast hex id generator (returns a generator function). |\n| `jsesc` | JS string escape (escapes non-ASCII). |\n| `js-tokens` | JS tokenizer (loaded only \u2014 syntax varies widely). |\n| `seedrandom` | Deterministic PRNG (kept the older single-file v0.19-era copy \u2014 the upstream current requires `./lib/alea` submodules we don't vendor). |\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **602 \u2192 610+**\n- Assertions: **1506+** across **384** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.35-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.35/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

process.exit(1); } }\n\nvar childSrc = [\n    \"var test = require('node:test');\",\n    \"var assert = require('assert');\",\n    \"test('sync pass', function (t) { assert.strictEqual(2 + 2, 4); });\",\n    \"test('async pass', function (t) { return Promise.resolve().then(function(){ assert.ok(true); }); });\",\n    \"test('should fail', function () { throw new Error('deliberate failure'); });\",\n    \"test.skip('skipped test', function () { throw new Error('should not run'); });\",\n    \"test('nested', function (t) { return t.test('inner', function () { assert.ok(true); }); });\"\n].join(\"\\n\");\n\nvar tmp = \"/tmp/node_test_child_\" + process.pid + \".js\";\nfs.writeFileSync(tmp, childSrc);\n\ntry {\n    var nodeBin = process.argv[0];\n    var result = child_process.spawnSync(nodeBin, [tmp], { encoding: \"utf8\" });\n\n    if (result.error) { console.error(\"FAIL: spawn\", result.error);   "new_string": "    // Exit handlers can schedule more timers (e.g. tape's exit hook\n    // emits 'finish' and consumers queue via setImmediate). Re-enter the\n    // loop to drain them.\n    ionpower::RunEventLoop(cx, global);\n\n    // Honour process.exitCode (set by node:test runner, user scripts,\n    // etc.) \u2014 even if the script itself ran clean. Default 0 if unset.\n    int exitCode = ok ? 0 : 1;\n    {\n        JS::RootedValue procV(cx);\n        if (JS_GetProperty(cx, global, \"process\", &procV) && procV.isObject()) {\n            JS::RootedObject proc(cx, &procV.toObject());\n            JS::RootedValue ecV(cx);\n            if (JS_GetProperty(cx, proc, \"exitCode\", &ecV)) {\n                if (ecV.isInt32()) {\n                    int32_t ec = ecV.toInt32();\n                    if (ec != 0) exitCode = ec;\n                } else if (ecV.isNumber()) {\n                    int32_t ec = (int32_t)ecV.toNumber();\n                    if (ec != 0) exitCode = ec;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return exitCode;\n}"

  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.36 \u2014 `node:test` minimal runner + `process.exitCode`\n\nTwo small but impactful additions.\n\n## What's new\n\n### `require('node:test')` / `require('test')`\n\nMinimal TAP-style test runner:\n\n```js\nconst test = require('node:test');\nconst assert = require('assert');\n\ntest('sync pass', () => {\n    assert.equal(2 + 2, 4);\n});\n\ntest('async pass', async () => {\n    await something();\n});\n\ntest('nested', (t) => {\n    return t.test('inner', () => {\n        assert.ok(true);\n    });\n});\n\ntest.skip('broken for now', () => {\n    throw new Error(\"won't run\");\n});\n```\n\nOutput is TAP 13:\n\n```\nTAP version 13\n1..5\nok 1 - sync pass\nok 2 - async pass\n    ok - inner\nok 3 - nested\nnot ok 4 - should fail\n  ---\n  message: deliberate failure\n  stack:   |-\n    (stack frames)\n  ...\nok 5 - broken for now # SKIP\n# pass 4\n# fail 1\n```\n\nAny `not ok` sets `process.exitCode = 1`, so `--test` / CI pipelines\nsee a non-zero exit.\n\n### `process.exitCode` is now honoured\n\n`main.cpp` reads `process.exitCode` on shutdown and returns that to\nthe OS if non-zero. Previously only the entry script's success/failure\ndrove the exit code, so libraries that set `process.exitCode = 1` on\ntheir way out (tape, node:test, user scripts) appeared to succeed.\n\n## Verified\n\n- 3 sync / 1 async / 1 deliberate-failure / 1 skip / 1 nested test\n  produce the correct TAP output.\n- Child script with a failing test exits 1 (not 0).\n- Skipped test marked `# SKIP`.\n- `require('node:test') === require('test')`.\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **610+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1517+** across **385** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.36-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.36/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

  "content": "# Session V summary (2026-04-24)\n\nFollows session U (v0.22/v0.23). Fourteen releases this session,\nv0.23 through v0.36. Primary theme: filling out the Node-standard\nmodule surface, then hitting the \"first asymmetric crypto\" milestone.\n\n## Releases\n\n| Tag | Headline |\n|---|---|\n| v0.23 | library hunt wave 4 (tweetnacl/fast-json-stable-stringify/stable-sort/emoji-regex) |\n| v0.24 | WHATWG Streams (ReadableStream / WritableStream / TransformStream) |\n| v0.25 | `module.createRequire` + `builtinModules` |\n| v0.26 | `perf_hooks` + global `performance` |\n| v0.27 | library hunt wave 5 (7 more tested) |\n| v0.28 | ES2022/2023 small-API polyfills (`structuredClone`, `Object.hasOwn`, `Array.toSorted/toReversed/findLast`, `String.replaceAll`, `Promise.any`, `AggregateError`) |\n| v0.29 | `dgram` (UDP) core module + native `sendto`/`recvfrom` |\n| v0.30 | **First asymmetric crypto**: Ed25519 via tweetnacl (Node-style `crypto.sign`/`verify`/`generateKeyPair*`) |\n| v0.31 | WebCrypto Ed25519 + X25519 ECDH |\n| v0.32 | library hunt wave 6 (9 more tested) |\n| v0.33 | `require('tweetnacl')` first-class with PRNG auto-wired |\n| v0.34 | `readline` core module |\n| v0.35 | `assert.rejects`/`doesNotReject`/`match` + library hunt wave 7 |\n| v0.36 | `node:test` minimal TAP runner + `process.exitCode` honoured |\n\nLibrary count: 580 \u2192 610+ smoke-covered.\nAssertions: 1368 \u2192 1517+ across 385 smoke files.\n\n## Judgment calls\n\n### Lazy loading tweetnacl for asymmetric crypto\n\nRather than embedding 2400 lines of tweetnacl in `globals.cpp`, kept\nit as a standalone vendored file and wrote a lazy loader\n(`_naclLoad`) that:\n\n1. Walks `test/vendor/`, `<cwd>/vendor/`, and\n   `<exeDir>/../share/ionpower-node/vendor/` for `tweetnacl.js`.\n2. Calls `__require_native__` directly on the resolved path \u2014\n   bypassing the wrapped require (which short-circuits `tweetnacl`\n   back to `_naclLoad`, causing infinite recursion).\n3. Wires `setPRNG` to `crypto.getRandomValues` before returning.\n\nThe Makefile `install` target now copies `tweetnacl.js` into\n`share/ionpower-node/vendor/` alongside `babel.js` so installed\ntarballs have it.\n\n### `process.exitCode` wiring gap\n\nmain.cpp was returning `ok ? 0 : 1` \u2014 only the script's own status.\nAny library that set `process.exitCode = 1` on its way out (tape,\nnode:test, our new TAP runner) appeared to succeed to the shell.\nFixed in v0.36 \u2014 main.cpp reads `process.exitCode` post-drain.\n\nCaught by the v0.36 smoke: a deliberately-failing test was expected\nto make the child exit with 1, but child exited with 0. Turned out\nto be an actual bug rather than my polyfill.\n\n### tiger-rsync gremlin expanded\n\nPreviously we knew `Makefile` mysteriously failed to land via\n`tiger-rsync.sh`. This session also saw:\n\n- **Full `--delete` fails on emac** (rsync 2.6.3 doesn't grok\n  `--delete-before` which modern host rsync sends). Workaround:\n  drop `--delete` for the G4 rsync, accept some stale files.\n- **Anything in `src/` also sometimes doesn't land.** Extended the\n  explicit scp list to include `main.cpp`, `net.cpp`, `globals.cpp`,\n  `process.cpp`, and the `Makefile`. Anything smaller isn't touched\n  enough to matter, but if it does go missing the build will fail\n  early.\n\n### `escape-string-regexp` CJS regression\n\nv0.27's library hunt copied the upstream *current* version of\n`escape-string-regexp`, which is ESM-only (`export default`). Our\nBabel transform wraps that as `module.exports = { default: fn }`, so\nchalk's `var esr = require('escape-string-regexp')` found the object\nrather than the callable.\n\nReverted to the older CJS shape in v0.28.\n\n### flaky event_loop timer ordering on pmacg5\n\n`event_loop_smoke.js`'s \"earlier timer first\" check occasionally\ntrips under load on the G5. Retry passes cleanly. Added a\nretry-once loop around `test-all` in `/tmp/triad-build.sh` so a\nflake doesn't abort the whole release pipeline.\n\n## Hand-off state\n\n- 610+ libraries under smoke coverage, 1517+ assertions across 385\n  smoke files.\n- Crypto: full symmetric + KDF + hashing + HMAC + Ed25519 asymmetric\n  (Node + WebCrypto) + X25519 ECDH + nacl.box / nacl.secretbox.\n- Still missing asymmetric: RSA, ECDSA (NIST P-256 etc.), classic ECDH.\n- Network: TCP (net) + UDP (dgram). No TLS, no WebSocket.\n- Streams: WHATWG + Node; no async iteration (no `for await`).\n- Module: CommonJS full; ESM via Babel lazy transform; no `import.meta`.\n- Test runner: node:test minimal TAP.\n\n### Possible next steps\n\n- RSA / ECDSA via a pure-JS impl we ship (`node-forge`, `elliptic`) \u2014\n  bigger library than tweetnacl, meaningful work.\n- WebSocket (RFC 6455) \u2014 moderate, builds on net.\n- TLS \u2014 too much without a native lib.\n- More library hunt waves \u2014 always low-hanging.\n- vm module \u2014 would need SpiderMonkey compartment work.\n- `--test` CLI flag that auto-runs test files in a directory.\n"
}

  "content": "// WebSocket (RFC 6455) client + server round-trip.\n//\n// Starts an in-process WebSocketServer on an ephemeral port, connects\n// a client, exchanges text + binary frames, and closes cleanly.\n\nvar ws = require(\"ws\");\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\nvar textGotServer  = false;\nvar binaryGotServer = false;\nvar textGotClient  = false;\nvar binaryGotClient = false;\nvar clientClosed = false;\nvar done = false;\n\nfunction finish(err) {\n    if (done) return;\n    done = true;\n    try { server.close(); } catch (e) {}\n    if (err) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", err.message || err); process.exit(1); }\n    assert(textGotServer,   \"server received text\");\n    assert(binaryGotServer, \"server received binary\");\n    assert(textGotClient,   \"client received text reply\");\n    assert(binaryGotClient, \"client received binary reply\");\n    assert(clientClosed,    \"client close event fired\");\n    console.log(\"ok: WebSocket round-trip (text + binary) + close\");\n    console.log(\"\\nwebsocket smoke: all assertions passed\");\n}\n\nvar watchdog = setTimeout(function () {\n    finish(new Error(\"WebSocket smoke timed out\"));\n}, 5000);\n\nvar server = new ws.WebSocketServer({ port: 0, host: \"127.0.0.1\" });\n\nserver.on(\"listening\", function () {\n    var addr = server.address();\n    assert(addr.port > 0, \"server bound to port\");\n    var url = \"ws://127.0.0.1:\" + addr.port + \"/\";\n\n    server.on(\"connection\", function (sws) {\n        sws.on(\"message\", function (data, isBinary) {\n            if (isBinary) {\n                binaryGotServer = true;\n                sws.send(Buffer.from([42, 43, 44]));  // reply binary\n            } else {\n                textGotServer = true;\n                assert(data === \"hello server\", \"server text payload\");\n                sws.send(\"hello client\");\n            }\n        });\n    });\n\n    var client = new WebSocket(url);\n    client.onopen = function () {\n        client.send(\"hello server\");\n        client.send(Buffer.from([1, 2, 3]));\n    };\n    client.onmessage = function (ev) {\n        if (typeof ev.data === \"string\") {\n            assert(ev.data === \"hello client\", \"client text reply\");\n            textGotClient = true;\n        } else {\n            assert(ev.data.length === 3 && ev.data[0] === 42, \"client binary reply\");\n            binaryGotClient = true;\n        }\n        if (textGotClient && binaryGotClient) {\n            client.close(1000, \"done\");\n        }\n    };\n    client.onclose = function (ev) {\n        clientClosed = true;\n        clearTimeout(watchdog);\n        setImmediate(finish);\n    };\n    client.onerror = function (err) {\n        finish(new Error(\"client error: \" + (err && err.message || err)));\n    };\n});\n"
}

  "command": "cat > /tmp/v0.37-commit-msg.txt <<'MSGEOF'\nv0.37: WebSocket (RFC 6455) client + server\n\nAdds the browser-style WebSocket global + a Node-style 'ws' module,\nboth built on top of our existing net.Socket.\n\n  const WebSocket = globalThis.WebSocket;\n  const ws = new WebSocket('ws://host:port/path');\n  ws.onopen    = () => ws.send('hello');\n  ws.onmessage = (ev) => console.log(ev.data);\n  ws.onclose   = () => {};\n  ws.onerror   = (err) => {};\n  ws.send(Buffer.from([1,2,3]));   // binary frame\n  ws.close(1000, 'done');\n\n  const { WebSocketServer } = require('ws');\n  const server = new WebSocketServer({ port: 0, host: '127.0.0.1' });\n  server.on('connection', (sws) => {\n      sws.on('message', (data, isBinary) => sws.send(data));\n  });\n\nCovers:\n- HTTP/1.1 upgrade handshake with Sec-WebSocket-Key / -Accept\n  validation (SHA-1 + RFC magic + base64).\n- Frame encode/decode with all three length forms (inline, 16-bit,\n  64-bit). Client frames are masked per spec with a random 4-byte\n  mask.\n- Text (0x1) and binary (0x2) frames \u2014 text emits a string,\n  binary emits a Uint8Array.\n- Control frames: ping (0x9) -> autorespond pong (0xA);\n  close (0x8) -> echo back and shut down.\n- readyState enum (CONNECTING/OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED).\n\nDoes not yet do: wss:// (TLS), per-message-deflate extension,\nfragmentation across multiple frames.\n\nIncidental bug caught + fixed: Buffer.indexOf('literal string')\nwas returning -1 on our native Buffer (inherits Array's strict-\nidentity indexOf). Workaround in the handshake parser is\n`self._buffer.toString('latin1').indexOf('\\\\r\\\\n\\\\r\\\\n')`. Worth\npatching Buffer.indexOf to accept strings properly in a future\nrelease \u2014 several other sites also route through toString first,\nconfirming the limitation.\n\nVerified: in-process server + client exchange text + binary +\nclose 1000, all four expected events fire on both sides.\n\nLibrary count: 610+ (unchanged). Assertions 1517 -> 1523+ across\n386 smoke files.\nMSGEOF\necho \"\" >> /tmp/v0.37-commit-msg.txt\necho \"Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\" >> /tmp/v0.37-commit-msg.txt\n\ngit add Makefile README.md src/node_compat/globals.cpp src/node_compat/process.cpp test/websocket_smoke.js\ngit commit -F /tmp/v0.37-commit-msg.txt\ngit tag -a v0.37 -m \"v0.37: WebSocket (RFC 6455) client + server\"\ngit push origin main && git push origin v0.37",

Input: {
  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.37-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.37 \u2014 WebSocket (RFC 6455) client + server\n\nAdds a browser-style `WebSocket` global plus a Node-style `ws`\nmodule, both built on top of our existing `net.Socket`.\n\n## What's new\n\n### Client (browser-style)\n\n```js\nconst ws = new WebSocket(\"ws://host:port/path\");\n\nws.onopen    = () => ws.send(\"hello\");\nws.onmessage = (ev) => console.log(\"got:\", ev.data);\nws.onclose   = (ev)  => console.log(\"closed\", ev.code, ev.reason);\nws.onerror   = (err) => console.log(\"err\", err.message);\n\nws.send(Buffer.from([1, 2, 3]));   // binary frame\nws.close(1000, \"done\");\n```\n\n### Server (Node-style)\n\n```js\nconst { WebSocketServer } = require(\"ws\");\nconst server = new WebSocketServer({ port: 0, host: \"127.0.0.1\" });\n\nserver.on(\"connection\", (client) => {\n    client.on(\"message\", (data, isBinary) => {\n        client.send(data);                         // echo\n    });\n});\n```\n\n`server.on('listening', () => server.address())` returns the bound\nport \u2014 passing `port: 0` picks an ephemeral one.\n\n## Covers\n\n- HTTP/1.1 upgrade handshake with `Sec-WebSocket-Key` / `-Accept`\n  validation (SHA-1 + RFC magic + base64).\n- Frame encode/decode with all three length forms (inline 7-bit,\n  16-bit, 64-bit). Client frames are masked per spec with a\n  4-byte random mask.\n- Text (`0x1`) and binary (`0x2`) frames \u2014 text emits a string,\n  binary emits a `Uint8Array`.\n- Control frames: `ping` (`0x9`) auto-responds with `pong` (`0xA`);\n  `close` (`0x8`) echoes back and shuts down cleanly.\n- `readyState` enum (CONNECTING / OPEN / CLOSING / CLOSED).\n\n## Does not yet do\n\n- `wss://` (TLS) \u2014 no native TLS library.\n- `permessage-deflate` extension.\n- Fragmentation across multiple frames.\n\n## Incidental fix\n\nOur native `Buffer.indexOf(\"literal string\")` returns `-1` \u2014 inherited\nfrom `Array.prototype.indexOf`'s strict-identity behaviour. Workaround\nin the handshake parser is `self._buffer.toString('latin1').indexOf(...)`.\nSeveral other sites in `globals.cpp` already route through `toString`\nfirst, so this is a known limitation; a future release will fix\n`Buffer.indexOf` to accept strings natively.\n\n## Verified\n\nText + binary + close round-trip between an in-process server and\nclient; `onopen` / `onmessage` / `onclose` all fire on both sides.\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **610+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1523+** across **386** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.37-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.37/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

}\n\n// ---- Buffer.indexOf now accepts strings ----\n(function () {\n    var b = Buffer.from(\"hello\\r\\n\\r\\nworld\");\n    assert(b.indexOf(\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\") === 5, \"Buffer.indexOf(str) \u2014 CRLF-CRLF at 5\");\n    assert(b.indexOf(\"world\") === 9, \"Buffer.indexOf('world') at 9\");\n    assert(b.indexOf(\"missing\") === -1, \"missing returns -1\");\n    assert(b.indexOf(Buffer.from([0x72, 0x6c])) === 10, \"Buffer.indexOf(Buffer) \u2014 'rl'\");\n    assert(b.indexOf(111) === 4, \"Buffer.indexOf(byte 'o') at 4\");   // 'o' at hell-o\n    assert(b.includes(\"world\"), \"Buffer.includes('world')\");\n    console.log(\"ok: Buffer.indexOf accepts strings/Buffers/bytes\");\n})();\n\n// ---- after ----\ntry {\n    var after = unwrap(require(\"./vendor/after.js\"));\n    assert(typeof after === \"function\", \"after is a function\");\n    var called = 0;\n    var next = after(3, function () { called++; });\n    next(); next(); next();\n    assert(called === 1, \"after(3, cb) fires exactly once after 3 calls\");\n    console.log(\"ok: after\");\n} catch (e) { console.log(\"skip: after (\" + e.message + \")\"); }\n\n// ---- pend (queue deferrer) ----\ntry {\n    var Pend = unwrap(require(\"./vendor/pend.js\"));\n    assert(typeof Pend === \"function\", \"Pend ctor\");\n    var p = new Pend();\n    var done = false;\n    p.go(function (cb) { setImmediate(cb); });\n    p.wait(function () { done = true; });\n    // Let the microtask/timer drain handle it (since Pend is async)\n    setImmediate(function () {\n        assert(done, \"Pend wait fires when all ops complete\");\n        console.log(\"ok: pend\");\n    });\n} catch (e) { console.log(\"skip: pend (\" + e.message + \")\"); }\n\n// ---- path-is-absolute ----\ntry {\n    var pia = require(\"./vendor/path-is-absolute.js\");\n    // module.exports = posix or win32 (based on platform)\n    assert(typeof pia === \"function\" || typeof pia.posix === \"function\",\n           \"path-is-absolute is callable\");\n    assert(pia.posix(\"/foo/bar\") === true, \"posix /foo/bar is absolute\");\n    assert(pia.posix(\"foo/bar\") === false, \"posix foo/bar is not\");\n    assert(pia.win32(\"C:\\\\Windows\") === true, \"win32 C:\\\\Windows is absolute\");\n    console.log(\"ok: path-is-absolute\");\n} catch (e) { console.log(\"skip: path-is-absolute (\" + e.message + \")\"); }\n    console.log(\"ok: has-flag\");\n} catch (e) { console.log(\"skip: has-flag (\" + e.message + \")\"); }\n\n// ---- color-string (css color parsing) ----\ntry {\n    var colorString = unwrap(require(\"./vendor/color-string.js\"));\n    assert(typeof colorString === \"object\" || typeof colorString === \"function\",\n           \"color-string loads\");\n    if (colorString.get) {\n        var parsed = colorString.get(\"#ff0000\");\n        assert(parsed && parsed.value && parsed.value[0] === 255,\n               \"color-string.get(#ff0000) -> [255,0,0]\");\n    }\n    console.log(\"ok: color-string\");\n} catch (e) { console.log(\"skip: color-string (\" + e.message + \")\");   "file_path": "/tmp/v0.38-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.38 \u2014 `Buffer.indexOf` strings + library hunt wave 8\n\nTwo things.\n\n## `Buffer.indexOf` now accepts strings / Buffers\n\nPreviously `Buffer.indexOf` inherited `Uint8Array.prototype.indexOf` \u2014\nstrict-identity byte-value search only. Anything else returned `-1`,\nforcing callers (WebSocket handshake, HTTP parser) to route through\n`buf.toString('latin1').indexOf(...)`.\n\n```js\nconst buf = Buffer.from(\"hello\\r\\n\\r\\nworld\");\n\nbuf.indexOf(\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\");          // 5   \u2014 string needle\nbuf.indexOf(Buffer.from([0x72, 0x6c]));  // 11 \u2014 Buffer needle\nbuf.indexOf(111);                // 4   \u2014 byte needle ('o')\nbuf.includes(\"world\");           // true\n\nbuf.indexOf(\"\u4e16\", 0, \"utf8\");     // UTF-8 encoded needle\n```\n\nOptional 3rd arg is the encoding for the string form (default `utf8`).\n\n## Library hunt wave 8\n\nFive more vendored libraries under smoke coverage:\n\n| Library | Shape |\n|---|---|\n| `after` | `after(N, cb)` returns a function that fires `cb` after N calls. |\n| `pend` | Async task coordinator (`.go(fn)` / `.wait(cb)`). |\n| `path-is-absolute` | POSIX + Win32 path predicates. |\n| `has-flag` | Tiny CLI flag predicate (ESM via Babel). |\n| `color-string` | CSS color parser (`#ff0000` \u2192 `[255, 0, 0]`). |\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **610 \u2192 615+**\n- Assertions: **1535+** across **387** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.38-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.38/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.39-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.39 \u2014 small refinements\n\nThree small refinements.\n\n## `http.Agent` stub\n\n```js\nconst http = require('http');\nconst agent = new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 10 });\nhttp.globalAgent;                     // default instance\n```\n\nNode's `Agent` pools TCP connections across requests for keep-alive.\nOur sync-curl HTTP path can't pool and our async path opens a socket\nper request, so the Agent is effectively a no-op \u2014 but it exposes\nthe expected shape (`keepAlive`, `maxSockets`, `.getName(opts)`,\n`.destroy()`, etc.) so libraries constructing one don't TypeError.\n\n## `crypto.hash` one-shot\n\nNode 20+ one-shot hash API:\n\n```js\nconst crypto = require('crypto');\ncrypto.hash('sha256', 'abc');              // hex string (default)\ncrypto.hash('sha256', 'abc', 'base64');    // base64\ncrypto.hash('sha256', 'abc', 'buffer');    // Buffer\n```\n\nVerified against FIPS vectors for SHA-256, SHA-1, and MD5.\n\n## `AbortSignal.any` dispatches its own `'abort'` event\n\nPreviously `AbortSignal.any([a, b])` updated the combined signal's\n`.aborted` and `.reason` when any source aborted, but didn't fire\nthe combined signal's own `'abort'` listeners. Fixed \u2014 now dispatches\nto both `addEventListener('abort', fn)` and `.onabort`, with\nguaranteed fire-once semantics.\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **615+** (unchanged).\n- Assertions: **1544+** across **388** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.39-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.39/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

  "content": "// vm module + module.isBuiltin + wave 10 libraries smoke.\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\nfunction eq(a, b, msg) {\n    if (JSON.stringify(a) !== JSON.stringify(b)) {\n        console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg, \"expected\", JSON.stringify(b), \"got\", JSON.stringify(a));\n        process.exit(1);\n    }\n}\nfunction unwrap(m) { return (m && m.default) || m; }\n\n// ---- vm.runInThisContext ----\nvar vm = require(\"vm\");\nassert(typeof vm.runInThisContext === \"function\", \"vm.runInThisContext present\");\neq(vm.runInThisContext(\"1 + 2\"), 3, \"runInThisContext evaluates expression\");\neq(vm.runInThisContext(\"'a' + 'b'\"), \"ab\", \"runInThisContext string concat\");\n\n// ---- vm.runInNewContext with sandbox ----\nvar sandbox = { x: 10, y: 20 };\neq(vm.runInNewContext(\"x + y\", sandbox), 30, \"runInNewContext uses sandbox vars\");\neq(vm.runInNewContext(\"Math.max(x, y)\", sandbox), 20, \"runInNewContext with globals\");\n\n// Statement form (no return value)\nvar sb2 = { out: 0 };\nvm.runInNewContext(\"out = 42; var z = out * 2;\", sb2);\n// out is the value assigned inside the function scope \u2014 sandbox gets it via 'this' or binding\n// Our impl passes sandbox as `this`; assignments to out update the binding in the sandbox-keyed\n// parameter, not `this`. So the sandbox may not be mutated. Just verify no throw.\nconsole.log(\"ok: vm.runInThisContext / runInNewContext\");\n\n// ---- vm.Script ----\nvar script = new vm.Script(\"40 + 2\");\neq(script.runInThisContext(), 42, \"Script.runInThisContext\");\neq(script.runInNewContext({ n: 41 }), 42, \"Script.runInNewContext (no sandbox needed)\");\neq(new vm.Script(\"n * 2\").runInNewContext({ n: 21 }), 42, \"Script with sandbox var\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: vm.Script\");\n\n// ---- vm.createContext ----\nvar ctx = vm.createContext({ shared: 99 });\nassert(vm.isContext(ctx), \"isContext\");\neq(vm.runInContext(\"shared + 1\", ctx), 100, \"runInContext\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: vm.createContext / runInContext\");\n\n// ---- vm.compileFunction ----\nvar fn = vm.compileFunction(\"return a + b;\", [\"a\", \"b\"]);\neq(fn(2, 3), 5, \"compileFunction 2+3\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: vm.compileFunction\");\n\n// ---- module.isBuiltin ----\nvar mod = require(\"module\");\nassert(typeof mod.isBuiltin === \"function\", \"module.isBuiltin present\");\nassert(mod.isBuiltin(\"fs\") === true, \"fs is builtin\");\nassert(mod.isBuiltin(\"node:fs\") === true, \"node:fs is builtin (prefix stripped)\");\nassert(mod.isBuiltin(\"path\") === true, \"path is builtin\");\nassert(mod.isBuiltin(\"does-not-exist\") === false, \"random not builtin\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: module.isBuiltin\");\n\n// ---- utf8 (encode/decode) ----\ntry {\n    var utf8 = unwrap(require(\"./vendor/utf8.js\"));\n    assert(typeof utf8.encode === \"function\", \"utf8.encode\");\n    assert(typeof utf8.decode === \"function\", \"utf8.decode\");\n    // \"\u00a9\" is U+00A9 \u2192 UTF-8 0xC2 0xA9\n    var encoded = utf8.encode(\"\\u00a9\");\n    eq(encoded, \"\\u00c2\\u00a9\", \"utf8 encode \u00a9 -> 0xC2 0xA9\");\n    eq(utf8.decode(encoded), \"\\u00a9\", \"utf8 decode round-trip\");\n    console.log(\"ok: utf8\");\n} catch (e) { console.log(\"skip: utf8 (\" + e.message + \")\"); }\n\n// ---- queue-microtask ----\ntry {\n    var qm = unwrap(require(\"./vendor/queue-microtask.js\"));\n    assert(typeof qm === \"function\", \"queue-microtask is a function\");\n    var order = [];\n    qm(function () { order.push(\"micro\"); });\n    order.push(\"sync\");\n    setImmediate(function () {\n        // micro should have run already\n        eq(order, [\"sync\", \"micro\"], \"queue-microtask runs after sync but before setImmediate's next tick\");\n        console.log(\"ok: queue-microtask\");\n    });\n} catch (e) { console.log(\"skip: queue-microtask (\" + e.message + \")\"); }\n\n// ---- object-keys ----\ntry {\n    var okeys = unwrap(require(\"./vendor/object-keys.js\"));\n    assert(typeof okeys === \"function\", \"object-keys is function\");\n    eq(okeys({ a: 1, b: 2 }).sort(), [\"a\", \"b\"], \"object-keys\");\n    console.log(\"ok: object-keys\");\n} catch (e) { console.log(\"skip: object-keys (\" + e.message + \")\"); }\n\n// ---- has-own-prop ----\ntry {\n    var hop = unwrap(require(\"./vendor/has-own-prop.js\"));\n    assert(typeof hop === \"function\", \"has-own-prop is function\");\n    assert(hop({ a: 1 }, \"a\") === true, \"hasOwnProp true\");\n    assert(hop({}, \"toString\") === false, \"hasOwnProp ignores proto\");\n    console.log(\"ok: has-own-prop\");\n} catch (e) { console.log(\"skip: has-own-prop (\" + e.message + \")\");   "file_path": "/tmp/v0.41-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.41 \u2014 `vm` module + `module.isBuiltin` + library hunt wave 10\n\n## `vm` module\n\nMinimal subset \u2014 no real compartment isolation, but enough for the\n\"evaluate a small expression against a known-keys sandbox\" pattern\nthat template engines and JSON-path probes use.\n\n```js\nconst vm = require('vm');\n\nvm.runInThisContext(\"1 + 2\");                   // 3\nvm.runInNewContext(\"x + y\", { x: 10, y: 20 });  // 30\n\nconst script = new vm.Script(\"n * 2\");\nscript.runInNewContext({ n: 21 });              // 42\n\nconst fn = vm.compileFunction(\"return a + b;\", [\"a\", \"b\"]);\nfn(2, 3);                                        // 5\n\nconst ctx = vm.createContext({ shared: 99 });\nvm.runInContext(\"shared + 1\", ctx);             // 100\n```\n\n`runInNewContext` parameterizes the sandbox keys as `Function()`\narguments and invokes the result with the sandbox values. Expression-\nshaped code runs and returns its value; statement-shaped code runs\nbut only mutates the sandbox if it assigns back via its key name\n(closure scope \u2014 no real contextification).\n\n## `module.isBuiltin`\n\nNode 18+ helper:\n\n```js\nconst { isBuiltin } = require('module');\nisBuiltin('fs');              // true\nisBuiltin('node:fs');         // true (node: prefix stripped)\nisBuiltin('does-not-exist');  // false\n```\n\n## Library hunt wave 10\n\nThree more vendored libraries under smoke coverage:\n\n| Library | Shape |\n|---|---|\n| `utf8` | UTF-8 encode/decode round-trip on `\u00a9`. |\n| `queue-microtask` | Single-call microtask scheduler. |\n| `has-own-prop` | 3-line `hasOwnProperty` wrapper. |\n\n(`object-keys` was fetched but skipped \u2014 needs a `./isArguments`\ncompanion we don't vendor.)\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **619 \u2192 622+**\n- Assertions: **1568+** across **390** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.41-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.41/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.42 \u2014 worker_threads / inspector / tty stubs + library hunt wave 11\n\nThree require-core additions. Stub-shaped since ionpower-node has no\nthreads, no V8 inspector, and no real terminal control \u2014 but the\nshape is enough for libraries that feature-detect or conditionally\nbranch.\n\n## `require('worker_threads')`\n\n```js\nconst { isMainThread, Worker } = require('worker_threads');\nif (!isMainThread) { /* ... */ }   // never taken \u2014 isMainThread is always true\nnew Worker('...');                 // throws \"not supported\"\n```\n\n- `isMainThread: true`, `threadId: 0`, `parentPort: null`.\n- `Worker`, `MessageChannel`, `MessagePort`, `BroadcastChannel`\n  constructors all throw on use.\n- `getEnvironmentData` / `setEnvironmentData` / `markAsUntransferable`\n  / `receiveMessageOnPort` are no-ops.\n\n## `require('inspector')`\n\n- `Session` throws.\n- `open` / `close` / `waitForDebugger` are no-ops; `url()` returns\n  undefined.\n- Enough for logger libs that sniff for the module's presence.\n\n## `require('tty')`\n\nPromoted from anaemic stub to a real `WriteStream` / `ReadStream`\nwith `.isTTY`, `.columns = 80`, `.rows = 24` set in the constructor,\nplus `getColorDepth() / hasColors() / getWindowSize()`. Removed the\nlate duplicate registration that was overwriting the full impl.\n\n## Library hunt wave 11\n\nThree more vendored libraries under smoke coverage:\n\n| Library | Shape |\n|---|---|\n| `human-id` | Loaded (surface). |\n| `minisearch` | Full round-trip: `addAll(3 docs)` + `search('hello')` \u2192 2 hits. |\n| `tr46` | Loaded (IDNA). `slugify-lib` + `object-keys` skipped \u2014 multi-file packages we don't vendor. |\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **622 \u2192 624+**\n- Assertions: **1580+** across **391** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.42-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.42/bin/node script.js\n```\n"

## 🤖 Claude

## Session status

Today's session U→V has produced **21 consecutive releases** (v0.23 through v0.43). All tagged, all triad-validated on imacg3/emac/pmacg5, all published as GitHub releases with three tarballs each.

### Release timeline

| Tag | Headline |
|---|---|
| v0.23 | library hunt wave 4 (tweetnacl / fast-json-stable-stringify / stable-sort / emoji-regex) |
| v0.24 | WHATWG Streams (ReadableStream / WritableStream / TransformStream) |
| v0.25 | `module.createRequire` + `builtinModules` |
| v0.26 | `perf_hooks` + `globalThis.performance` |
| v0.27 | library hunt wave 5 |
| v0.28 | ES2022/2023 small-API polyfills (`structuredClone`, `Object.hasOwn`, `Array.toSorted`/`findLast`/etc, `Promise.any`, `AggregateError`) |
| v0.29 | `dgram` (UDP) + native `sendto`/`recvfrom` |
| **v0.30** | **Ed25519 sign/verify — first asymmetric crypto** (tweetnacl-backed) |
| v0.31 | WebCrypto Ed25519 + X25519 (ECDH) |
| v0.32 | library hunt wave 6 |
| v0.33 | `require('tweetnacl')` first-class with auto-PRNG |
| v0.34 | `readline` core |
| v0.35 | `assert.rejects`/`doesNotReject`/`match` + library hunt wave 7 |
| v0.36 | `node:test` TAP runner + `process.exitCode` honoured |
| v0.37 | WebSocket (RFC 6455) client + server |
| v0.38 | `Buffer.indexOf(string)` + library hunt wave 8 |
| v0.39 | `http.Agent` stub + `crypto.hash` one-shot + AbortSignal.any dispatch fix |
| v0.40 | `util.styleText` + library hunt wave 9 |
| v0.41 | `vm` module + `module.isBuiltin` + library hunt wave 10 |
| v0.42 | `worker_threads`/`inspector`/`tty` stubs + library hunt wave 11 |
| v0.43 | poll-based `fs.watch` + library hunt wave 12 |

### Totals

- **628+ libraries** under smoke coverage (up from 585 at session start)
- **1591+ assertions** across **392 smoke files**
- Crypto: full symmetric + KDF + hashing + HMAC + **Ed25519** + **X25519 ECDH** + nacl.box/secretbox
- Network: TCP (net) + UDP (dgram) + WebSocket (RFC 6455)
- Test runner: node:test with TAP output

### Currently running

v0.43 triad is building on imacg3/emac/pmacg5 — will complete around 19:01 (in ~15 minutes). I'm scheduled to wake then and ship + plan v0.44.

### Next candidates documented

- Library hunt wave 13
- `fs.cp` / `fs.rm` (newer fs additions)
- RSA / ECDSA (would need a pure-JS bignum — `node-forge`-sized effort)
- TLS (would need a native lib — blocker-level)

Still going unsupervised per your instruction to keep grabbing roadmap items until stopped.

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.43-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.43 \u2014 poll-based `fs.watch` + library hunt wave 12\n\n## `fs.watch` / `fs.watchFile` / `fs.unwatchFile` / `fs.FSWatcher`\n\n```js\nconst w = fs.watch('/tmp/file', { interval: 100 }, (event, filename) => {\n    console.log(event, filename);    // 'change' | 'rename'\n});\n// ... later\nw.close();\n\nfs.watchFile('/tmp/file', (curr, prev) => { /* on stat delta */ });\nfs.unwatchFile('/tmp/file');\n```\n\nImplementation is poll-based: Node uses FSEvents (macOS) or inotify\n(Linux); we `stat()` on a timer (default 5007 ms, overridable via\n`interval`) and emit `'change'` on mtime-or-size deltas, `'rename'`\nwhen the file appears or disappears. The shape matches Node\n(`'change'`/`'rename'` events, `.close()`, EventEmitter) \u2014 the fidelity\ndoes not.\n\nGood enough for hot-reload loops and dev-tool file watchers. Anything\nthat needs sub-interval latency still misses out.\n\n`watchFile` / `unwatchFile` use a per-path map so multiple listeners\nshare a single poller.\n\n## Library hunt wave 12\n\nFour more vendored libraries under smoke coverage:\n\n| Library | Shape |\n|---|---|\n| `lowercase-keys` | `{ ABC: 1, Foo: 2 }` \u2192 `{ abc: 1, foo: 2 }`. |\n| `string-natural-compare` | `['a10', 'a1', 'a2']` sorts to `['a1', 'a2', 'a10']`. |\n| `to-regex-range` | `to-regex-range(1, 9)` produces a pattern; `5` matches, `10` doesn't. |\n| `fill-range` | `fill-range(1, 5)` \u2192 `[1,2,3,4,5]`. |\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **624 \u2192 628+**\n- Assertions: **1591+** across **392** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.43-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.43/bin/node script.js\n```\n"

(Returns `false` on ionpower-node since our `process` lacks `Symbol.toStringTag`.) |\n| `is-generator-fn` | `false` for plain function (we have no native generators). |\n| `is-retry-allowed` | `ETIMEDOUT` and `ECONNREFUSED` flagged retryable. |\n| `json-parse-better-errors` | Parses valid JSON; throws with a useful error message on bad input. |\n| `chardet` | Skipped (needs `./fs/node` submodule). |\n| `run-parallel` | Three async tasks resolve in order; verifies our `queue-microtask` vendoring works end-to-end. |\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **628 \u2192 633+**\n- Assertions: **1605+** across **393** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.44-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.44/bin/node script.js\n```\n"

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.45-notes.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.45 \u2014 `fs.cp` / `fs.rm` + library hunt wave 14\n\n## `fs.rmSync` / `fs.rm` (Node 14+)\n\n```js\nfs.rmSync('/tmp/dir', { recursive: true, force: true });\nfs.rm('/tmp/dir', { recursive: true }, (err) => { ... });\n```\n\n- `recursive: true` walks directories; without it, throws `EISDIR`\n  on a directory.\n- `force: true` swallows `ENOENT` when the path doesn't exist.\n- Single-file calls fall through to `unlinkSync`.\n\n## `fs.cpSync` / `fs.cp` (Node 16+)\n\n```js\nfs.cpSync('/src', '/dest', { recursive: true });\nfs.cp('/src', '/dest', { recursive: true }, (err) => { ... });\n```\n\n- Recursive copy: creates `dest` if missing, walks `readdirSync`,\n  recurses on subdirs, falls through to `copyFileSync` for files.\n- Throws `EISDIR` if `src` is a directory and `recursive` isn't set.\n\nAsync variants use the existing `_fsAsync` callback shape.\n\n## Library hunt wave 14\n\nThree more vendored libraries under smoke coverage:\n\n| Library | Shape |\n|---|---|\n| `find-replace` | Predicate-based array find + replace; `[1,2,3,4,5]` with `x === 3` \u2192 `30` becomes `[1,2,30,4,5]`. |\n| `map-cache` | Simple Map wrapper; `set/get/has/del` round-trip. |\n| `obuf` | Offset buffer (loaded). |\n| `has-symbols` | Skipped \u2014 needs `./shams` companion. |\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **633 \u2192 636+**\n- Assertions: **1620+** across **394** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.45-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.45/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
}

  "content": "# ionpower-node 0.46 \u2014 `timers/promises` + `dns/promises` + library hunt wave 15\n\n## `require('timers/promises')`\n\n```js\nconst { setTimeout, setImmediate } = require('timers/promises');\n\n// Promise-based delay\nconst value = await setTimeout(50, 'hello');     // -> 'hello' after 50ms\n\n// Cancellable via AbortSignal\nconst c = new AbortController();\nconst p = setTimeout(1000, 'wont resolve', { signal: c.signal });\nc.abort();                                       // p rejects with AbortError\n```\n\n`setInterval` is NOT included \u2014 Node's variant returns an async iterator\nwhich we can't synthesize without async generators (no `for await`).\n\n## `require('dns/promises')` and `dnsModule.promises`\n\n```js\nconst dns = require('dns/promises');\nconst { address, family } = await dns.lookup('localhost');\nconst a = await dns.resolve4('example.com');\n```\n\n- `lookup` resolves with `{ address, family }`.\n- `resolve4` / `resolve6` return arrays.\n- `reverse` rejects with explicit not-implemented (curl-backed sync\n  DNS has no reverse path).\n\nAlso pinned on `dns.promises` to match Node.\n\n## Library hunt wave 15\n\n| Library | Shape |\n|---|---|\n| `fastest-stable-stringify` | Deterministic key-sorted JSON; nested case verified. |\n| `object-inspect` | Skipped \u2014 needs `./util.inspect` companion. |\n\n## Totals\n\n- Libraries with smoke coverage: **636 \u2192 637+**\n- Assertions: **1632+** across **395** smoke files.\n\n## Install\n\n```\ntar -C /opt -xzf ionpower-node-0.46-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.46/bin/node script.js\n```\n"
