Up to v0.72 the curl-shim\n// HTTPS path tried to UTF-8 decode the body and the failed decode\n// poisoned the JS context, leaving response.bodyBytes unset.\n//\n// v0.73 clears the pending exception so binary fetches work\n// end-to-end. We exercise that against a known-binary endpoint\n// (a small PNG from npm), and verify the bytes round-trip.\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\n// We need network \u2014 skip cleanly if offline. Use the smallest known\n// binary asset on a stable URL: an npm package tarball (mri@1.2.0\n// is 7193 bytes).\nvar URL = \"https://registry.npmjs.org/mri/-/mri-1.2.0.tgz\";\n\nconsole.log(\"fetching \" + URL);\n\nfetch(URL).then(function (r) {\n    assert(r.status === 200, \"HTTP 200 (got \" + r.status + \")\");\n    return r.arrayBuffer();\n}).then(function (ab) {\n    assert(ab instanceof ArrayBuffer, \"arrayBuffer() returns ArrayBuffer\");\n    assert(ab.byteLength > 0, \"body has bytes (got \" + ab.byteLength + \")\");\n    var bytes = new Uint8Array(ab);\n    // gzip magic bytes\n    assert(bytes[0] === 0x1f && bytes[1] === 0x8b, \"gzip magic 1f 8b at start\");\n    assert(bytes[2] === 0x08, \"deflate compression method\");\n    console.log(\"ok: fetched \" + bytes.length + \" bytes; gzip header intact\");\n\n    // Now decompress with our zlib.gunzipSync to prove the bytes\n    // are real and not corrupted.\n    var zlib = require(\"zlib\");\n    var tar = zlib.gunzipSync(Buffer.from(bytes));\n    assert(tar.length > 0, \"gunzip produced output\");\n    // First 100 bytes of a tar are the filename of the first entry.\n    // Should be ASCII like 'package/...'.\n    var firstName = tar.slice(0, 100).toString(\"utf8\").replace(/\\0.*/, \"\");\n    assert(firstName.indexOf(\"package/\") === 0, \"first tar entry is package/* (got \" + JSON.stringify(firstName) + \")\");\n    console.log(\"ok: gunzipped \" + tar.length + \" bytes, first entry: \" + firstName);\n\n    console.log(\"\\nfetch_binary smoke: all assertions passed\");\n}).catch(function (e) {\n    var msg = (e && e.message) || String(e);\n    if (/network|getaddrinfo|connect|timeout|EHOSTUNREACH|EAI_AGAIN/i.test(msg)) {\n        console.log(\"skip: offline or unreachable (\" + msg + \")\");\n        return;\n    }\n    console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg);\n    if (e && e.stack) console.error(e.stack);\n    process.exit(1);\n});\n"

  "new_string": "## Setup on a Tiger PPC host\n\nThe runtime needs a matching SpiderMonkey + IonPower JIT installed\nbeside it. The runtime is\narch-specific too \u2014 the G3 tarball expects the G3 mozjs.\n\n### One-time: install SpiderMonkey\n\nThe mozjs build is identical across all our releases \u2014 pulled once\nfrom the [v0.73 release page](https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/tag/v0.73)\nand reused thereafter:\n\n```bash\n# G3 (PPC 750 / G3 600-900 MHz iMac/iBook/PowerBook G3)\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz -C /opt/\n\n# G4 (PPC 7400 / 7450 / eMac / iBook G4 / PowerBook G4 / Mac mini G4)\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g4.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g4.tar.gz -C /opt/\n\n# G5 (PPC 970 / Power Mac G5)\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g5.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g5.tar.gz -C /opt/\n```\n\n### Per-release: install the runtime\n\nFor each `v0.NN` release, grab the matching `ionpower-node-NN-{g3,g4,g5}-ppc.tar.gz`:\n\n```bash\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/latest/download/ionpower-node-NN-g3-ppc.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf ionpower-node-NN-g3-ppc.tar.gz -C /opt/\n/opt/ionpower-node-NN/bin/node --version\n```\n\n### Building from source\n\nIf you want to rebuild on a host that already has the matching mozjs:\n\n```bash\n~/bin/tiger-rsync.sh --exclude=.git . <host>:~/tmp/ionpower-node/\nssh <host> 'cd ~/tmp/ionpower-node && make MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS=\"-mcpu=750 -mtune=750\"'\nssh <host> 'cd ~/tmp/ionpower-node && ./node test/hello.js'\nssh <host> 'cd ~/tmp/ionpower-node && make test-all'   # full smoke suite\n```\n\nThe [`scripts/triad-build.sh`](scripts/triad-build.sh) helper automates\nthe above against one of {ibookg37, emac, pmacg5} per release tag."

  "file_path": "/Users/cell/claude/ionpower-node/test/ecdsa_smoke.js",
  "content": "// ECDSA via vendored elliptic. v0.75 closes the asymmetric-crypto\n// gap that was the last \"Still missing\" item alongside RSA + Ed25519.\n//\n// We test P-256 only here -- P-384 and P-521 work the same way but\n// are slow on G3 (a single verify is ~13 s on 900 MHz, P-521 would\n// be 30+ s).\n\nvar crypto = require(\"crypto\");\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\nconsole.log(\"Generating EC P-256 keypair...\");\nvar t0 = Date.now();\nvar pair = crypto.generateKeyPairSync(\"ec\", { namedCurve: \"P-256\" });\nconsole.log(\"keygen took\", Date.now() - t0, \"ms\");\n\nassert(pair && pair.publicKey && pair.privateKey, \"keypair returned\");\nassert(pair.publicKey.type === \"public\", \"public type\");\nassert(pair.privateKey.type === \"private\", \"private type\");\nassert(pair.publicKey.asymmetricKeyType === \"ec\", \"asymmetricKeyType = ec\");\nassert(pair.publicKey.asymmetricKeyDetails &&\n       pair.publicKey.asymmetricKeyDetails.namedCurve === \"P-256\",\n       \"asymmetricKeyDetails.namedCurve = P-256\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: generateKeyPairSync('ec', { namedCurve: 'P-256' })\");\n\n// ---- Sign + verify SHA-256 (ES256) ----\nvar msg = Buffer.from(\"ECDSA on PowerPC Tiger\", \"utf8\");\nconsole.log(\"Signing (ES256)...\");\nt0 = Date.now();\nvar sig = crypto.sign(\"sha256\", msg, pair.privateKey);\nconsole.log(\"sign took\", Date.now() - t0, \"ms\");\nassert(Buffer.isBuffer(sig), \"sig is Buffer\");\n// DER-encoded ECDSA sig is variable length; for P-256 typically 70-72 bytes.\nassert(sig.length >= 64 && sig.length <= 80, \"sig is plausible DER length: \" + sig.length);\nconsole.log(\"ok: ES256 sign produced \" + sig.length + \"-byte DER signature\");\n\nconsole.log(\"Verifying...\");\nt0 = Date.now();\nvar ok = crypto.verify(\"sha256\", msg, pair.publicKey, sig);\nconsole.log(\"verify took\", Date.now() - t0, \"ms\");\nassert(ok === true, \"verify true\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: ES256 verify\");\n\n// ---- Tamper rejected ----\nvar bad = Buffer.from(sig);\nbad[0] ^= 1;\nassert(crypto.verify(\"sha256\", msg, pair.publicKey, bad) === false, \"tampered sig rejected\");\nvar other = Buffer.from(\"different msg\", \"utf8\");\nassert(crypto.verify(\"sha256\", other, pair.publicKey, sig) === false, \"wrong msg rejected\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: tamper rejected\");\n\n// ---- Sign with one key, verify with a different keypair fails ----\nconsole.log(\"Generating second EC P-256 keypair for cross-key check...\");\nvar pair2 = crypto.generateKeyPairSync(\"ec\", { namedCurve: \"P-256\" });\nassert(crypto.verify(\"sha256\", msg, pair2.publicKey, sig) === false,\n       \"verify with wrong public key fails\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: cross-key verify fails\");\n\n// ---- secp256k1 (Bitcoin curve) ----\nconsole.log(\"Generating secp256k1 keypair...\");\nvar k1pair = crypto.generateKeyPairSync(\"ec\", { namedCurve: \"secp256k1\" });\nassert(k1pair.publicKey.asymmetricKeyDetails.namedCurve === \"secp256k1\", \"secp256k1 curve label\");\nvar k1sig = crypto.sign(\"sha256\", msg, k1pair.privateKey);\nassert(crypto.verify(\"sha256\", msg, k1pair.publicKey, k1sig) === true, \"secp256k1 sign/verify\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: secp256k1 sign/verify\");\n\nconsole.log(\"\\necdsa smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"
}

  "content": "v0.75: ECDSA via vendored elliptic \u2014 closes the asymmetric crypto gap\n\nUp to v0.74 we had RSA (forge) + Ed25519 (tweetnacl) + X25519 ECDH\n(tweetnacl), but no NIST-curve ECDSA. JWT ES256/ES384, OAuth flows\nthat ship ES256, modern X.509 certs (which increasingly use ECDSA\nover RSA) all needed it. v0.75 vendors `elliptic` (the standard JS\nECC implementation, used by jws/jwa/jsonwebtoken under the hood)\nplus its 6 deps and wires it into our crypto API.\n\nCurves: P-256, P-384, P-521, secp256k1 (Bitcoin curve).\nHash algorithms: sha1, sha256, sha384, sha512.\n\n  crypto.generateKeyPairSync('ec', { namedCurve: 'P-256' })\n    -> { publicKey, privateKey }   # KeyObjects, asymmetricKeyType='ec'\n  crypto.sign('sha256', data, privateKey)   -> DER-encoded Buffer\n  crypto.verify('sha256', data, publicKey, sig) -> bool\n\nKeyObject carries asymmetricKeyDetails.namedCurve so libraries can\nintrospect the curve.\n\nPerformance on ibookg37 (G3 900 MHz): keygen ~100 ms, sign ~3 s,\nverify ~13 s. Slow because bn.js's bignum arithmetic is not tuned\nfor 32-bit PowerPC, but functionally correct.\n\nVendor layout:\n\n  test/vendor/elliptic/\n    package.json\n    lib/elliptic.js + lib/elliptic/{ec,curve,curves,utils,...}\n    node_modules/{bn.js,brorand,hash.js,hmac-drbg,\n                  minimalistic-assert,minimalistic-crypto-utils}/\n\n452 KB total in test/vendor/. Also installed under\nshare/ionpower-node/vendor/elliptic/ via the Makefile install rule.\n\nSmoke (test/ecdsa_smoke.js): P-256 keygen + sign + verify + tamper\n+ wrong-key + cross-key check + secp256k1 round-trip.\n\nREADME crypto entry now reads \"Still missing: NIST ECDH\" (down from\n\"ECDSA / NIST ECDH\"). Scope-limits prose updated accordingly.\n\nTriad: ibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) all\ngreen. 1945+ assertions across 426 smoke files.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n"

  "content": "## What's new\n\n### ECDSA on P-256 / P-384 / P-521 / secp256k1\n\nThe asymmetric crypto stack is now complete on the sign/verify side.\nUp to v0.74 we had RSA + Ed25519 + X25519. v0.75 vendors `elliptic`\n(the standard JS ECC implementation) and wires it into the existing\n`crypto.{sign,verify,generateKeyPairSync}` API:\n\n```js\nvar pair = crypto.generateKeyPairSync('ec', { namedCurve: 'P-256' });\nvar sig = crypto.sign('sha256', Buffer.from('hello'), pair.privateKey);\ncrypto.verify('sha256', Buffer.from('hello'), pair.publicKey, sig);  // true\n```\n\nCurves supported: `P-256` (`prime256v1` / `secp256r1`), `P-384`,\n`P-521`, `secp256k1` (Bitcoin's curve). Hash algorithms: `sha1`,\n`sha256`, `sha384`, `sha512`. KeyObjects carry\n`asymmetricKeyDetails.namedCurve` for libraries that introspect.\n\n### Performance heads-up\n\nECDSA is **slow** on G3:\n\n| Op | G3 (900 MHz) |\n|---|---|\n| keygen   | ~100 ms |\n| sign     | ~3 s    |\n| verify   | ~13 s   |\n\n`bn.js`'s bignum arithmetic isn't tuned for 32-bit PowerPC. Functionally\ncorrect but expect to wait. RSA via forge is similarly slow. G4 / G5\nare noticeably faster.\n\n### Vendor layout\n\n```\ntest/vendor/elliptic/\n  package.json\n  lib/elliptic.js + lib/elliptic/{ec,curve,curves,...}\n  node_modules/{bn.js,brorand,hash.js,hmac-drbg,\n                minimalistic-assert,minimalistic-crypto-utils}/\n```\n\nTotal 452 KB. Installed under `share/ionpower-node/vendor/elliptic/`\nby the Makefile install rule, so binary releases work out of the box.\n\n### What's left\n\nThe `crypto` row's last \"Still missing\" item drops from \"ECDSA / NIST\nECDH\" to just \"NIST ECDH\". P-256 / P-384 ECDH key agreement isn't\nwired yet \u2014 that needs `ec.derive(otherPubKey)` + a\n`crypto.diffieHellman` shape. X25519 ECDH (via tweetnacl) does work.\n\n## Setup (unchanged from v0.73)\n\n```bash\n# One-time mozjs install (skip if you already did this):\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz -C /opt/\n\n# v0.75 runtime\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/latest/download/ionpower-node-0.75-g3-ppc.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf ionpower-node-0.75-g3-ppc.tar.gz -C /opt/\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.75/bin/node --version\n```\n\n(Ditto with `g4`/`g5`.)\n\n## Triad\n\nibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) \u2014 all green.\n1945+ assertions across 426 smoke files, including the new\n`ecdsa_smoke.js`.\n"

Works for the common entry-script case:\n\n    var fs = require('fs');\n    var data = await fetch('https://api...').then(r => r.json());\n    fs.writeFileSync('snapshot.json', JSON.stringify(data));\n\nThe pre-detection is a brace-depth-tracking scanner that strips\ncomments + string literals, then looks for `await` tokens at\ntop level (depth 0, not inside an `async function` body). Tracks\nboth regular `async function` declarations and `async ... =>`\narrow forms. Triggers the wrap whenever a TLA token is found.\n\nLimitations:\n- CJS modules can't synchronously export a top-level-await result.\n  The wrapper kicks off async work that finishes after `require()`\n  has already returned. This is a property of CJS, not specific\n  to our runtime. Real Node only supports TLA in ESM.\n- The brace scanner has known imprecisions on async arrow bodies\n  that don't use braces. False-negatives are possible there.\n\nSmoke (test/top_level_await_smoke.js):\n- Top-level `await fakeAsync(21)` -> \"DOUBLED=42\" via spawnSync.\n- Top-level `for await (var n of gen()) { ... }` -> \"SUM=6\".\n\nThe pre-detection only runs when Babel is invoked (i.e., on parse\nfailure of the original source), so non-TLA scripts don't pay any\nextra cost.\n\nTriad: ibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) all\ngreen. 1957+ assertions across 428 smoke files.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n"
}

  "content": "## What's new\n\n### Top-level `await` for entry-point scripts\n\nCloses one of the three \"Missing\" CommonJS items in the README. The\nbootstrap now pre-detects top-level await in source files and wraps\nthem in an `async function` IIFE before handing them to Babel:\n\n```js\n// snapshot.js\nvar fs = require('fs');\nvar data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data').then(r => r.json());\nfs.writeFileSync('snapshot.json', JSON.stringify(data));\nconsole.log('saved', Object.keys(data).length, 'keys');\n```\n\n```bash\n$ ./node snapshot.js\nsaved 42 keys\n```\n\nThe pre-detection is a brace-depth-tracking scanner that strips\ncomments + string literals, then looks for `await` tokens at the\ntop level (depth 0, outside any `async function` body). It\nrecognises both `async function` declarations and `async ... =>`\narrow forms. The wrap is harmless if applied to code that doesn't\nneed it; we only invoke it when the parser has already rejected the\nsource, so non-TLA scripts pay no extra cost.\n\n### Limitations\n\n- **CJS modules** can't synchronously export a top-level-await\n  result. The wrapper kicks off async work that finishes after\n  `require()` has already returned. This is a property of CJS, not\n  specific to ionpower-node \u2014 real Node only supports TLA in ESM.\n- The brace scanner has known imprecisions on async arrow bodies\n  that don't use braces (`const f = async () => await x();`).\n  False-negatives are possible there.\n\n### Smoke\n\n`test/top_level_await_smoke.js` exercises both:\n\n```\n$ ./node test/top_level_await_smoke.js\nok: top-level await in entry-point script\nok: top-level for-await-of\n\ntop_level_await smoke: all assertions passed\n```\n\n## Setup (unchanged from v0.73)\n\n```bash\n# One-time mozjs install (skip if you already did this):\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz -C /opt/\n\n# v0.77 runtime\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/latest/download/ionpower-node-0.77-g3-ppc.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf ionpower-node-0.77-g3-ppc.tar.gz -C /opt/\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.77/bin/node --version\n```\n\n## Triad\n\nibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) \u2014 all green.\n1957+ assertions across 428 smoke files.\n\n## Tarballs\n\n| Arch | Tarball |\n|---|---|\n| G3 | `ionpower-node-0.77-g3-ppc.tar.gz` |\n| G4 | `ionpower-node-0.77-g4-ppc.tar.gz` |\n| G5 | `ionpower-node-0.77-g5-ppc.tar.gz` |\n"

  "content": "// import.meta.* + dynamic import() \u2014 both rewritten by the Babel-side\n// pre-processor (regex substitutions) so that real Node code that\n// uses ESM-only constructs runs on our CJS-only runtime.\n//\n// We test via spawned child scripts because our own *_smoke.js\n// suite is loaded directly (no parse failure path).\n\nvar fs = require(\"fs\");\nvar path = require(\"path\");\nvar os = require(\"os\");\nvar child_process = require(\"child_process\");\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\nvar nodeBin = process.argv[0];\n\nfunction runChild(name, src) {\n    var p = path.join(os.tmpdir(), \"ion-\" + name + \"-\" + process.pid + \".js\");\n    fs.writeFileSync(p, src);\n    var r = child_process.spawnSync(nodeBin, [p], { encoding: \"utf8\" });\n    try {\n        if (r.status !== 0) {\n            console.error(\"script \" + name + \" exit \" + r.status + \"\\nstderr: \" + r.stderr +\n                          \"\\nstdout: \" + r.stdout);\n            process.exit(1);\n        }\n        return r.stdout;\n    } finally { try { fs.unlinkSync(p); } catch (e) {} }\n}\n\n// ---- import.meta.url ----\nvar out = runChild(\"ima-url\",\n    'console.log(\"URL=\" + import.meta.url);\\n');\nassert(/^URL=file:\\/\\/.+ima-url-\\d+\\.js$/m.test(out),\n       \"import.meta.url is file:// + __filename: \" + JSON.stringify(out));\nconsole.log(\"ok: import.meta.url\");\n\n// ---- import.meta.filename + .dirname ----\nvar out2 = runChild(\"ima-fd\",\n    'console.log(\"FN=\" + import.meta.filename);\\n' +\n    'console.log(\"DN=\" + import.meta.dirname);\\n');\nassert(/FN=.+ima-fd-\\d+\\.js/.test(out2), \"import.meta.filename: \" + out2);\nassert(/DN=.+/.test(out2), \"import.meta.dirname: \" + out2);\nconsole.log(\"ok: import.meta.filename / .dirname\");\n\n// ---- Dynamic import() of a built-in ----\nvar out3 = runChild(\"dyn-fs\",\n    'import(\"fs\").then(function (m) { console.log(\"HAS_RFS=\" + (typeof m.default.readFileSync === \"function\")); });\\n');\nassert(/HAS_RFS=true/.test(out3), \"dynamic import('fs') resolves: \" + out3);\nconsole.log(\"ok: dynamic import('fs')\");\n\n// ---- Dynamic import() of a relative file ----\nvar helper = path.join(os.tmpdir(), \"ion-dyn-helper-\" + process.pid + \".js\");\nfs.writeFileSync(helper, 'module.exports = { greet: function (n) { return \"hi \" + n; } };\\n');\ntry {\n    var out4 = runChild(\"dyn-rel\",\n        'import(\"' + helper + '\").then(function (m) { console.log(\"OUT=\" + m.default.greet(\"world\")); });\\n');\n    assert(/OUT=hi world/.test(out4), \"dynamic import of absolute path: \" + out4);\n    console.log(\"ok: dynamic import('/abs/path')\");\n} finally { try { fs.unlinkSync(helper); } catch (e) {} }\n\n// ---- await import() (combines TLA + dynamic import) ----\nvar out5 = runChild(\"dyn-await\",\n    'var m = await import(\"fs\");\\n' +\n    'console.log(\"HAS_EXISTS=\" + (typeof m.default.existsSync === \"function\"));\\n');\nassert(/HAS_EXISTS=true/.test(out5), \"await import('fs') works: \" + out5);\nconsole.log(\"ok: await import('fs')\");\n\nconsole.log(\"\\nimport_meta smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"

  "content": "v0.78: import.meta + dynamic import() via pre-Babel regex rewrites\n\nCloses the last two \"Missing\" CommonJS items from v0.71's README.\nBoth are implemented as regex substitutions in the Babel-on-parse-\nfailure preprocessor (`_preprocessImports`), so they cost nothing\non parses that already succeed.\n\n  import.meta.url       -> (\"file://\" + __filename)\n  import.meta.filename  -> __filename\n  import.meta.dirname   -> __dirname\n  import.meta            -> { url, filename, dirname }   (object literal)\n  import(spec)           -> __dynamic_import__(spec, require)\n\n`__dynamic_import__` is a new global:\n\n    function __dynamic_import__(spec, req) {\n      return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) {\n        try {\n          var mod = (typeof req === 'function' ? req : require)(spec);\n          resolve(mod && typeof mod === 'object' && 'default' in mod\n                    ? mod : { default: mod });\n        } catch (e) { reject(e); }\n      });\n    }\n\nThe local `require` is passed in as a second arg by the regex\nrewrite, so relative specifiers (`import('./foo')`) resolve against\nthe importing module's directory. The wrapper-of-`{ default: x }`\nshape matches what real ESM dynamic-import returns, so consumer\ncode that does `(await import('./mod')).default` works against\nboth ESM-native and our CJS-backed implementations.\n\nThe detection runs only when Babel is being invoked anyway (i.e.,\non parser rejection), and string-literal / comment stripping is\ndone before the need-check so that `'import(' inside a string`\ndoesn't trigger a pointless rewrite. The substitution itself uses\n\\\\b token boundaries which are robust enough in practice.\n\nSmoke (test/import_meta_smoke.js) covers, via spawned children:\n- import.meta.url / .filename / .dirname\n- dynamic import('fs') (built-in)\n- dynamic import('/abs/path') (absolute)\n- await import('fs') (combines v0.77 TLA + v0.78 dynamic import)\n\nLimitations: import() with a specifier expression containing nested\nparens or commas isn't matched by the regex. Static `import x from\n'./y'` continues to be lowered by Babel as ESM->CJS.\n\nTriad: ibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) all\ngreen. 1962+ assertions across 429 smoke files.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n"

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.78-release/notes.md",
  "content": "## What's new\n\nCloses both remaining \"Missing\" CommonJS items from v0.71's README.\n\n### `import.meta`\n\n```js\nconsole.log(import.meta.url);       // 'file:///Users/.../app.js'\nconsole.log(import.meta.filename);  // '/Users/.../app.js'\nconsole.log(import.meta.dirname);   // '/Users/.../'\n```\n\nImplemented via regex substitutions in the Babel-on-parse-failure\npreprocessor:\n\n```\nimport.meta.url       -> (\"file://\" + __filename)\nimport.meta.filename  -> __filename\nimport.meta.dirname   -> __dirname\nimport.meta           -> { url, filename, dirname }\n```\n\n### Dynamic `import()`\n\n```js\nconst fs = (await import('fs')).default;\nfs.writeFileSync('hello.txt', 'world');\n\nconst mod = await import('./helper.js');\nmod.default.greet('world');\n```\n\n`import(spec)` is regex-rewritten to `__dynamic_import__(spec, require)`,\nwhich returns `Promise.resolve({ default: <require result> })`. The\nlocal `require` is passed in so relative specifiers resolve against\nthe importing module's directory. The `{ default: ... }` wrapper shape\nmatches what real ESM dynamic-import returns, so consumer code that\ndoes `(await import('./mod')).default` works against both ESM-native\nruntimes and our CJS-backed implementation.\n\n### Cost\n\nBoth substitutions only run when the Babel-on-parse-failure path is\nalready invoked (i.e., the source had a syntax error the SM45 parser\nrejected). String-literal / comment stripping happens before the\nneed-check, so `'import(' inside a string` doesn't trigger a pointless\nrewrite. Scripts that don't use ESM-only constructs pay zero overhead.\n\n### Limitations\n\n- `import()` with a specifier expression containing nested parens\n  or commas isn't matched by the regex (e.g.,\n  `import(\\`./pkg/${name}-${version}.js\\`)` works; `import((a, b))`\n  doesn't).\n- Static `import x from './y'` continues to be lowered by Babel as\n  ESM -> CJS as before.\n- CJS modules can't synchronously export a value computed via\n  top-level await (this is a CJS limitation, not specific to us).\n\n### Smoke\n\n`test/import_meta_smoke.js` exercises all five paths via spawned\nchildren. Output:\n\n```\nok: import.meta.url\nok: import.meta.filename / .dirname\nok: dynamic import('fs')\nok: dynamic import('/abs/path')\nok: await import('fs')\n```\n\n## Setup (unchanged from v0.73)\n\n```bash\n# One-time mozjs install (skip if you already did this):\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz -C /opt/\n\n# v0.78 runtime\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/latest/download/ionpower-node-0.78-g3-ppc.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf ionpower-node-0.78-g3-ppc.tar.gz -C /opt/\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.78/bin/node --version\n```\n\n## Triad\n\nibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) \u2014 all green.\n1962+ assertions across 429 smoke files.\n\n## Tarballs\n\n| Arch | Tarball |\n|---|---|\n| G3 | `ionpower-node-0.78-g3-ppc.tar.gz` |\n| G4 | `ionpower-node-0.78-g4-ppc.tar.gz` |\n| G5 | `ionpower-node-0.78-g5-ppc.tar.gz` |\n"

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.79-msg.txt",
  "content": "v0.79: subtle ECDSA + NIST ECDH -- WebCrypto catches up to Node-side\n\nLifts the v0.75 (ECDSA) + v0.76 (NIST ECDH) Node-shape crypto into\nthe WebCrypto `crypto.subtle` API so browser-style code works the\nsame way it does on real Node 20+.\n\n  crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'ECDSA', namedCurve: 'P-256' }, ...)\n  crypto.subtle.sign({ name: 'ECDSA', hash: 'SHA-256' }, key, data)\n  crypto.subtle.verify({ name: 'ECDSA', hash: 'SHA-256' }, key, sig, data)\n  crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'ECDH', namedCurve: 'P-256' }, ...)\n  crypto.subtle.deriveBits({ name: 'ECDH', public: peerPub }, baseKey, 256)\n\nCurves: P-256, P-384, secp256k1 (P-521 works at the elliptic level\nbut is very slow on G3 -- ~30 s per verify; we don't smoke it).\n\nInternals:\n\n- _CryptoKey gains an optional `_keyObject` field carrying our\n  Node-shape KeyObject for EC keys. subtle.{sign,verify,deriveBits}\n  delegate to the existing _ecdsaSign / _ecdsaVerify / _ecdhDerive\n  helpers via that handle.\n- _ecdsaDerToRaw + _ecdsaRawToDer convert between Node's DER\n  signatures and WebCrypto's raw r||s padded to the curve byte\n  length. r/s components are left-padded; if the high bit is set,\n  the DER encoder prepends 0x00 to keep the integer non-negative.\n- ECDH branch in deriveBits short-circuits NIST curves (where\n  baseKey._keyObject.asymmetricKeyType === 'ec') through _ecdhDerive,\n  before the existing X25519 (curve25519 via tweetnacl) branch.\n\nSmoke (test/subtle_ecdsa_smoke.js):\n- subtle.generateKey ECDSA P-256\n- subtle.sign -> raw r||s 64 bytes\n- subtle.verify true; tamper rejected\n- subtle.generateKey ECDH P-256 + deriveBits round-trip both sides\n\nTriad: ibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) all\ngreen. 1971+ assertions across 430 smoke files.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n"
}

  "content": "## What's new\n\nWebCrypto catches up to the Node-side ECDSA + NIST ECDH that landed\nin v0.75 and v0.76:\n\n```js\nconst pair = await crypto.subtle.generateKey(\n    { name: 'ECDSA', namedCurve: 'P-256' },\n    true,\n    ['sign', 'verify']\n);\n\nconst sig = await crypto.subtle.sign(\n    { name: 'ECDSA', hash: 'SHA-256' },\n    pair.privateKey,\n    new TextEncoder().encode('hello')\n);\n\nconst ok = await crypto.subtle.verify(\n    { name: 'ECDSA', hash: 'SHA-256' },\n    pair.publicKey,\n    sig,\n    new TextEncoder().encode('hello')\n);                                                // true\n```\n\n```js\nconst alice = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'ECDH', namedCurve: 'P-256' }, true, ['deriveBits']);\nconst bob   = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'ECDH', namedCurve: 'P-256' }, true, ['deriveBits']);\n\nconst sharedAlice = await crypto.subtle.deriveBits(\n    { name: 'ECDH', public: bob.publicKey },\n    alice.privateKey,\n    256\n);\n// sharedAlice equals the symmetric derive on bob's side\n```\n\nCurves: P-256, P-384, secp256k1. (P-521 works at the elliptic level\nbut is glacial on G3 \u2014 ~30 s per verify \u2014 so it's not smoke-tested.)\n\n### Why this matters\n\nBrowser-style code that uses `crypto.subtle` (the modern alternative\nto Node's `crypto.{sign,verify}`) now works without library shims.\nThat includes the `jose` family of JWT libraries (when configured\nto use WebCrypto), modern OAuth flows, and any code that targets the\nWebCrypto-or-Node convergence pattern.\n\n### Internals\n\n- `_CryptoKey` gains an optional `_keyObject` field that carries our\n  Node-shape KeyObject for EC keys. `subtle.{sign,verify,deriveBits}`\n  delegate via that handle to the existing `_ecdsaSign` /\n  `_ecdsaVerify` / `_ecdhDerive` helpers.\n- `_ecdsaDerToRaw` + `_ecdsaRawToDer` convert between Node's DER\n  signatures and WebCrypto's raw `r \u2016 s` (left-padded to the curve\n  byte length, with proper non-negative DER encoding when the high\n  bit is set).\n\n###   "old_string": "static const JSFunctionSpec kProcessFuncs[] = {\n    JS_FN(\"cwd\",            ProcessCwd,           0, 0),\n    JS_FN(\"exit\",           ProcessExit,          1, 0),\n    JS_FN(\"getenv\",         ProcessGetenv,        1, 0),",
  "new_string": "// process._setRawMode(fd, raw): tcsetattr-based raw-mode toggle for\n// process.stdin (or any TTY fd). Caches the original termios on\n// first raw-mode call so a setRawMode(false) afterwards restores\n// exactly what the user had before. Returns the previous raw state.\nstatic struct termios kSavedTermios[3];\nstatic bool           kSavedTermiosValid[3] = { false, false, false };\nstatic bool           kCurrentlyRaw[3]      = { false, false, false };\n\nstatic bool ProcessSetRawMode(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 2 || !args[0].isInt32()) {\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"process._setRawMode: (fd, bool) required\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    int fd = args[0].toInt32();\n    bool wantRaw = JS::ToBoolean(args[1]);\n    if (fd < 0 || fd > 2) {\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"process._setRawMode: fd must be 0/1/2\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    if (!isatty(fd)) {\n        // Not a TTY \u2014 silently no-op (matches Node when stdin is a pipe).\n        args.rval().setBoolean(false);\n        return true;\n    }\n    bool prev = kCurrentlyRaw[fd];\n    if (wantRaw) {\n        // Save original on first raw call.\n        if (!kSavedTermiosValid[fd]) {\n            if (tcgetattr(fd, &kSavedTermios[fd]) != 0) {\n                JS_ReportError(cx, \"process._setRawMode: tcgetattr: %s\", strerror(errno));\n                return false;\n            }\n            kSavedTermiosValid[fd] = true;\n        }\n        struct termios raw = kSavedTermios[fd];\n        // Mirror Node's setRawMode \u2014 disable canonical mode + echo +\n        // signal char generation; turn off CR/NL translation; keep\n        // 8-bit clean.\n        raw.c_iflag &= ~(IGNBRK | BRKINT | PARMRK | ISTRIP | INLCR | IGNCR | ICRNL | IXON);\n        raw.c_oflag &= ~OPOST;\n        raw.c_lflag &= ~(ECHO | ECHONL | ICANON | ISIG | IEXTEN);\n        raw.c_cflag &= ~(CSIZE | PARENB);\n        raw.c_cflag |= CS8;\n        raw.c_cc[VMIN]  = 1;\n        raw.c_cc[VTIME] = 0;\n        if (tcsetattr(fd, TCSANOW, &raw) != 0) {\n            JS_ReportError(cx, \"process._setRawMode: tcsetattr raw: %s\", strerror(errno));\n            return false;\n        }\n        kCurrentlyRaw[fd] = true;\n    } else {\n        if (kSavedTermiosValid[fd]) {\n            if (tcsetattr(fd, TCSANOW, &kSavedTermios[fd]) != 0) {\n                JS_ReportError(cx, \"process._setRawMode: tcsetattr restore: %s\", strerror(errno));\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n        kCurrentlyRaw[fd] = false;\n    }\n    args.rval().setBoolean(prev);\n    return true;\n}\n\n// process._tty_size(fd): returns { columns, rows } using TIOCGWINSZ,\n// or null if the fd isn't a TTY or the ioctl fails.\nstatic bool ProcessTtySize(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    int fd = (args.length() >= 1 && args[0].isInt32()) ? args[0].toInt32() : 1;\n    if (!isatty(fd)) { args.rval().setNull(); return true; }\n    struct winsize ws;\n    if (ioctl(fd, TIOCGWINSZ, &ws) != 0) {\n        args.rval().setNull(); return true;\n    }\n    JS::RootedObject o(cx, JS_NewPlainObject(cx));\n    JS::RootedValue cv(cx, JS::Int32Value(ws.ws_col ? ws.ws_col : 80));\n    JS::RootedValue rv(cx, JS::Int32Value(ws.ws_row ? ws.ws_row : 24));\n    if (!JS_DefineProperty(cx, o, \"columns\", cv, JSPROP_ENUMERATE)) return false;\n    if (!JS_DefineProperty(cx, o, \"rows\",    rv, JSPROP_ENUMERATE)) return false;\n    args.rval().setObject(*o);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic const JSFunctionSpec kProcessFuncs[] = {\n    JS_FN(\"cwd\",            ProcessCwd,           0, 0),\n    JS_FN(\"exit\",           ProcessExit,          1, 0),\n    JS_FN(\"getenv\",         ProcessGetenv,        1, 0),\n    JS_FN(\"_setRawMode\",    ProcessSetRawMode,    2, 0),\n    JS_FN(\"_tty_size\",      ProcessTtySize,       1, 0),"

  "content": "// process.stdin.setRawMode + tty size: now backed by tcsetattr +\n// TIOCGWINSZ instead of the v0.79 no-op stub.\n\nfunction assert(c, msg) { if (!c) { console.error(\"FAIL:\", msg); process.exit(1); } }\n\n// ---- process._setRawMode + _tty_size are exposed natively ----\nassert(typeof process._setRawMode === \"function\", \"process._setRawMode is fn\");\nassert(typeof process._tty_size === \"function\",   \"process._tty_size is fn\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: process._setRawMode + _tty_size native bindings exposed\");\n\n// ---- TTY-fd vs non-TTY-fd behaviour ----\n// stdin under our smoke runner isn't a TTY (it's the make child), so\n// setRawMode should return false (= not previously raw, no-op) and\n// tty_size should return null.\nvar prevWasRaw = process._setRawMode(0, true);\nassert(prevWasRaw === false, \"setRawMode on non-TTY stdin returns false: \" + prevWasRaw);\nconsole.log(\"ok: setRawMode no-ops on non-TTY stdin\");\n\nvar size = process._tty_size(0);\nassert(size === null, \"tty_size on non-TTY returns null: \" + JSON.stringify(size));\nconsole.log(\"ok: tty_size returns null for non-TTY\");\n\n// ---- process.stdin.setRawMode wrapper sets isRaw flag ----\nprocess.stdin.setRawMode(true);\n// On non-TTY, isRaw still flips because the wrapper sets it after the\n// native call (which is a no-op). Real Node would reject; we silently\n// mirror what the user asked for.\nassert(process.stdin.isRaw === true, \"stdin.isRaw flipped true\");\nprocess.stdin.setRawMode(false);\nassert(process.stdin.isRaw === false, \"stdin.isRaw flipped back false\");\nconsole.log(\"ok: process.stdin.setRawMode flag toggling\");\n\n// ---- Verify the function signature behaves on a real TTY ----\n// We can't actually exercise raw-mode reads in a non-interactive smoke\n// (the test runner's stdin is piped). But we can verify that calling\n// _setRawMode on a fd we know is a TTY would route through tcsetattr.\n// Check the function signature accepts (fd, bool) cleanly.\ntry { process._setRawMode(0, false); }\ncatch (e) { console.error(\"FAIL: setRawMode(0, false) threw: \" + e.message); process.exit(1); }\nconsole.log(\"ok: _setRawMode(0, false) doesn't throw\");\n\n// ---- columns / rows on process.stdout (TTY when run interactively) ----\n// This may or may not be a TTY depending on how the suite is run; just\n// check the type/range when present.\nif (process.stdout.isTTY) {\n    assert(typeof process.stdout.columns === \"number\", \"stdout.columns is number\");\n    assert(process.stdout.columns > 0 && process.stdout.columns < 4096,\n           \"stdout.columns plausible: \" + process.stdout.columns);\n    assert(typeof process.stdout.rows === \"number\", \"stdout.rows is number\");\n    console.log(\"ok: stdout.columns=\" + process.stdout.columns +\n                \" rows=\" + process.stdout.rows + \" (real TIOCGWINSZ)\");\n} else {\n    console.log(\"skip: stdout not a TTY (running under make/pipe)\");\n}\n\nconsole.log(\"\\nraw_mode smoke: all assertions passed\");\n"

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.80-msg.txt",
  "content": "v0.80: real process.stdin.setRawMode + TIOCGWINSZ terminal sizing\n\n`process.stdin.setRawMode(bool)` was a no-op stub that just flipped\nan `isRaw` flag. CLI prompt libraries (inquirer, prompts, blessed)\nsilently broke because they couldn't actually put the terminal in\nraw mode -- their per-keystroke read loops kept seeing the line-\nbuffered ICANON-mode TTY.\n\nNative bindings:\n\n- process._setRawMode(fd, raw) -- termios.h tcgetattr/tcsetattr.\n  Saves the original termios on first raw call so a subsequent\n  setRawMode(false) restores it byte-for-byte. Mirrors Node's flag\n  set: clears ICANON / ECHO / ISIG / IEXTEN, OPOST output processing,\n  and the NL/CR translation set; sets CS8 + VMIN=1/VTIME=0 for\n  per-keystroke reads. No-op (returns false) when fd isn't a TTY,\n  matching Node's behaviour for piped stdin.\n\n- process._tty_size(fd) -- sys/ioctl.h ioctl(fd, TIOCGWINSZ).\n  Returns { columns, rows } for a TTY fd, null otherwise. Used at\n  process.stdout / process.stderr install time so the columns/rows\n  fields reflect the actual terminal size instead of a hardcoded\n  80x24.\n\nJS-side:\n\n- process.stdin.setRawMode(raw) now calls process._setRawMode(0, !!raw)\n  and then sets `this.isRaw = !!raw`. The native side handles the\n  non-TTY case silently.\n- process.stdin.isRaw exposed as a normal field (was missing).\n\nREADME's `tty` row goes from \"Stub\" to \"Working\". CLI prompt tools\nthat gate behaviour on real raw-mode now work end-to-end.\n\nSmoke (test/raw_mode_smoke.js):\n- Native bindings exposed and callable.\n- _setRawMode on non-TTY stdin no-ops cleanly.\n- _tty_size returns null on non-TTY.\n- process.stdin.setRawMode flag toggling.\n- columns/rows on stdout when running interactively.\n\n(The smoke can't actually exercise raw-mode reads because the test\nrunner pipes stdin, but the surface is verified end-to-end.)\n\nTriad: ibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) all\ngreen. 1980+ assertions across 431 smoke files.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n"
}

  "file_path": "/tmp/v0.80-release/notes.md",
  "content": "## What's new\n\n### Real `process.stdin.setRawMode()`\n\nUp to v0.79, `process.stdin.setRawMode(true)` was a no-op stub that\nonly flipped an `isRaw` flag. CLI prompt libraries (inquirer, prompts,\nblessed, ink) silently broke \u2014 their per-keystroke read loops kept\nseeing line-buffered, ICANON-mode TTY input.\n\nv0.80 ships a `tcsetattr`-backed implementation:\n\n```js\nprocess.stdin.setRawMode(true);\n// terminal is now in raw mode:\n//   - no line buffering\n//   - no echo\n//   - no signal-char generation (^C / ^Z bypassed)\n//   - 8-bit clean\n//   - per-byte reads (VMIN=1, VTIME=0)\n\nprocess.stdin.setRawMode(false);\n// terminal restored to exactly what the user had before the first\n// setRawMode(true) call -- saved at first call via tcgetattr.\n```\n\nBacked by a new `process._setRawMode(fd, raw)` native that uses\n`tcgetattr` / `tcsetattr` from `<termios.h>`. No-op (returns false)\nwhen `fd` isn't a TTY, matching Node's behaviour for piped stdin.\n\n### `TIOCGWINSZ`-backed terminal sizing\n\n`process.stdout.columns` / `.rows` now report the real terminal size\nqueried via `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` at install time, instead of the\nhardcoded 80\u00d724 placeholder. Falls back to 80\u00d724 if the ioctl fails\nor the controlling terminal hasn't been sized yet.\n\n### Why this matters\n\nThe `tty` row in the README goes from \"Stub\" to \"Working\". CLI tools\nthat gate behaviour on real raw-mode (prompt UIs, single-keypress\nmenus, line editors) now actually work \u2014 previously they'd hang\nwaiting for line-buffered input that never came in raw mode.\n\n### Smoke\n\n`test/raw_mode_smoke.js` exercises the surface (native bindings\nexposed, no-op behaviour on non-TTY stdin, flag toggling, columns/rows\nwhen run interactively). The smoke runner pipes stdin, so we can't\nexercise raw-mode reads end-to-end in CI, but the surface is verified.\n\n## Setup (unchanged from v0.73)\n\n```bash\n# One-time mozjs install (skip if you already did this)\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz -C /opt/\n\n# v0.80 runtime\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/latest/download/ionpower-node-0.80-g3-ppc.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf ionpower-node-0.80-g3-ppc.tar.gz -C /opt/\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.80/bin/node --version\n```\n\n## Triad\n\nibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) \u2014 all green.\n1980+ assertions across 431 smoke files.\n\n## Tarballs\n\n| Arch | Tarball |\n|---|---|\n| G3 | `ionpower-node-0.80-g3-ppc.tar.gz` |\n| G4 | `ionpower-node-0.80-g4-ppc.tar.gz` |\n| G5 | `ionpower-node-0.80-g5-ppc.tar.gz` |\n"
}

  "content": "## What's new\n\nCloses the WebCrypto JWK story for EC keys. After v0.79 wired ECDSA\nand ECDH into `crypto.subtle`, the only missing piece was JWK\nserialisation \u2014 real-world JWS / JWT / JOSE libraries hand keys\naround in `{ kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256', x, y, d? }` form, but\n`subtle.importKey` / `exportKey` only knew OKP (Ed25519 / X25519) and\n`oct` (HMAC, AES).\n\n```js\n// Export -> JWK\nconst jwk = await crypto.subtle.exportKey('jwk', privateKey);\n//  { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256',\n//    x: '...', y: '...', d: '...',\n//    ext: true, key_ops: ['sign'] }\n\n// Import <- JWK\nconst key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(\n    'jwk', jwk,\n    { name: 'ECDSA', namedCurve: 'P-256' },\n    true, ['sign']\n);\n\n// Round-trip: signatures from the re-imported private verify against\n// the originally generated public.\n\n// Raw uncompressed point (public only):\nconst raw = await crypto.subtle.exportKey('raw', publicKey);\n//  ArrayBuffer(65): 0x04 || X(32) || Y(32)\n```\n\n### Why this matters\n\n`jose` and most modern JOSE libraries route key data through JWK at\nsome point. Until v0.81, code paths that fed our subtle's JWK importer\nan EC key got `JWK kty must be OKP` and refused to load. With v0.81 the\nimport / export round-trip works for `ECDSA` and `ECDH` on `P-256`,\n`P-384`, `secp256k1` (matching v0.75/v0.76's curve coverage on the\nNode side).\n\n### Smoke\n\n```\nok: exportKey('jwk', publicKey) -> { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256', x, y }\nok: exportKey('jwk', privateKey) -> { kty, crv, x, y, d }\nok: importKey('jwk', ...) reproduces both halves\nok: round-trip JWK -> sign -> original pub verify\nok: exportKey('raw', publicKey) -> 65-byte uncompressed point\n```\n\n## Setup (unchanged from v0.73)\n\n```bash\n# One-time mozjs install (skip if you already did this)\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz -C /opt/\n\n# v0.81 runtime\ncurl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/latest/download/ionpower-node-0.81-g3-ppc.tar.gz\nsudo tar xzpf ionpower-node-0.81-g3-ppc.tar.gz -C /opt/\n/opt/ionpower-node-0.81/bin/node --version\n```\n\n(Ditto with `g4`/`g5`.)\n\n## Triad\n\nibookg37 (G3 900 MHz), emac (G4 7450), pmacg5 (G5 970) \u2014 all green.\n1990+ assertions across 432 smoke files.\n\n## Tarballs\n\n| Arch | Tarball |\n|---|---|\n| G3 | `ionpower-node-0.81-g3-ppc.tar.gz` |\n| G4 | `ionpower-node-0.81-g4-ppc.tar.gz` |\n| G5 | `ionpower-node-0.81-g5-ppc.tar.gz` |\n"

A short menu, in rough order of "would feel like a win":

**1. Catch the session notes up.** [`docs/sessions/2026-04-25-session-1-…/notes.md`](docs/sessions/2026-04-25-session-1-v0.66-thru-v0.71-rsa-x509-zlib-jwt-mocks-ibookg37/notes.md) only documents v0.66-v0.71; the dir name is also stale (it implies the session ended at v0.71). Either rename the dir to reflect v0.66-v0.81 + the demos + workflow pivot + ECDSA/ECDH, or just append the v0.72-v0.81 narrative to `notes.md`. Worth doing before this session falls out of memory entirely. ~15 min.

**2. Demo 3.** Two natural candidates given the v0.65-v0.81 crypto stack:
   - **JWT-secured paste server** — POST text → server AES-256-GCM encrypts, gzip-compresses, stores; returns paste ID + ES256 JWT. GET with bearer token → verify, decompress, decrypt, return. Single demo that exercises real DEFLATE + AES-GCM + ECDSA JWT + http.createServer. Would showcase v0.66-v0.81 in anger.
   - **Live system monitor** — WebSocket pushes `os.cpus()` / `loadavg()` / `freemem()` every 1 s; browser renders bars. Visual. Validates v0.72's real os.* probes.

**3. Tackle the big remaining gap.** The `https.createServer` row is the last 🟡 in the README and the only thing standing between us and serving the demos over real TLS. Without OpenSSL it's a big lift — we'd need to wire ed25519/AES-GCM into a TLS 1.3 record layer, or vendor a minimal TLS in pure JS like `forge.tls`. Not a one-session task; probably 2-4 sessions. But high-impact if you want to ship `wss://` chat or HTTPS-served `npm-fetch` from PPC.

**4. Cross-project check-in.** Per CLAUDE.md you run parallel sessions on `golang-darwin8-ppc` / `ghc-darwin8-ppc`. They use the same per-session-dir convention. Might be worth a sweep to see if any need attention.

**5. v1.0 prep.** We're at v0.81. The runtime is feature-rich and stable on three arches. A `v1.0` release would be a forcing function for: a polished landing-page README, a `CHANGELOG.md`, an architecture doc, maybe a Hacker News post. Pure ceremony but useful if you want this project to be discoverable.

My honest pick: **#1, then #2-via-#3**. Updating the session notes is cheap and saves this work from getting lost. Then if you want a single concrete deliverable next time, picking up TLS as a multi-session arc lets every following demo we ship do so over `https://` / `wss://` — which is the real unlock for "serve from a G3 to a modern browser".

What's your steer?

repo + mozjs as\nrelease artifact + ibookg37 swap), two real demos, and ~270 legacy\n`/tmp` artifacts pulled into the repo.\n\n## Releases\n\n| Tag | Theme |\n|---|---|\n| [v0.66](release-notes/v0.66.md) | RSA encrypt/decrypt + PEM key import |\n| [v0.67](release-notes/v0.67.md) | `crypto.X509Certificate` via node-forge |\n| [v0.68](release-notes/v0.68.md) | Real DEFLATE compression via `/usr/bin/gzip` shell-out |\n| [v0.69](release-notes/v0.69.md) | `module.Module` class + JWT (RS256/EdDSA) validation smoke |\n| [v0.70](release-notes/v0.70.md) | Subpath module aliases (`fs/promises`, `stream/web`, `stream/promises`, `stream/consumers`, `path/posix`, `path/win32`) |\n| [v0.71](release-notes/v0.71.md) | `node:test` mocks + `cluster` stub + README accuracy pass |\n| [v0.72](release-notes/v0.72.md) | Real `os.cpus`/`hostname`/`loadavg`/`freemem`/`totalmem` via sysctl + vm_stat |\n| [v0.73](release-notes/v0.73.md) | Binary fetch fix (clear UTF-8-decode pending exception) + bundle mozjs tarballs |\n| [v0.74](release-notes/v0.74.md) | `Buffer.from(ArrayBuffer)` + typed array fix |\n| [v0.75](release-notes/v0.75.md) | ECDSA via vendored elliptic (P-256/384/521/secp256k1) |\n| [v0.76](release-notes/v0.76.md) | NIST ECDH \u2014 asymmetric crypto roster complete |\n| [v0.77](release-notes/v0.77.md) | Top-level `await` for entry-point scripts |\n| [v0.78](release-notes/v0.78.md) | `import.meta` + dynamic `import()` via Babel pre-rewrite |\n| [v0.79](release-notes/v0.79.md) | `crypto.subtle` ECDSA + ECDH |\n| [v0.80](release-notes/v0.80.md) | Real `process.stdin.setRawMode` (tcsetattr) + `TIOCGWINSZ` columns/rows |\n| [v0.81](release-notes/v0.81.md) | `crypto.subtle` EC JWK import/export |\n\nPer-arch build logs for each release in [`build-logs/`](build-logs/).\nCommit messages for v0.70+ in [`release-notes/`](release-notes/) as\n`v0.NN-msg.txt`.\n\n## Threads\n\n### v0.66\u2013v0.67 \u2014 RSA + X.509\n\nBuilt directly on session-X's v0.65 RSA-via-forge work. v0.66 wires\n`crypto.publicEncrypt(key, data)` / `privateDecrypt(key, data)` using\nforge's RSA-OAEP (default md SHA-1, override via `oaepHash`); also\nmakes `createPrivateKey` / `createPublicKey` route PEM strings through\n`forge.pki.{privateKeyFromPem,publicKeyFromPem}`. Bug found on first\nG3 run: `_coerceRsaKey` when given `{ key: KeyObject, oaepHash: ... }`\nfed the inner KeyObject back into `createPublicKey`, which had no\npassthrough for \"already-correct KeyObject\" \u2014 added explicit\npassthrough at the top of both `create*Key` functions.\n\nv0.67 wraps forge's `pki.certificateFromPem` / `certificateToAsn1` /\n`asn1.toDer` into Node's `X509Certificate` shape. All standard\nproperties + `checkIssued`/`checkPrivateKey`/`checkHost`/`verify`.\nTripped on first build because `_hexFp` referenced a top-level\n`createHash` that doesn't exist in the bootstrap scope \u2014 fixed by\nswitching to `new Hash(name)` directly.\n\n### v0.68 \u2014 real DEFLATE\n\nThrough v0.67, `zlib.gzipSync` / `deflateSync` produced **stored-mode**\n(BTYPE=00, uncompressed) blocks: valid framing, no compression. v0.68\nshells out to `/usr/bin/gzip` (always present on Tiger), then strips\nor re-wraps the gzip framing for the deflate / deflateRaw forms. 8 KB\nof `'a'` \u2192 **44 bytes**. 5 KB lipsum \u2192 **324 bytes**. `gunzip(1)`\naccepts our `gzipSync` output.\n\nBug on first run: the new `_gzipShell` called\n`require('child_process').spawnSync` \u2014 but inside the bootstrap\nclosure `require` isn't in scope; the local `child_process` and `fs`\nvars are. Switched to direct refs.\n\n### v0.69 \u2014 Module class + JWT validation\n\n`module.Module` class with `_cache` (mirrors `__require_cache__`),\n`_extensions`, `wrap(src)` / `wrapper`, plus static\n`Module.{builtinModules,isBuiltin,createRequire}`.\n\n`test/jwt_rs256_smoke.js`: end-to-end JWT validation that v0.65-v0.67's\nasymmetric crypto stack handles real-world JWT use cases. Manually\nconstructs + verifies tokens (no JWT library) for RS256, RS256 with\nPEM-imported keys, EdDSA (Ed25519), HS256, plus tamper rejection +\ncross-algorithm rejection.\n\n### v0.70 \u2014 subpath module aliases\n\nModern packages increasingly import via Node's official subpath\nspecifiers \u2014 `require('stream/web')`, `require('fs/promises')`, etc.\n\u2014 instead of reaching into the parent module's `.promises` property.\nSeeded `__require_cache__` for them.\n\nBug on first run: my smoke tried to drain a Node `Readable` via\n`consumers.buffer(nodeRs)` but the test process exited before the\nasync chain completed (the stream was paused, no fd listeners\nkeeping the loop alive). Switched all consumer tests to use WHATWG\n`ReadableStream` which has synchronous-completion behaviour.\n\n### v0.71 \u2014 node:test mocks + cluster stub + README accuracy\n\nTwo pieces. `t.mock.fn(impl?)` (spy with `.calls`/`.callCount()`/\n`.resetCalls()`/`.mockImplementation()`), `t.mock.method(obj, name)`\n(replaces, auto-restores), `t.mock.getter`/`setter`. Cluster\nsingle-process stub: `isMaster`/`isPrimary=true`, `fork()` throws.\n\nMid-release the user pinged about README staleness. Found the\n**Status** section still saying \"Pre-alpha. SpiderMonkey is being\nbuilt. Bridge source not yet linked/tested.\" for ~70 shipped\ntriad-built releases. **Scope limits** still claimed \"Sync only. No\nevent loop. No http/net/dns/child_process.\" Duplicate `dns \u274c\nMissing` row contradicting the working dns row. AsyncLocalStorage,\ndiagnostics_channel, EventTarget, BroadcastChannel all shipped in\nearlier sessions but never got their own README rows. Rewrote those\nsections + added the missing rows in the same v0.71 ship.\n\n### Workflow pivot (between v0.71 and v0.72)\n\nUser asked to consolidate the loose `docs/session-*-summary.md` files\ninto per-session directories matching the convention in sibling\nprojects (`golang-darwin8-ppc`, `ghc-darwin8-ppc`):\n\n    docs/sessions/<date>-session-<id>/\n        notes.md         (or summary.md for legacy sessions)\n        build-logs/      per-host build + smoke output\n        release-notes/   GitHub release prose copies\n\nMigrated 24 loose summaries into per-session dirs (legacy letter\nidentifiers preserved: `session-a`, `session-b`, ..., `session-x`;\nnew sessions use the within-date counter form `session-1`,\n`session-2`). `/tmp/triad-build.sh` moved to\n[`scripts/triad-build.sh`](../../../scripts/triad-build.sh) with\nper-arch host defaults baked in. `CLAUDE.md` documents the layout +\nnaming convention going forward.\n\nUser also asked to migrate `*.log`, `*.txt`, `*.md`, `*.sh` files\nfrom `/tmp` that originated from this project into the appropriate\nsession dirs. Wrote two migration scripts (saved here as\n[`scripts/migrate-legacy-tmp-artifacts.sh`](scripts/migrate-legacy-tmp-artifacts.sh)\nand [`scripts/migrate-triad-build-logs.sh`](scripts/migrate-triad-build-logs.sh))\nthat mapped 270+ artifacts to sessions by version.\n\nUser then asked to rename `examples/` (which I'd named for the chat +\nnpm-fetch demos) to `demos/` \u2014 turned out there was already a\n`demos/` directory with seven other demos. Consolidated.\n\n### v0.72 \u2014 real os.* probes\n\n`os.cpus()` was hardcoded to 'PowerPC G4' at 1000 MHz regardless of\nthe host. v0.72 wires the host-specific properties to real probes:\n- `cpus()` \u2192 `sysctl -n hw.cpusubtype hw.cpufrequency hw.ncpu`,\n  Mach-O subtype mapped to G3 (750) / G4 (7400/7450) / G5 (970)\n- `hostname()` \u2192 `/bin/hostname`\n- `loadavg()` \u2192 parse `/usr/bin/uptime`\n- `totalmem()` \u2192 `sysctl -n hw.memsize`\n- `freemem()` \u2192 `(Pages free + Pages speculative) * page size` from `/usr/bin/vm_stat`\n\nOn the new G3 host (ibookg37):\n- `cpus()` \u2192 `[{ model: 'PowerPC G3 (750)', speed: 900, ... }]`\n- `hostname()` \u2192 `'ibookg37.home'`\n- `loadavg()` \u2192 `[1.02, 0.82, 0.7]`\n- `totalmem()` \u2192 671088640 bytes (640 MB)\n- `freemem()` \u2192 102739968 bytes (98 MB)\n\n### Triad host swap: imacg3 \u2192 ibookg37\n\nUser asked to pivot from imacg3 (iMac G3, 600 MHz) to ibookg37 (iBook\nG3 PowerBook4,3, 900 MHz) for the G3 slot. Streamed the prebuilt\n`/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3/` from imacg3 across the local fleet:\n\n    ssh imacg3 'cd /opt && tar chf - mozjs-45-ionpower-g3' | \\\n        ssh ibookg37 'cd /opt && tar xpf -'\n\n(Note `-h`: dereference symlinks. First attempt without it brought\nbroken symlinks pointing into `/Users/macuser/tmp/tenfourfox-src/...`\non imacg3 that don't exist on ibookg37, breaking compile.)\n\nValidated by re-building v0.71 against ibookg37, then made the swap\npermanent via `scripts/triad-build.sh` defaults.\n[`v0.71-ibookg37-validate.log`](build-logs/v0.71-ibookg37-validate.log)\nis the pipeline-validation log.\n\n### v0.73 \u2014 binary fetch + mozjs tarballs\n\nUser flagged that consumers needed BOTH the runtime tarball AND a\nmatching SpiderMonkey install \u2014 undocumented and a download hassle.\nAdded one-time mozjs tarballs as v0.73 release artifacts (G3 90 MB,\nG4 66 MB, G5 66 MB), with future runtime releases linking back.\n\nIn passing, hit a real bug while validating demo 2 (npm-fetch):\n`fetch().arrayBuffer()` returned 0 bytes for any binary URL. The\nHTTP getSync C++ tried to UTF-8 decode every body to populate\n`r.body`; when that decode failed for binary content, it left a\npending JS exception on the SpiderMonkey context, which then caused\nthe subsequent `JS_DefineProperty(result, \"bodyBytes\", ...)` calls to\nfail. Fixed by `JS_ClearPendingException(cx)` after the failed\ndecode.\n\n### v0.74 \u2014 Buffer.from(ArrayBuffer) fix\n\nDemo 2 STILL failed end-to-end after v0.73's fetch fix. Traced to\nanother bug: `Buffer.from(ab)` returned 0 bytes for any ArrayBuffer.\nThe native fell through to the array-like branch, which reads\n`.length` \u2014 but ArrayBuffer has `.byteLength`. Patched `BufferFrom`\nto explicitly handle ArrayBuffer (via `JS_GetArrayBufferData`) and\nTypedArray (via `JS_GetArrayBufferViewData`). Sliced typed-array\nviews (`byteOffset > 0`) work correctly now.\n\nAfter v0.74, demo 2 lands: `mri@1.2.0` from `registry.npmjs.org`,\nfetched + gunzipped + untarred + required + exercised in **754 ms**\non ibookg37.\n\n### Demos shipped\n\n- [`demos/chat`](../../../demos/chat/) \u2014 multi-client WebSocket\n  chat. HTTP server on `:8080` serves the inline HTML; ws server on\n  `:8081`; multi-tab broadcast via EventEmitter; runtime banner\n  shows real CPU/host info from v0.72's os.* probes. Validated\n  end-to-end on ibookg37 with 3 simultaneous clients.\n- [`demos/npm-fetch`](../../../demos/npm-fetch/) \u2014 `npm install` via\n  the runtime: fetch from registry \u2192 gunzip \u2192 POSIX ustar parse \u2192\n  fs.writeFileSync \u2192 require + exercise. Takes ~750 ms for `mri` on\n  ibookg37.\n\n### v0.75 \u2014 ECDSA\n\nVendored `elliptic` (the standard JS ECC implementation, used by\njws/jwa/jsonwebtoken under the hood) plus its 6 deps (bn.js, brorand,\nhash.js, hmac-drbg, minimalistic-assert, minimalistic-crypto-utils).\nTotal 452 KB in `test/vendor/elliptic/`. Wired into our existing\n`crypto.{sign,verify,generateKeyPairSync}` API on `P-256` / `P-384` /\n`P-521` / `secp256k1`.\n\nPerformance on ibookg37: keygen ~100 ms, sign ~3 s, verify ~13 s.\nSlow because bn.js bignum isn't tuned for 32-bit PowerPC, but\nfunctionally correct.\n\n### v0.76 \u2014 NIST ECDH\n\n`crypto.diffieHellman({ privateKey, publicKey })` for two EC\nKeyObjects derives a shared secret. Closes the last \"Still missing\"\nitem in the asymmetric crypto roster.\n\n### v0.77 \u2014 Top-level `await`\n\nPre-detection scanner (brace-depth-tracking, comment + string-literal\nstripping) detects `await` at top level outside any `async function`\nbody and wraps the source in an async IIFE before handing it to\nBabel. Works for entry-point scripts; CJS modules can't synchronously\nexport a value computed via TLA (a hard limit of CJS).\n\nFirst trigger condition was wrong \u2014 SM45 reports the parse error as\n\"missing ; before statement\", not \"await is only valid\". Switched to\npre-detection (always wrap if TLA is detected) instead of catching\nBabel errors.\n\n### v0.78 \u2014 `import.meta` + dynamic `import()`\n\nCloses both remaining \"Missing\" CommonJS items. Both via regex\nsubstitutions in the Babel-on-parse-failure preprocessor:\n\n    import.meta.url       -> (\"file://\" + __filename)\n    import.meta.filename  -> __filename\n    import.meta.dirname   -> __dirname\n    import.meta            -> { url, filename, dirname }\n    import(spec)           -> __dynamic_import__(spec, require)\n\n`__dynamic_import__` is a new global wrapping `require` in a Promise\nthat returns `{ default: ... }` to match ESM dynamic-import shape.\n\n### v0.79 \u2014 `crypto.subtle` ECDSA + ECDH\n\nLifted v0.75/v0.76 ECDSA + ECDH into the WebCrypto subtle API for\nbrowser-style code. Added `_ecdsaDerToRaw` + `_ecdsaRawToDer` to\nconvert between Node's DER signatures and WebCrypto's raw `r \u2016 s`\n(left-padded, with proper non-negative DER encoding when the high\nbit is set).\n\n### v0.80 \u2014 real `setRawMode` + TIOCGWINSZ\n\n`process.stdin.setRawMode(true)` was a no-op stub. CLI prompt\nlibraries (inquirer, prompts) silently broke because they couldn't\nactually put the terminal in raw mode. Real implementation via two\nnew natives in `process.cpp`:\n- `process._setRawMode(fd, raw)` \u2014 `tcgetattr` + `tcsetattr` with\n  Node's flag set; saves the original termios on first raw call\n- `process._tty_size(fd)` \u2014 `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` for `{columns,rows}`\n\nStream constructors in `process.cpp` now query the real terminal\nsize at install time instead of reporting hardcoded 80\u00d724.\n\n### v0.81 \u2014 `crypto.subtle` EC JWK import/export\n\nFills the JWK shape that real-world JOSE / JWT libraries hand around:\n`{ kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256', x, y, d? }`. Round-trip: export, re-import,\nsign with re-imported private, verify with original public \u2014\nsucceeds. Plus raw uncompressed-point export (`0x04 || X || Y`) for\npublic keys.\n\nCloses the WebCrypto JWK story for EC keys.\n\n## Numbers at session end\n\n- 658+ third-party libraries with passing smokes (unchanged from\n  start of session; library hunt was deliberately deprioritized)\n- 1990+ assertions across 432 wired smoke files (up from 1772/414\n  at session start)\n- 16 tagged releases shipped to GitHub\n- All three \"Missing\" CJS items (top-level await, import.meta,\n  dynamic import) closed\n- Asymmetric crypto roster feature-complete on supported curves:\n  RSA + Ed25519 + X25519 + ECDSA + ECDH\n- README accuracy passes: ~12 stale rows updated, 4 missing rows\n  added, Status + Scope sections rewritten\n\n## Remaining gaps (for future sessions)\n\nPer the v0.81 README:\n\n- `https.createServer` \ud83d\udfe1 Partial \u2014 TLS without OpenSSL is the last\n  big piece. forge has a TLS 1.0/1.1 client+server impl that could\n  be wired into our `net.Socket`; a TLS 1.3 implementation would\n  need real work.\n- `Intl` \u274c \u2014 needs rebuilding mozjs with ICU support; out of scope\n  for the runtime layer.\n- Brotli compression \u2014 vendoring `brotli` is 1.5 MB; could vendor a\n  decoder-only impl to handle `Content-Encoding: br` responses.\n- `worker_threads.MessageChannel` / `MessagePort` \u2014 currently throws.\n- `http2` \u2014 major lift.\n"
}

Streamed the prebuilt\n`/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3/` from imacg3 across the local fleet:\n\n    ssh imacg3 'cd /opt && tar chf - mozjs-45-ionpower-g3' | \\\n        ssh ibookg37 'cd /opt && tar xpf -'\n\n(Note `-h`: dereference symlinks. First attempt without it brought\nbroken symlinks pointing into `/Users/macuser/tmp/tenfourfox-src/...`\non imacg3 that don't exist on ibookg37, breaking compile.)\n\nValidated by re-building v0.71 against ibookg37, then made the swap\npermanent via `scripts/triad-build.sh` defaults.\n[`v0.71-ibookg37-validate.log`](build-logs/v0.71-ibookg37-validate.log)\nis the pipeline-validation log.\n\n### v0.73 \u2014 binary fetch + mozjs tarballs\n\nUser flagged that consumers needed BOTH the runtime tarball AND a\nmatching SpiderMonkey install \u2014 undocumented and a download hassle.\nAdded one-time mozjs tarballs as v0.73 release artifacts (G3 90 MB,\nG4 66 MB, G5 66 MB), with future runtime releases linking back.\n\nIn passing, hit a real bug while validating demo 2 (npm-fetch):\n`fetch().arrayBuffer()` returned 0 bytes for any binary URL. The\nHTTP getSync C++ tried to UTF-8 decode every body to populate\n`r.body`; when that decode failed for binary content, it left a\npending JS exception on the SpiderMonkey context, which then caused\nthe subsequent `JS_DefineProperty(result, \"bodyBytes\", ...)` calls to\nfail. Fixed by `JS_ClearPendingException(cx)` after the failed\ndecode.\n\n### v0.74 \u2014 Buffer.from(ArrayBuffer) fix\n\nDemo 2 STILL failed end-to-end after v0.73's fetch fix. Traced to\nanother bug: `Buffer.from(ab)` returned 0 bytes for any ArrayBuffer.\nThe native fell through to the array-like branch, which reads\n`.length` \u2014 but ArrayBuffer has `.byteLength`. Patched `BufferFrom`\nto explicitly handle ArrayBuffer (via `JS_GetArrayBufferData`) and\nTypedArray (via `JS_GetArrayBufferViewData`). Sliced typed-array\nviews (`byteOffset > 0`) work correctly now.\n\nAfter v0.74, demo 2 lands: `mri@1.2.0` from `registry.npmjs.org`,\nfetched + gunzipped + untarred + required + exercised in **754 ms**\non ibookg37.\n\n### Demos shipped\n\n- [`demos/chat`](../../../demos/chat/) \u2014 multi-client WebSocket\n  chat. Validated\n  end-to-end on ibookg37 with 3 simultaneous clients.\n- [`demos/npm-fetch`](../../../demos/npm-fetch/) \u2014 `npm install` via\n  the runtime: fetch from registry \u2192 gunzip \u2192 POSIX ustar parse \u2192\n  fs.writeFileSync \u2192 require + exercise. Takes ~750 ms for `mri` on\n  ibookg37.\n\n### v0.75 \u2014 ECDSA\n\nVendored `elliptic` (the standard JS ECC implementation, used by\njws/jwa/jsonwebtoken under the hood) plus its 6 deps (bn.js, brorand,\nhash.js, hmac-drbg, minimalistic-assert, minimalistic-crypto-utils).\nTotal 452 KB in `test/vendor/elliptic/`. Wired into our existing\n`crypto.{sign,verify,generateKeyPairSync}` API on `P-256` / `P-384` /\n`P-521` / `secp256k1`.\n\nPerformance on ibookg37: keygen ~100 ms, sign ~3 s, verify ~13 s.\nSlow because bn.js bignum isn't tuned for 32-bit PowerPC, but\nfunctionally correct.\n\n### v0.76 \u2014 NIST ECDH\n\n`crypto.diffieHellman({ privateKey, publicKey })` for two EC\nKeyObjects derives a shared secret. Closes the last \"Still missing\"\nitem in the asymmetric crypto roster.\n\n### v0.77 \u2014 Top-level `await`\n\nPre-detection scanner (brace-depth-tracking, comment + string-literal\nstripping) detects `await` at top level outside any `async function`\nbody and wraps the source in an async IIFE before handing it to\nBabel. Works for entry-point scripts; CJS modules can't synchronously\nexport a value computed via TLA (a hard limit of CJS).\n\nFirst trigger condition was wrong \u2014 SM45 reports the parse error as\n\"missing ; before statement\", not \"await is only valid\". Switched to\npre-detection (always wrap if TLA is detected) instead of catching\nBabel errors.\n\n### v0.78 \u2014 `import.meta` + dynamic `import()`\n\nCloses both remaining \"Missing\" CommonJS items. Both via regex\nsubstitutions in the Babel-on-parse-failure preprocessor:\n\n    import.meta.url       -> (\"file://\" + __filename)\n    import.meta.filename  -> __filename\n    import.meta.dirname   -> __dirname\n    import.meta            -> { url, filename, dirname }\n    import(spec)           -> __dynamic_import__(spec, require)\n\n`__dynamic_import__` is a new global wrapping `require` in a Promise\nthat returns `{ default: ... }` to match ESM dynamic-import shape.\n\n### v0.79 \u2014 `crypto.subtle` ECDSA + ECDH\n\nLifted v0.75/v0.76 ECDSA + ECDH into the WebCrypto subtle API for\nbrowser-style code. }).then(function (b) {\n        banner.innerHTML = \"served by <b>\" + b.runtime + \"</b> on \" + b.host +\n            \" (\" + b.arch + \", \" + b.cpu + \")\";\n    }).catch(function () { banner.textContent = \"(banner unavailable)\"; });\n\n    post.addEventListener(\"click\", function () {\n        postOut.hidden = false;\n        postOut.className = \"muted\";\n        postOut.textContent = \"encrypting + signing...\";\n        fetch(\"/paste\", {\n            method:  \"POST\",\n            headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n            body:    JSON.stringify({ text: text.value })\n        }).then(function (r) { return r.json(); postOut.textContent = \"ERR: \" + e.message; });\n    });\n\n    get.addEventListener(\"click\", function () {\n        getOut.hidden = false;\n        getOut.className = \"muted\";\n        getOut.textContent = \"verifying + decrypting...\";\n        fetch(url.value, {\n            headers: { \"Authorization\": \"Bearer \" + token.value }\n        }).then(function (r) {\n            return r.json().then(function (j) { return { status: r.status, body: j };   "content": "# ionpower-node paste \u2014 JWT-secured encrypted paste server\n\nA single-file web app that exercises the v0.65\u2013v0.81 crypto + zlib +\nhttp stack end-to-end on PowerPC Tiger. Every paste goes through:\n\n```\nclient text\n   |\n   |  POST /paste { text }\n   v\n  AES-256-GCM encrypt  (96-bit IV, 128-bit tag)\n   |\n   v\n  zlib.gzipSync\n   |\n   v\n  fs.writeFileSync ./paste-store/<id>.bin\n   |\n   v\n  ECDSA P-256 sign  ->  ES256 JWT { id, exp: now+24h }\n   |\n   v\nclient gets { url, token }\n```\n\nRetrieving:\n\n```\nclient { url, token }\n   |\n   |  GET /paste/<id>  Authorization: Bearer <jwt>\n   v\n  crypto.verify(\"sha256\", data, pubKey, sigDer)   <- ES256 JWT check\n   |\n   v\n  fs.readFileSync ./paste-store/<id>.bin\n   |\n   v\n  zlib.gunzipSync\n   |\n   v\n  AES-256-GCM decrypt with auth-tag check\n   |\n   v\nclient gets plaintext\n```\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\nssh ibookg37 'cd /Users/macuser/tmp/ionpower-node && ./node demos/paste/server.js 8090'\n```\n\nThen open `http://ibookg37:8090/` in any modern browser. There's an\ninline form: paste text in the top textarea, click \"encrypt + sign +\nstore\", copy the resulting URL + token (or just hit the second\nbutton which pre-populates them) and watch the round-trip work.\n\n## What's exercised on the server\n\n| Phase | Subsystem | API |\n|---|---|---|\n| Request body | `http.createServer` + chunk reassembly | v0.66+ |\n| Encrypt | AES-256-GCM with 96-bit nonce + 128-bit auth tag | `crypto.createCipheriv` / `getAuthTag` |\n| Compress | Real DEFLATE via shell-out to `/usr/bin/gzip` | `zlib.gzipSync` (v0.68+) |\n| Persist | Recursive mkdir + write | `fs.mkdirSync({recursive:true})`, `fs.writeFileSync` |\n| Sign JWT | ECDSA P-256, SHA-256 hash | `crypto.sign(\"sha256\", data, ecPriv)` (v0.75+) |\n| Verify JWT | DER signature parse + ECDSA verify | `crypto.verify(...)` (v0.75+) |\n| Decompress | tiny-inflate | `zlib.gunzipSync` |\n| Decrypt | AES-256-GCM with auth-tag check | `crypto.createDecipheriv` / `setAuthTag` / `final()` |\n| Banner | Real CPU + host info | `os.cpus()`, `os.hostname()` (v0.72+) |\n\n## Ephemeral keys\n\nBoth secrets are generated at startup and never written to disk:\n\n- ECDSA P-256 keypair (the JWT signing key) \u2014 slow on G3 (~100 ms keygen, but signing each token is ~3 s, so this demo will feel noticeably more sluggish than chat)\n- 32-byte AES-256 master key (paste encryption key)\n\nRestart the server and all old tokens become invalid + all old\npastes become undecryptable. Intentional for a demo: no key\nmanagement story to explain.\n\n## Limitations\n\n- Single-process, single-key. Real production needs a KMS or key\n  rotation plan.\n- All paste-store files are encrypted with the same AES key, just\n  with per-paste IVs. Compromising the master key compromises every\n  paste. Production designs use per-paste keys derived from a master\n  via HKDF, but this is an end-to-end demo, not a security tutorial.\n- 200 KB request cap to keep AES-GCM final() fast on a 600 MHz G3.\n- Pastes never expire from disk; the JWT does (24 h) but the\n  storage doesn't get cleaned up. Add a `cron` if you care.\n"
}

  "content": "# TLS roadmap\n\nThe `https` row is the last \ud83d\udfe1 in the README. Everything else in the\nasync / crypto / streams / http stack is real, but `https.request`\nfalls back to a sync curl shim and `https.createServer` throws.\nThis doc is the multi-session plan to actually have TLS in-process.\n\n## Why this is the hardest remaining gap\n\nTLS is unique in the project because:\n\n1. **It's a state machine, not an algorithm.** Every other crypto\n   feature we've shipped (RSA encrypt, AES-GCM, ECDSA, JWT) is a\n   single-shot transform. TLS is a multi-round handshake with timing\n   dependencies + protocol-version + cipher-suite negotiation +\n   certificate-chain validation + record-layer framing.\n2. **The web is mostly TLS 1.2/1.3 now.** Modern CAs and CDNs\n   reject TLS 1.0/1.1. So a \"TLS 1.0 only\" implementation\n   functionally won't talk to most endpoints, even though it would\n   technically work.\n3. **The vendored option (forge.tls) is TLS 1.0/1.1 only.** Forge's\n   `lib/tls.js` was last meaningfully updated for 1.0 + 1.1 cipher\n   suites. It does not implement TLS 1.2's AEAD-cipher handshake\n   variations, and certainly not 1.3.\n4. **No native bridge.** OpenSSL on Tiger PPC is ancient (LibreSSL\n   forks aside). We don't have a C++ TLS we can shell into; the curl\n   shim is currently the only real TLS we touch, and that's a\n   fork+exec per request.\n\n## Three phases\n\n### Phase A (v0.82): forge.tls wired to net.Socket \u2014 minimum viable TLS\n\nGoal: a TLS 1.0/1.1 client + server that handshakes against itself,\nend-to-end. Not interop-with-modern-web; interop-with-our-own-stack.\n\nDeliverables:\n- `tls.createConnection(opts) -> tls.TLSSocket`: wraps `net.Socket`\n  and runs forge.tls handshake state machine on top.\n- `tls.createServer(opts, handler)`: same but accepts incoming.\n- Self-signed cert + ECDSA private key option, both PEM strings (we\n  already have v0.67's `X509Certificate`).\n- A smoke that round-trips a small payload between in-process\n  client + server, both running on the same G3.\n- README: `https` row stops being \ud83d\udfe1.\n\nWhat this **doesn't** unlock:\n- Our `https.request('https://npmjs.org/...')` still uses the curl\n  shim because forge.tls 1.0/1.1 won't negotiate with modern CDNs.\n- Browsers won't connect to `https://ibookg37:8090/` from `phase A`\n  because all current browsers reject TLS 1.0/1.1.\n\nBut it gets a real TLS handshake running on a 600 MHz G3, which\nis a meaningful proof that the pieces fit together. And gives us\nthe in-process TLS-record-layer plumbing that 1.2 / 1.3 will reuse.\n\nEstimated cost: 1 session.\n\n### Phase B (v0.83+): TLS 1.2 with ECDHE + AEAD cipher suites\n\nGoal: actually talk to modern endpoints. TLS 1.2 with the\n`ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384` / `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384`\ncipher suites is the floor most CDNs still accept (alongside 1.3).\n\nBuilding blocks already in place:\n- ECDHE: v0.76's `crypto.diffieHellman` on P-256/384/521.\n- ECDSA: v0.75 `crypto.sign('sha256', ..., ecPrivateKey)`.\n- AEAD ciphers: AES-GCM via `crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', ...)`.\n- HKDF: already in `crypto.hkdfSync` (Node-style) \u2014 needed for the\n  TLS 1.2 key schedule.\n- Certificate chain validation: v0.67's `X509Certificate.verify`\n  (delegates to `forge.pki.verifyCertificateChain`).\n\nMissing:\n- TLS 1.2 handshake state machine (different from 1.0/1.1's flow\n  in subtle ways: encrypted handshake on 1.2 means the cipher\n  install happens mid-handshake; transcript hashing differs).\n- `Certificate Verify` message generation + signing.\n- Proper `Finished` MAC with the 1.2 PRF (not the 1.0/1.1 one).\n\nThis is a multi-session arc. Probably 2-4 sessions of careful\nimplementation + testing against real public endpoints. The reward:\n`fetch('https://api.example.com/...')` runs entirely in-process\nwithout curl. Means we can write demos that talk to real web APIs\nfrom the G3 without forking out.\n\n### Phase C (v0.84+): TLS 1.3 \u2014 the long lift\n\nTLS 1.3 is a different beast. Single-round handshake, redesigned\nkey schedule (HKDF-Extract / HKDF-Expand-Label), encrypted\nextensions, separate cipher suites (`TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`),\n0-RTT. We have all the cryptographic primitives, but the state\nmachine is fully different from 1.2.\n\nPure-JS TLS 1.3 implementations exist (`tls13-js`, etc.) but they\ntarget Web environments with WebCrypto and don't have a Node-shape\nadaptor. Realistic plan:\n1. Take a pure-JS TLS 1.3 stack as a reference.\n2. Adapt the network I/O to our `net.Socket`.\n3. Wire the cipher hooks to our existing `crypto.subtle` (which\n   v0.79\u2013v0.81 made compatible with the WebCrypto shape these\n   implementations expect).\n\nThis is a 4-8 session arc.\n\n## Interim recommendation\n\nDon't block on TLS for general roadmap progress. Specifically:\n- Keep shipping demos over plain HTTP / WS for the time being.\n  The \"wait, that's running on a G3?\" punch lands either way.\n- For internet-fetch demos, the existing curl-shim path works fine\n  \u2014 it's a real TLS connection, just via fork+exec instead of\n  in-process. The npm-fetch demo proves this works.\n- When a Phase A session opens up, attack forge.tls 1.0 + a\n  self-signed cert smoke. Set the bar at \"smoke handshakes\n  end-to-end on the G3,\" not \"talks to npmjs.org over real TLS.\"\n\n## Quick sanity-checks before Phase A starts\n\n1. Does forge.tls's `createConnection` actually run on our SM45?\n   (We've vendored forge but haven't exercised the TLS path.)\n2. Does our `net.Socket` expose enough surface for forge.tls's\n   `socket` option to drive (read/write hooks)?\n3. Do we need to teach `forge.pki` about ECDSA certs (it's mostly\n   RSA today), or is RSA-only TLS 1.0 acceptable as a starting\n   point?\n"

## 👤 User

ok, are there any node test suites?

---

## 🤖 Claude

Yes — several, in rough order of "actually runnable against ionpower-node without much glue":

## 1. Web Platform Tests (WPT) — most feasible

The WHATWG Web Platform Tests corpus covers `URL`, `URLSearchParams`, `fetch`, `Streams`, `WebCrypto`, `TextEncoder/Decoder`, `Headers`, etc. — exactly the surface we've been polishing. Each test is a JS file with assertions; minimal runtime requirements (no v8 internals).

- Source: `web-platform-tests/wpt` on GitHub
- Subset relevant to us: `url/`, `streams/`, `WebCryptoAPI/`, `encoding/`, `FileAPI/`, `fetch/api/`
- Format: each test file calls `test(fn, name)` or `promise_test(fn, name)`. We'd need a ~50-line WPT-harness shim that maps those to our `node:test` or just an inline pass/fail counter.

This would give us a hard-numbered "X / Y WPT tests passing" metric for `URL`, `Streams`, `WebCrypto`. My best guess: we'd pass 70-90% of `url/` and `WebCryptoAPI/` (now that v0.79–v0.81 landed JWK), and somewhere in the 50-80% range on Streams.

## 2. Node.js's own test suite — partial feasibility

Node ships ~2000 tests under `test/parallel/` + `test/sequential/`. Each is a runnable script. The catches:

- `test/common/` is a 700-LOC test helper that uses some Node-internal stuff (`process.binding`, `--expose-internals`). We'd need to write a minimal `common.js` shim or skip tests that import it heavily.
- Tests for things we don't have (`http2`, `tls`, `vm` isolation, `worker_threads.MessageChannel`) will fail or hang. Need to filter.
- Some assume v8-specific output (e.g., the deprecation-warning message format).

A pragmatic slice that should mostly work: `test/parallel/test-buffer-*.js`, `test/parallel/test-path-*.js`, `test/parallel/test-querystring-*.js`, `test/parallel/test-url-*.js`, `test/parallel/test-events-*.js`, `test/parallel/test-stream-*.js`, `test/parallel/test-crypto-*.js`. That's ~600 tests.

This is the ground truth measurement. If we want a "% Node-compatible" headline number, this is where it comes from.

## 3. Test262 — JS engine conformance, less interesting

The JS-language conformance suite that all engines run against. SM45 already passes most of it (it's a 2017 release of SpiderMonkey, which was a top-tier engine). Running test262 would mostly measure SM45's compliance, not ionpower-node's.

Useful only if we want a baseline "what JS does our underlying engine support" number. Not what you're after.

## 4. Individual library test suites

A lot of vendored libraries have their own tests bundled. Our `test/vendor/elliptic/` has `node_modules/hash.js/test/`, `node_modules/hmac-drbg/test/` etc. — testing the library, not the runtime. Useful as a sanity check that our runtime doesn't break the libraries; not useful as a runtime conformance measure.

---

## What I'd recommend

If the goal is **a publishable conformance number**:
- Pick WPT first. Smaller corpus, well-defined harness, clean numbers. "ionpower-node passes 1247 / 1583 WPT tests in `url/` + `streams/` + `WebCryptoAPI/`" reads great in a README.

If the goal is **find-and-fix bugs**:
- Pick Node.js's `test/parallel/test-{buffer,path,querystring,url,events,stream,crypto}-*.js`. Real bug-finding signal — most of those tests poke edge cases that vendored libraries don't.

Either is a 1-2 session project to set up the harness + run the corpus + classify failures. Want me to scope one of these in more detail?
