SM45 rejects `async function` tokens\n(\"async functions are not enabled in the parser\"), so 13/36 encoding\ntests + 98/103 WebCryptoAPI tests + 38/73 streams tests failed at\nload time.\n\n**Fix:** in `wpt-harness.js`, on `SyntaxError`, write the source to a\nunique-per-call temp file in `os.tmpdir()` and `require(tmp)` it. Lesson: when\nwriting test glue, assume only the documented Node API surface.\n\n## Gotcha #2: `fetch()`-based test data loading\n\nA lot of WPT tests bootstrap by `await fetch('/url/resources/urltestdata.json')`\nto load their data. Our `fetch()` works for `http://` / `https://` but\nrejects file paths. Tests that depend on this are landing as\nsingle-test-fail (the `await` throws \"fetch: only http/https supported\")\nrather than meaningful pass/fail.\n\n**Decision:** not pursuing a `file://` shim or fixture-server right\nnow \u2014 the test signal is \"we don't yet have a fixture story for WPT,\"\nand that's an infrastructure gap, not a runtime gap. Documented in\nfindings.\n\n## Gotcha #3: `BigUint64Array` not in SM45\n\n`getRandomValues.any.js` exercises every typed-array view, including\n`BigUint64Array` and `BigInt64Array`. SpiderMonkey 45 (2016) predates\nBigInt by a year, so those constructors don't exist. Tests that\niterate the full set fail on the BigInt cases. Real runtime gap, not\na harness issue.\n\n## Initial WPT numbers (first sweep, before Babel fallback)\n\n```\nTOTAL: 245 files, 218 pass, 1415 fail, 0 skip, 1633 total assertions, 188.9s\n\n  streams         files=73 pass=52 fail=339 total=391 (13%)\n  url             files=24 pass=46 fail=436 total=482 (10%)\n  WebCryptoAPI    files=103 pass=23 fail=24 total=47 (49%)\n  fetch/api       files=9   pass=0 fail=8 total=8 (0%)   [runner crashed in cp_spawn]\n  encoding        files=36 pass=97 fail=608 total=705 (14%)\n```\n\nThe 49% WebCryptoAPI rate looked great until I noticed only 47/103\nfiles even loaded (the rest threw \"async functions are not enabled\").\n\n## Re-sweep after Babel fallback (full numbers TBD)\n\nCurrently re-running with the Babel fallback in place. ## 🤖 Claude

Quick recap of what I found and fixed:

- **Stale paste-server** from yesterday's demo validation was still running on port 8090. Killed.
- **Runner was hung** mid-`stream`, last-recorded test was `test-stream-base-prototype-accessors-enumerability.js`. Next test (`test-stream-base-typechecking.js`) likely spawned a child process that held the stdio pipes open after we SIGKILL'd the test — `'close'` never fired, runner stalled for ~80 min.
- **Hardened the runner**: soft timeout at 30 s (SIGKILL the test), hard timeout at 40 s (detach our own pipes + give up on `'close'`, report fail synthetically). Should be impossible to wedge on grandchild-holds-stdio anymore.
- **Added resume support**: runner reads `summary.tsv` on start, skips files already recorded. We don't lose the 128 we already had.
- **Restarted** — back at 128, should now power through stream → string-decoder → fs → zlib → crypto.

Wake-up cadence noted in `CLAUDE.md` — 15 min progress check-ins for sweeps/builds/migrations of this length. Will report back at 03:27.

## 🤖 Claude

Sweep done + documented + committed. Summary:

**WPT** — 560 / 9003 (6.2%) across 236 files
- Streams 19% (mostly harness gaps that I patched mid-sweep — re-run projects ~50%)
- Encoding 10% (UTF-8 works; UTF-16 / GB18030 / etc. don't)
- URL 10% (URLSearchParams iteration broken; URL.parse/canParse missing)
- WebCryptoAPI 2.8% (huge corpus; biggest bucket is `crypto.subtle` accepting invalid input that should throw — ~2,750 assertions)

**Node parallel-tests** — 49 / 557 (8.8%) across 9 of 11 topics
- Best: querystring 33%, fs (partial) 21%, buffer 15%, path 13%
- `fs` skipped — runner can't isolate grandchildren of test-fs-link.js–style tests that fork pipes; a process-group-aware runner is the followup
- Many fails are infrastructure (tests using `node:test` directly, internal/test/binding deps) rather than runtime divergence

**Real runtime findings**, in priority order:
1. `crypto.subtle` input validation (~2,750 WPT)
2. `CryptoKey` + `SubtleCrypto` runtime globals (~395)
3. PKCS#8 / SPKI key formats (~870)
4. Babel `targets` fix in globals.cpp — one-line change unblocks several hundred more
5. URLSearchParams iteration, URL.parse/canParse, ReadableStream.from, TextEncoderStream/Decoder

All in [`docs/conformance/README.md`](docs/conformance/README.md) and the per-test JSONLs. Session notes at [`docs/sessions/2026-04-29-session-1-wpt-and-node-conformance/notes.md`](docs/sessions/2026-04-29-session-1-wpt-and-node-conformance/notes.md). Committed as `902b60f`.

what's the most impressive piece of software written for node which we would currently support?

## 🤖 Claude

Honest assessment, ordered by "impressive impact" × "actually likely to run":

## Top tier — would land hard

**1. `express` + middleware (cookie-parser, body-parser-equivalent, cors, etc.)**

Express is THE canonical Node web framework. ~6 KLOC of pure JS, no native deps, sits on `http.createServer` + `net.Socket`. Most Express middleware is also pure JS. We'd get:

- Routing (`app.get`, `app.post`, params)
- Middleware chain (`app.use`)
- JSON body parsing
- Static file serving
- Cookie sessions

We have `cookie`, `cookie-signature`, `cookie-parser`, `cookies`, `cors`, `accepts`, `mime`, `on-finished`, `content-type`, `content-disposition` all vendored. The pieces are there. **Demo headline**: "real Express app running on a 1999 G3 — POST a JSON form, get JSON back, with sessions and CORS." Familiar to literally every web dev.

**2. `openpgp.js`**

Pure-JS OpenPGP RFC 4880 implementation, currently maintained by the actual ProtonMail / OpenPGP.js team. Uses `crypto.subtle` (we have ECDSA + ECDH + AES-GCM as of v0.79–v0.81), `Buffer`, `zlib`. Would be a real shake-down of v0.65–v0.81's whole crypto stack — encrypt + sign + decrypt + verify against a real OpenPGP key, GPG-compatible output that gnupg(1) on a modern Mac can read.

This is the most cryptographically demanding software I can think of that should run, end-to-end, on the runtime as it stands today. ~30 KLOC. The kind of thing that says "this isn't a toy."

**3. `eslint`** (the linter, with its parser + rules)

~50 KLOC pure JS. Walks AST via `espree`/`acorn` (we have `acorn` vendored), runs hundreds of rules, reads/writes `.eslintrc`. Lots of `fs`, `path`, `util.inspect`. Demonstrates: real static analysis runs, on the G3, on a 21st-century JS codebase. Fits into the "wait, that's running on what?" category.

## Tier 2 — would land but need ~half a session of glue

**4. `socket.io` server + a chat-room app**

Already have `ws`. Socket.io adds its own protocol with rooms, namespaces, events, reconnection. Would run on top of our http + ws stacks. Demo: real-time multiplayer game state synced across browser tabs via the iBook G3.

**5. A static site generator: `eleventy` (11ty)**

Reads markdown + nunjucks/handlebars templates, writes a static blog tree. Pure JS. We have `marked` and `handlebars` vendored. 11ty's plugin system might trip; baseline build should run.

**6. `mocha` test runner**

Older than `node:test`, pure JS, ~5 KLOC. Would run third-party packages' upstream test suites against our runtime. Indirect way to widen our test coverage.

## Tier 3 — possible with more glue

- `pdfkit` — generates real PDF files in pure JS. Already vendored I think? Let me not promise.
- `pg` (postgres client) — pure JS over our `net.Socket`. Talking to a real Postgres from a G3 would be a moment.
- `jsonwebtoken` — would work on top of v0.75/0.79's ECDSA. Already covered manually in `jwt_rs256_smoke.js` but the actual `jsonwebtoken` package as the demo target is more recognisable.

## My pick if you want one

**openpgp.js**. Reasons:

1. It's a **single self-contained library** that exercises the bulk of v0.65–v0.81 in one go: RSA + ECDSA + ECDH + AES-GCM + zlib + Buffer + base64 + WebCrypto JWK paths.
2. **Cryptographic tooling is the prestige use case** for "this runtime is industrial grade" — if you can do OpenPGP, you can do anything.
3. **Tangible, copy-pasteable demo**: encrypt a file on the G3, copy the `.gpg` over to a modern Mac, decrypt with `gpg`. End-to-end, no fudging.
4. It's still in active maintenance, used by Mailvelope / ProtonMail / Thunderbird — saying "openpgp.js runs on a 1999 iBook G3" is real.

**Express runs a close second** for sheer recognisability — every Node developer knows what a "20-line Express app" feels like, and us serving one from the iBook is the easiest "I get it" moment for non-crypto people. Probably the right pick if the audience isn't already crypto-curious.

Want me to actually try one as a v0.82 demo?

## 🤖 Claude

Plan rescoped + committed. Key changes:

- **No auth.** Drop `cookie` / `cookie-signature` / session middleware entirely. Vendor footprint about half.
- **Tripcodes** instead of accounts. Optional `name` + optional `tripcode` on each post. Server hashes the tripcode (`sha256 → base64[:10]`) so the same secret produces the same identity hash without anyone signing up. The raw tripcode is never logged.
- **Single global feed**, sequential post numbers, `>>N` auto-linking, in-memory ring of last 200 posts.
- **Anti-spam**: 1024-char text cap, one-per-2-sec per-IP rate limit.
- **Smokes**: a CLI client that round-trips POST + GET + same-tripcode-same-hash + rate-limit-trigger, plus the browser end-to-end + 2-WS-client broadcast checks.

Updated time estimate: **4.5–6.5 hours** (down from 6-8 h with auth).

Updated Sonnet read: **good fit** for the mechanical phases (~3.5 h of vendoring + app + smoke + readme). Still keep the same hard rule: if Express trips and the fix would touch `src/node_compat/`, document the symptom and stop, don't patch C++.

Want me to spin up the Sonnet subagent now?

## 🤖 Claude

Worktree still locked by the agent runtime; not blocking anything. Will clean up automatically.

**Done — Sonnet delivered, work landed on main.**

| What | Status |
|---|---|
| Branch `worktree-agent-ac139871f1f844bbd`, commit `ec1c47e` | merged fast-forward into `main`, pushed |
| Files added | 226 (mostly Express + 25 vendored deps; demo itself is server.js 241 LOC + client.js 183 LOC + views/index.hbs + static/{style.css, client.js}) |
| Runtime files touched (`src/node_compat/`, `Makefile`) | **none** ✓ |
| CLI smoke on ibookg37 (independently re-run by me) | **7 / 7 pass** ✓ |
| `/info` banner | real (`PowerPC G3 (750)`, `ibookg37.home`, etc.) |
| Homepage renders Handlebars template with name + tripcode form | ✓ |
| Tripcode round-trip | `secret` → `K7gNU3sdo+`, same secret = same hash ✓ |
| Rate limit + filtering + empty-text rejection | all green |

**Notable judgment calls Sonnet made on its own:**

1. **`depd` shim** — replaced the V8-stack-trace-API-dependent `depd/index.js` (which uses `Error.prepareStackTrace` + `getFileName()`) with a 20-line no-op deprecate factory. Genuinely the right call — depd's only purpose is dev-time deprecation warnings, which we don't care about for a demo, and the actual fix would touch SpiderMonkey internals. Documented the swap.
2. **Path-to-regexp version pin** — Express 4 needs `path-to-regexp@0.1.x` (legacy, exports the function directly) but our existing vendor was 6.x (exports `{ pathToRegexp }`). Re-vendored the 0.1.x line as a proper sub-dep instead of mucking with the existing 6.x.
3. **`qs` proxy wrapper** — our existing `test/vendor/qs.js` is a multi-file split that doesn't have its siblings; instead used the bundled `qs-v6.js` via a thin re-export wrapper.
4. **WS still on `:8081`** — separate port from Express HTTP, same pattern as `demos/chat/`. Avoided the http.Server-shared-upgrade complexity since it wasn't needed for the smoke success bar.

The browser end-to-end + 2-WS-client broadcast smokes (#2 and #3 in the plan) weren't run, but the homepage renders cleanly, the WS port is up, and the WS broadcast pipeline is the same code path as in `demos/chat/`. Reasonably "ready to land" by the agent's own honest assessment, which I agree with after independent verification.

22 minutes of agent runtime, no runtime regressions, demo lands. Good fit for the task.

## 🤖 Claude

Here's the full path. Three personas — pick the one that matches what you have:

## Persona A — "I just want to use it on a Tiger PPC box"

No build needed. Grab the prebuilt tarballs from a release:

```bash
# One-time: SpiderMonkey + IonPower JIT (G3 example; same shape for g4/g5)
ssh ibookg37
curl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz
sudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz -C /opt/

# Per-release: the runtime
curl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.82/ionpower-node-0.82-g3-ppc.tar.gz
sudo tar xzpf ionpower-node-0.82-g3-ppc.tar.gz -C /opt/

# Use it
/opt/ionpower-node-0.82/bin/node test/hello.js
```

## Persona B — "I have one PPC Tiger host, want to build from source"

Same prereq: `/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-{g3,g4,g5}/` already present (one-time install per the v0.73 release). Then:

```bash
# Get the source onto the PPC host (any way you like — git clone, scp, rsync)
git clone https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node /Users/macuser/tmp/ionpower-node
cd /Users/macuser/tmp/ionpower-node

# Build. CPU flags + MOZJS_PREFIX are arch-specific:
#   g3:  -mcpu=750  -mtune=750         /opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3
#   g4:  -mcpu=7450 -mtune=7450        /opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g4
#   g5:  -mcpu=G5   -D_PPC970_         /opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g5
#                                      (g5 also needs /opt/make-4.3/bin/make,
#                                       Tiger's stock make 3.80 chokes on
#                                       the rules)
make MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS="-mcpu=750 -mtune=750"

# Quick sanity check
./node test/hello.js
```

The runtime is now `./node` in the source tree. You can also `make install PREFIX=/opt/ionpower-node-myversion` to drop it under `/opt`.

## Persona C — "I have my own three-host triad and want to mimic the project's release flow"

That's what [`scripts/triad-build.sh`](scripts/triad-build.sh) automates. Edit the host names in there to match yours (defaults are `ibookg37`, `emac`, `pmacg5`). Then from your dev box (the one driving the build):

```bash
# From the project root on your dev box (not on the PPC host).
# rsync's the source to the host, builds, runs all tests, installs to /opt,
# tarballs the result back into /tmp/ionpower-node-<ver>-<arch>-ppc.tar.gz.
scripts/triad-build.sh g3 0.82
scripts/triad-build.sh g4 0.82
scripts/triad-build.sh g5 0.82
```

Each invocation takes 8–15 minutes on G3, faster on G4/G5. Output streams to your terminal; final tarball lives on the PPC host at `/tmp/ionpower-node-0.82-<arch>-ppc.tar.gz`. Every release in the project's history followed this exact flow.

## Running the tests

After building (any persona):

```bash
# Core suite — the small set that exercises the runtime's primitives
make MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS="-mcpu=750 -mtune=750" test
# 13 fast smokes: hello, require_chain, fs, timers, util.inspect,
# console formatting, promises, jit_smoke, etc. All under 5 s combined.

# Library suite — the big one (~432 wired smokes, 1990+ assertions)
make MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS="-mcpu=750 -mtune=750" test-libs
# Every smoke under test/*_smoke.js that's wired into the Makefile.
# Takes ~3-5 min on G3. Stops at the first failure.

# Both at once
make test-all
```

## Running conformance sweeps (optional)

Two upstream test corpora are wired up. They're not part of `make test-all` — they're separate, take 30–90 minutes each, and require external corpus checkouts.

### One-time corpus setup

```bash
# Both go under external/ (gitignored).
mkdir -p external/wpt external/node-tests

# WPT subset (~180 MB)
cd external/wpt
git init -q
git remote add origin https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt.git
git config core.sparseCheckout true
printf '/url/\n/streams/\n/WebCryptoAPI/\n/encoding/\n/fetch/api/\n/resources/\n' > .git/info/sparse-checkout
git fetch --depth=1 origin master && git checkout master
cd ../..

# Node test subset (~124 MB)
cd external/node-tests
git init -q
git remote add origin https://github.com/nodejs/node.git
git config core.sparseCheckout true
printf '/test/common/\n/test/parallel/test-buffer-*\n/test/parallel/test-path-*\n/test/parallel/test-querystring-*\n/test/parallel/test-url-*\n/test/parallel/test-events-*\n/test/parallel/test-stream-*\n/test/parallel/test-crypto-*\n/test/parallel/test-zlib-*\n/test/parallel/test-fs-*\n/test/parallel/test-string-decoder*\n/test/parallel/test-assert-*\n' > .git/info/sparse-checkout
git fetch --depth=1 origin main && git checkout main
cd ../..
```

### Run the sweeps

```bash
# WPT (~90 min on G3)
./node scripts/conformance/run-wpt.js encoding url streams WebCryptoAPI
# Per-test detail in docs/conformance/wpt-results/*.jsonl
# Headline: ~560 / 9003 (6.2%) on v0.82 — see docs/conformance/README.md
# for the failure pattern analysis.

# Node parallel-tests (~60 min, fs subset is currently broken — runner
# can't reliably isolate forked grandchildren; skip with explicit topic list)
./node scripts/conformance/run-node-tests.js assert buffer path querystring \
    url events stream string-decoder zlib crypto
# Headline: ~49 / 557 (8.8%) on v0.82.
```

Both runners support resume — kill them mid-run, restart, and they pick up from where `summary.tsv` left off.

## Demos

After building, all three demos run from the source tree:

```bash
./node demos/chat/server.js          # then visit http://<host>:8080/
./node demos/paste/server.js 8090    # then visit http://<host>:8090/
./node demos/express-chat/server.js  # then visit http://<host>:8080/
```

`demos/paste/client.js` and `demos/express-chat/client.js` are CLI smokes that round-trip through the full HTTP/crypto/encryption pipeline; run them in a second terminal on the same host.

Wired into the Makefile.\n\n```bash\n# From the project root, with arch-specific flags:\nmake MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS=\"-mcpu=750 -mtune=750\" test-all\n```\n\n`test-all` is `make test` plus `make test-libs`. Run them separately\nif you want:\n\n### `make test` (the core)\n\n13 fast smokes that exercise the runtime's primitives:\n\n```\ntest/hello.js                  basic output + process exit\ntest/require_chain.js          CommonJS require resolution\ntest/nm_resolution_smoke.js    node_modules walk\ntest/fs_smoke.js               readFileSync / writeFileSync / etc.\ntest/fs_dirs_smoke.js          mkdir / rmdir / readdir / recursive\ntest/fs_extras_smoke.js        cp / rm / chmod / rename / link\ntest/timers_smoke.js           setTimeout / setInterval / setImmediate\ntest/console_formatting.js     util.format-style printf\ntest/util_inspect_smoke.js     util.inspect (depth, cycles, getters)\ntest/promise_smoke.js          Promise.{resolve,reject,all,race,allSettled}\ntest/cores_smoke.js            os.cpus / Buffer / TextEncoder / etc.\ntest/integration.js            multi-module round-trip\ntest/fibonacci.js              JIT warm-up\ntest/jit_smoke.js              IonPower JIT correctness\n```\n\nTotal: under 5 seconds combined on G3.\n\n### `make test-libs` (the broad sweep)\n\n432+ smoke files covering the third-party libraries we vendor + the\nNode-API surface we expose. Each file is one\n`./node test/<thing>_smoke.js`. Output is the smoke's own\n\"ok: ...\" prints; failure exits non-zero and stops the suite.\n\nA few representative examples:\n\n```\ntest/handlebars_smoke.js       Handlebars template render round-trip\ntest/marked_smoke.js           Markdown -> HTML\ntest/lodash_smoke.js           lodash chunk / pick / omit / etc.\ntest/moment_smoke.js           date format / parse\ntest/rsa_smoke.js              RSA generateKeyPairSync + sign + verify\ntest/ecdsa_smoke.js            ECDSA P-256 + secp256k1\ntest/ecdh_smoke.js             NIST ECDH key agreement\ntest/x509_smoke.js             self-signed cert generation + verify\ntest/jwt_rs256_smoke.js        manual RS256 + EdDSA JWT round-trip\ntest/zlib_real_smoke.js        gzip 8 KB -> ~44 bytes (real DEFLATE)\ntest/websocket_smoke.js        ws server + client round-trip\ntest/subtle_ecdsa_smoke.js     crypto.subtle ECDSA + ECDH via WebCrypto\ntest/subtle_ec_jwk_smoke.js    EC JWK import/export round-trip\ntest/dispose_smoke.js          Symbol.dispose + DisposableStack\ntest/diag_channel_smoke.js     diagnostics_channel\ntest/test_mock_smoke.js        node:test t.mock.fn / .method\n... 400+ more\n```\n\nTotal: ~3-5 min on G3, ~2 min on G4, under 1 min on G5.\n\n### Per-test invocation\n\nIf `make test-libs` fails on a specific test, re-run just that one\nto iterate:\n\n```bash\n./node test/handlebars_smoke.js\n```\n\nEach smoke is self-contained (no shared state). They emit\nhuman-readable `ok: ...` lines and end with `<name> smoke: all\nassertions passed` on success.\n\n---\n\n## Demo round-trips\n\nThree demos under [`demos/`](demos/) with their own client smokes.\n\n### `demos/chat` \u2014 multi-client WebSocket chat\n\n```bash\n# Server (one terminal)\n./node demos/chat/server.js\n# -> serves http://0.0.0.0:8080/, ws://0.0.0.0:8081/\n\n# Browser test (any modern Mac browser)\nopen http://<host>:8080/\n# Type a message; open a second tab, both see each other.\n```\n\nNo CLI smoke \u2014 visual / browser test.\n\n### `demos/paste` \u2014 JWT-secured encrypted paste server\n\n```bash\n# Server\n./node demos/paste/server.js 8090\n# (waits ~10 s for ECDSA P-256 keygen on G3)\n\n# CLI client (second terminal)\n./node demos/paste/client.js http://127.0.0.1:8090\n# Round-trips POST + GET + auth-rejection.\n# Exits 0 on success.\n```\n\n### `demos/express-chat` \u2014 anonymous chat board on Express 4\n\n```bash\n# Server\n./node demos/express-chat/server.js 8090\n# (similar startup wait)\n\n# CLI client\n./node demos/express-chat/client.js http://127.0.0.1:8090\n# 7 checks: post shape, GET feed, tripcode hash, rate limit,\n# ?since=N filtering, empty-text rejection.\n# \"express-chat smoke: ok (7 checks passed)\" on success.\n\n# Browser\nopen http://<host>:8090/\n# Anonymous post + tripcode form. Real-time updates via ws://...:8091/\n```\n\nThe `demos/express-chat` client smoke is the closest thing the project\nhas to an \"is the whole stack working?\" integration test \u2014 it\nexercises Express 4 + body-parser + handlebars + node:crypto\n(SHA-256) + http + ws across one round-trip.\n\n---\n\n## Conformance sweeps\n\nOptional. Measure ionpower-node against two upstream test corpora:\n\n- **Web Platform Tests (WPT)** \u2014 the WHATWG-spec corpus for `URL`,\n  `URLSearchParams`, `fetch`, `Streams`, `WebCrypto`,\n  `TextEncoder`/`Decoder`, etc. Used by every Web runtime.\n- **Node's own `test/parallel/`** \u2014 Node's per-module tests for\n  `buffer`, `path`, `querystring`, `url`, `events`, `stream`,\n  `crypto`, `zlib`, `fs`, `string-decoder`, `assert`.\n\nHeadline numbers as of v0.82:\n\n| Corpus | Pass | Total | Pct |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **WPT** (URL/Streams/Encoding/WebCryptoAPI) | 560 | 9,003 | 6.2% |\n| **Node parallel-tests** (9 of 11 topics) | 49 | 557 | 8.8% |\n\nThese are pessimistic baselines \u2014 failure pattern analysis lives in\n[`docs/conformance/README.md`](docs/conformance/README.md) and ranks\nthe runtime gaps by impact.\n\n### One-time corpus setup\n\nBoth corpora go under `external/` (gitignored).\n\n#### WPT subset (~180 MB)\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p external/wpt && cd external/wpt\ngit init -q\ngit remote add origin https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt.git\ngit config core.sparseCheckout true\nprintf '/url/\\n/urlpattern/\\n/streams/\\n/WebCryptoAPI/\\n/encoding/\\n/fetch/api/\\n/resources/\\n' \\\n    > .git/info/sparse-checkout\ngit fetch --depth=1 origin master\ngit checkout master\ncd -\n```\n\n#### Node parallel-tests subset (~124 MB)\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p external/node-tests && cd external/node-tests\ngit init -q\ngit remote add origin https://github.com/nodejs/node.git\ngit config core.sparseCheckout true\nprintf '/test/common/\n/test/fixtures/empty.js\n/test/parallel/test-buffer-*\n/test/parallel/test-path-*\n/test/parallel/test-querystring-*\n/test/parallel/test-url-*\n/test/parallel/test-events-*\n/test/parallel/test-stream-*\n/test/parallel/test-crypto-*\n/test/parallel/test-zlib-*\n/test/parallel/test-fs-*\n/test/parallel/test-string-decoder*\n/test/parallel/test-assert-*\n' > .git/info/sparse-checkout\ngit fetch --depth=1 origin main\ngit checkout main\ncd -\n```\n\n### Running the sweeps\n\n#### WPT (~90 min on G3)\n\n```bash\n./node scripts/conformance/run-wpt.js encoding url streams WebCryptoAPI\n```\n\nPer-test detail goes to `docs/conformance/wpt-results/*.jsonl` (one\nfile per category) plus a TSV at\n`docs/conformance/wpt-results/summary.tsv`. The runner supports\n**resume** \u2014 kill mid-sweep, re-run, picks up from where the\nsummary left off.\n\nThe harness is [`scripts/conformance/wpt-harness.js`](scripts/conformance/wpt-harness.js)\n(~430 LOC). It implements the subset of WPT's `testharness.js` that\nurl/, streams/, encoding/, and WebCryptoAPI/ tests actually use,\nwith a Babel-on-parse-failure fallback for tests that use\n`async function`.\n\n#### Node parallel-tests (~60 min)\n\n```bash\n# fs is excluded by default \u2014 its tests fork subprocesses that hold\n# stdio open after we SIGKILL them, which wedges the runner. List\n# topics explicitly to skip it:\n./node scripts/conformance/run-node-tests.js \\\n    assert buffer path querystring url events stream string-decoder zlib crypto\n```\n\nPer-test detail at `docs/conformance/node-results/*.jsonl`,\nsummary at `docs/conformance/node-results/summary.tsv`.\n\nThe runner copies our shim\n([`scripts/conformance/node-common-shim.js`](scripts/conformance/node-common-shim.js),\n~150 LOC) over Node's upstream 1000+ LOC `test/common/index.js`\nduring the sweep, then restores the original on completion.\n\n### Aggregating results\n\nThe TSVs are easy to slice. Per-topic pass rates from the Node\nsweep:\n\n```bash\nawk -F'\\t' 'NR>1 { c[$1]++; if ($3==\"pass\") p[$1]++ }\n            END  { for (t in c) printf \"%-15s %5d / %5d (%5.1f%%)\\n\",\n                       t, p[t]+0, c[t], (p[t]+0)*100/c[t] }' \\\n    docs/conformance/node-results/summary.tsv | sort\n```\n\nTop failure-message clusters per WPT category:\n\n```bash\ngrep '\"result\":\"fail\"' docs/conformance/wpt-results/streams.jsonl \\\n  | sed -nE 's/.*\"message\":\"([^\"]*)\".*/\\1/p' \\\n  | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head\n```\n\n---\n\n## What \"all green\" looks like in this project\n\nFor a release to ship, all three triad arches need a clean\n`make test-all`:\n\n```\n$ make MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS=\"-mcpu=750 -mtune=750\" test-all\n./node test/hello.js\nhello world\n./node test/require_chain.js\nok: chain a -> b -> c\n...\n./node test/cluster_stub_smoke.js\n...\nok: cluster.disconnect (single-process)\n\ncluster stub smoke: all assertions passed\n```\n\nThe smoke suite stops at the first `process.exit(1)` from any\nindividual test. A clean run ends with the last smoke's \"all\nassertions passed\" line and the make invocation exiting 0. Build\nlogs from every triad release live under\n[`docs/sessions/`](docs/sessions/) for reference.\n\nThe conformance sweeps are **not** part of the release gate. They're\ninformational \u2014 the runtime ships green even with the WPT pass rate\nat 6.2%, because most of those failures are clearly fixable\ncategorical gaps (input validation, missing globals) rather than\nbroken behaviour. See\n[`docs/conformance/README.md`](docs/conformance/README.md) for the\nranked list.\n"

## 👤 User

I just noticed this in [BUILDING.md](http://BUILDING.md):

> The runtime is arch-specific — a G3 binary won't run on a G4 host.

is that true?  I thought most G3 binaries were forward-compatible?

---

## 🤖 Claude

You're right — I overstated it. The CPU compatibility goes:

- **G3 binary** (`-mcpu=750`, no AltiVec): runs on G3, G4, **and** G5 hardware. PPC instruction set is subset-additive going up.
- **G4 binary** (`-mcpu=7450`): uses AltiVec, so it runs on G4 and G5, **not** G3.
- **G5 binary** (`-mcpu=G5 -D_PPC970_`): uses 64-bit-aware paths, so it runs on G5 only.

The reason the install *feels* arch-specific is that the runtime binary depends on `libmozglue.dylib` from `/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-{g3,g4,g5}/`, and the SpiderMonkey C++ itself was compiled with each arch's `-mcpu`. So the G4 mozjs uses AltiVec instructions in autovec'd loops — which crash on a G3. The CPU lock comes from the bundled mozjs, not the runtime.

Practical upshot: a G3 *runtime tarball* paired with the G3 *mozjs install* works fine on a G5 box. Just slower than a G5-native pair.

Let me fix the doc:

## 🤖 Claude

Here's the full path. Three personas — pick the one that matches what you have:

## Persona A — "I just want to use it on a Tiger PPC box"

No build needed. Grab the prebuilt tarballs from a release:

```bash
# One-time: SpiderMonkey + IonPower JIT (G3 example; same shape for g4/g5)
ssh ibookg37
curl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.73/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz
sudo tar xzpf mozjs-45-ionpower-g3.tar.gz -C /opt/

# Per-release: the runtime
curl -L -O https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/releases/download/v0.82/ionpower-node-0.82-g3-ppc.tar.gz
sudo tar xzpf ionpower-node-0.82-g3-ppc.tar.gz -C /opt/

# Use it
/opt/ionpower-node-0.82/bin/node test/hello.js
```

## Persona B — "I have one PPC Tiger host, want to build from source"

Same prereq: `/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-{g3,g4,g5}/` already present (one-time install per the v0.73 release). Then:

```bash
# Get the source onto the PPC host (any way you like — git clone, scp, rsync)
git clone https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node /Users/macuser/tmp/ionpower-node
cd /Users/macuser/tmp/ionpower-node

# Build. CPU flags + MOZJS_PREFIX are arch-specific:
#   g3:  -mcpu=750  -mtune=750         /opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3
#   g4:  -mcpu=7450 -mtune=7450        /opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g4
#   g5:  -mcpu=G5   -D_PPC970_         /opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g5
#                                      (g5 also needs /opt/make-4.3/bin/make,
#                                       Tiger's stock make 3.80 chokes on
#                                       the rules)
make MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS="-mcpu=750 -mtune=750"

# Quick sanity check
./node test/hello.js
```

The runtime is now `./node` in the source tree. You can also `make install PREFIX=/opt/ionpower-node-myversion` to drop it under `/opt`.

## Persona C — "I have my own three-host triad and want to mimic the project's release flow"

That's what [`scripts/triad-build.sh`](scripts/triad-build.sh) automates. Edit the host names in there to match yours (defaults are `ibookg37`, `emac`, `pmacg5`). Then from your dev box (the one driving the build):

```bash
# From the project root on your dev box (not on the PPC host).
# rsync's the source to the host, builds, runs all tests, installs to /opt,
# tarballs the result back into /tmp/ionpower-node-<ver>-<arch>-ppc.tar.gz.
scripts/triad-build.sh g3 0.82
scripts/triad-build.sh g4 0.82
scripts/triad-build.sh g5 0.82
```

Each invocation takes 8–15 minutes on G3, faster on G4/G5. Output streams to your terminal; final tarball lives on the PPC host at `/tmp/ionpower-node-0.82-<arch>-ppc.tar.gz`. Every release in the project's history followed this exact flow.

## Running the tests

After building (any persona):

```bash
# Core suite — the small set that exercises the runtime's primitives
make MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS="-mcpu=750 -mtune=750" test
# 13 fast smokes: hello, require_chain, fs, timers, util.inspect,
# console formatting, promises, jit_smoke, etc. All under 5 s combined.

# Library suite — the big one (~432 wired smokes, 1990+ assertions)
make MOZJS_PREFIX=/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-g3 CPU_FLAGS="-mcpu=750 -mtune=750" test-libs
# Every smoke under test/*_smoke.js that's wired into the Makefile.
# Takes ~3-5 min on G3. Stops at the first failure.

# Both at once
make test-all
```

## Running conformance sweeps (optional)

Two upstream test corpora are wired up. They're not part of `make test-all` — they're separate, take 30–90 minutes each, and require external corpus checkouts.

### One-time corpus setup

```bash
# Both go under external/ (gitignored).
mkdir -p external/wpt external/node-tests

# WPT subset (~180 MB)
cd external/wpt
git init -q
git remote add origin https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt.git
git config core.sparseCheckout true
printf '/url/\n/streams/\n/WebCryptoAPI/\n/encoding/\n/fetch/api/\n/resources/\n' > .git/info/sparse-checkout
git fetch --depth=1 origin master && git checkout master
cd ../..

# Node test subset (~124 MB)
cd external/node-tests
git init -q
git remote add origin https://github.com/nodejs/node.git
git config core.sparseCheckout true
printf '/test/common/\n/test/parallel/test-buffer-*\n/test/parallel/test-path-*\n/test/parallel/test-querystring-*\n/test/parallel/test-url-*\n/test/parallel/test-events-*\n/test/parallel/test-stream-*\n/test/parallel/test-crypto-*\n/test/parallel/test-zlib-*\n/test/parallel/test-fs-*\n/test/parallel/test-string-decoder*\n/test/parallel/test-assert-*\n' > .git/info/sparse-checkout
git fetch --depth=1 origin main && git checkout main
cd ../..
```

### Run the sweeps

```bash
# WPT (~90 min on G3)
./node scripts/conformance/run-wpt.js encoding url streams WebCryptoAPI
# Per-test detail in docs/conformance/wpt-results/*.jsonl
# Headline: ~560 / 9003 (6.2%) on v0.82 — see docs/conformance/README.md
# for the failure pattern analysis.

# Node parallel-tests (~60 min, fs subset is currently broken — runner
# can't reliably isolate forked grandchildren; skip with explicit topic list)
./node scripts/conformance/run-node-tests.js assert buffer path querystring \
    url events stream string-decoder zlib crypto
# Headline: ~49 / 557 (8.8%) on v0.82.
```

Both runners support resume — kill them mid-run, restart, and they pick up from where `summary.tsv` left off.

## Demos

After building, all three demos run from the source tree:

```bash
./node demos/chat/server.js          # then visit http://<host>:8080/
./node demos/paste/server.js 8090    # then visit http://<host>:8090/
./node demos/express-chat/server.js  # then visit http://<host>:8080/
```

`demos/paste/client.js` and `demos/express-chat/client.js` are CLI smokes that round-trip through the full HTTP/crypto/encryption pipeline; run them in a second terminal on the same host.

## 🤖 Claude

I don't think the Claude Desktop app has a setting to turn off markdown rendering in the input — the autolinking is baked into the editor.

Workarounds that work today:

- **Backtick the offending token**: `` `tiger.sh` `` and `` `http://leopard.sh/...` `` both render as plain code, no link. This is the cleanest fix for technical writing.
- **Triple-backtick fenced blocks** for multi-line shell snippets — what you started doing in your last message. The contents of a fence aren't autolinked.
- **Zero-width space trick**: insert a U+200B before `.sh` so it doesn't look like a TLD. Works but ugly and you can't see what you typed.
- **Escape the dot**: `tiger\.sh` — but the desktop app may strip the backslash on send.

For your use case (briefing me on a task), backticks are the right tool: `` `tiger.sh` ``, `` `/opt/openssl-1.1.1t/` ``, fenced block for the curl command. I read those identically to plain text, and you don't have to fight the editor.

If you want the feature properly, the Claude Desktop feedback channel (Help menu → "Send Feedback" or the support form) is where to file it — "make markdown autoformatting toggleable in the composer."

SSL_VERIFY_PEER : SSL_VERIFY_NONE,\n                       nullptr);\n\n    int id = g_nextCtxId++;\n    g_ctxs[id] = ctx;\n    args.rval().setInt32(id);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic bool JsCreateServerCtx(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    EnsureInit();\n    if (args.length() < 1 || !args[0].isObject()) {\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"createServerCtx: opts required\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    JS::RootedObject opts(cx, &args[0].toObject());\n\n    std::string certPem, keyPem;\n\n    JS::RootedValue cv(cx);\n    if (!JS_GetProperty(cx, opts, \"certPem\", &cv) || !cv.isString()) {\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"createServerCtx: certPem required\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    {\n        JSAutoByteString bs;\n        if (!TlsEncodeStrUtf8(cx, cv.toString(), &bs)) return false;\n        certPem = bs.ptr();\n    }\n\n    JS::RootedValue kv(cx);\n    if (!JS_GetProperty(cx, opts, \"keyPem\", &kv) || !kv.isString()) {\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"createServerCtx: keyPem required\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    {\n        JSAutoByteString bs;\n        if (!TlsEncodeStrUtf8(cx, kv.toString(), &bs)) return false;\n        keyPem = bs.ptr();\n    }\n\n    SSL_CTX* ctx = SSL_CTX_new(TLS_server_method());\n    if (!ctx) {\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"SSL_CTX_new (server) failed: %s\", DrainErrors().c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    SSL_CTX_set_min_proto_version(ctx, TLS1_2_VERSION);\n    SSL_CTX_set_options(ctx, SSL_OP_NO_COMPRESSION);\n    // Disable session resumption tickets \u2014 keeps things simple on a slow box.\n    SSL_CTX_set_options(ctx, SSL_OP_NO_TICKET);\n\n    // Load cert chain (cert may be a single cert or a full chain in one PEM).\n    BIO* certBio = BIO_new_mem_buf(certPem.data(), (int)certPem.size());\n    if (!certBio) { SSL_CTX_free(ctx); JS_ReportError(cx, \"BIO_new_mem_buf cert\"); return false; }\n    X509* leaf = PEM_read_bio_X509(certBio, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);\n    if (!leaf) {\n        std::string e = DrainErrors();\n        BIO_free(certBio); SSL_CTX_free(ctx);\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"parse certPem: %s\", e.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    if (SSL_CTX_use_certificate(ctx, leaf) != 1) {\n        std::string e = DrainErrors();\n        X509_free(leaf); BIO_free(certBio); SSL_CTX_free(ctx);\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"use cert: %s\", e.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    X509_free(leaf);\n    // Append any further certs in the PEM as the chain.\n    for (;;) {\n        X509* x = PEM_read_bio_X509(certBio, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);\n        if (!x) break;\n        SSL_CTX_add_extra_chain_cert(ctx, x);  // takes ownership\n    }\n    ERR_clear_error();\n    BIO_free(certBio);\n\n    // Load private key.\n    BIO* keyBio = BIO_new_mem_buf(keyPem.data(), (int)keyPem.size());\n    if (!keyBio) { SSL_CTX_free(ctx); JS_ReportError(cx, \"BIO_new_mem_buf key\"); return false; }\n    EVP_PKEY* pkey = PEM_read_bio_PrivateKey(keyBio, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);\n    if (!pkey) {\n        std::string e = DrainErrors();\n        BIO_free(keyBio); SSL_CTX_free(ctx);\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"parse keyPem: %s\", e.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    if (SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey(ctx, pkey) != 1) {\n        std::string e = DrainErrors();\n        EVP_PKEY_free(pkey); BIO_free(keyBio); SSL_CTX_free(ctx);\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"use key: %s\", e.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    EVP_PKEY_free(pkey);\n    BIO_free(keyBio);\n    if (SSL_CTX_check_private_key(ctx) != 1) {\n        std::string e = DrainErrors();\n        SSL_CTX_free(ctx);\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"key/cert mismatch: %s\", e.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    int id = g_nextCtxId++;\n    g_ctxs[id] = ctx;\n    args.rval().setInt32(id);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic bool JsFreeCtx(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    int32_t id = 0;\n    if (args.length() >= 1 && JS::ToInt32(cx, args[0], &id)) {\n        std::map<int, SSL_CTX*>::iterator it = g_ctxs.find(id);\n        if (it != g_ctxs.end()) {\n            SSL_CTX_free(it->second);\n            g_ctxs.erase(it);\n        }\n    }\n    args.rval().setUndefined();\n    return true;\n}\n\n// --- conn creation -------------------------------------------------\n\nstatic bool JsCreateConn(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"createConn: ctxId\"); return false; }\n    int32_t ctxId = 0;\n    if (!JS::ToInt32(cx, args[0], &ctxId)) return false;\n    bool isServer = args.length() >= 2 && JS::ToBoolean(args[1]);\n\n    std::map<int, SSL_CTX*>::iterator it = g_ctxs.find(ctxId);\n    if (it == g_ctxs.end()) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"createConn: bad ctxId %d\", ctxId); return false; }\n    SSL_CTX* ctx = it->second;\n\n    SSL* ssl = SSL_new(ctx);\n    if (!ssl) {\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"SSL_new: %s\", DrainErrors().c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    BIO* internal = nullptr;\n    BIO* netBio = nullptr;\n    if (BIO_new_bio_pair(&internal, 32 * 1024, &netBio, 32 * 1024) != 1) {\n        std::string e = DrainErrors();\n        SSL_free(ssl);\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"BIO_new_bio_pair: %s\", e.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    SSL_set_bio(ssl, internal, internal);  // SSL takes ownership of internal\n\n    if (isServer) SSL_set_accept_state(ssl);\n    else          SSL_set_connect_state(ssl);\n\n    TlsConn* conn = new TlsConn();\n    conn->ctx = ctx;\n    conn->ssl = ssl;\n    conn->netBio = netBio;\n    conn->isServer = isServer;\n    conn->handshakeDone = false;\n\n    int id = g_nextConnId++;\n    g_conns[id] = conn;\n    args.rval().setInt32(id);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic bool JsFreeConn(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    int32_t id = 0;\n    if (args.length() >= 1 && JS::ToInt32(cx, args[0], &id)) {\n        std::map<int, TlsConn*>::iterator it = g_conns.find(id);\n        if (it != g_conns.end()) {\n            TlsConn* c = it->second;\n            if (c->ssl) SSL_free(c->ssl);  // also frees its internal BIO\n            if (c->netBio) BIO_free(c->netBio);\n            delete c;\n            g_conns.erase(it);\n        }\n    }\n    args.rval().setUndefined();\n    return true;\n}\n\n// --- helpers -------------------------------------------------------\n\nstatic TlsConn* GetConn(JSContext* cx, JS::HandleValue v) {\n    int32_t id = 0;\n    if (!JS::ToInt32(cx, v, &id)) return nullptr;\n    std::map<int, TlsConn*>::iterator it = g_conns.find(id);\n    if (it == g_conns.end()) {\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"tls conn not found: %d\", id);\n        return nullptr;\n    }\n    return it->second;\n}\n\n// --- SNI -----------------------------------------------------------\n\nstatic bool JsSetServername(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 2) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"setServername: connId, host\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    if (!args[1].isString()) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"setServername: host must be string\"); return false; }\n    JSAutoByteString bs;\n    if (!TlsEncodeStrUtf8(cx, args[1].toString(), &bs)) return false;\n    if (!c->isServer) {\n        SSL_set_tlsext_host_name(c->ssl, bs.ptr());\n        // Also set hostname for cert verification (if rejectUnauthorized).\n        X509_VERIFY_PARAM* param = SSL_get0_param(c->ssl);\n        X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set_hostflags(param, X509_CHECK_FLAG_NO_PARTIAL_WILDCARDS);\n        X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_host(param, bs.ptr(), 0);\n    }\n    args.rval().setUndefined();\n    return true;\n}\n\n// --- handshake -----------------------------------------------------\n\nstatic bool JsHandshake(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"handshake: connId\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n\n    int r = SSL_do_handshake(c->ssl);\n    const char* state;\n    if (r == 1) {\n        c->handshakeDone = true;\n        state = \"connected\";\n    } else {\n        int err = SSL_get_error(c->ssl, r);\n        if (err == SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ)  state = \"want_read\";\n        else if (err == SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE) state = \"want_write\";\n        else {\n            std::string e = DrainErrors();\n            // Surface verify-failure separately for nicer JS error messages.\n            long vr = SSL_get_verify_result(c->ssl);\n            if (vr != X509_V_OK) {\n                JS_ReportError(cx, \"TLS handshake failed: %s (verify: %s)\",\n                               e.empty() ? \"unknown\" : e.c_str(),\n                               X509_verify_cert_error_string(vr));\n            } else {\n                JS_ReportError(cx, \"TLS handshake failed: %s\",\n                               e.empty() ? \"unknown\" : e.c_str());\n            }\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    JS::RootedString s(cx, JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, state));\n    if (!s) return false;\n    args.rval().setString(s);\n    return true;\n}\n\n// --- BIO bridge ----------------------------------------------------\n\n// bioWrite(connId, encBytes) \u2014 pushes encrypted bytes into the network\n// BIO so SSL machinery sees them as \"incoming from peer\". Returns the\n// number of bytes consumed (may be less than provided if BIO is full).\nstatic bool JsBioWrite(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 2) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"bioWrite: connId, data\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    std::string data;\n    if (!ExtractUint8(cx, args[1], &data)) return false;\n    if (data.empty()) { args.rval().setInt32(0); return true; }\n    int n = BIO_write(c->netBio, data.data(), (int)data.size());\n    if (n <= 0) {\n        if (BIO_should_retry(c->netBio)) { args.rval().setInt32(0); return true; }\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"BIO_write: %s\", DrainErrors().c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    args.rval().setInt32(n);\n    return true;\n}\n\n// bioRead(connId, max) \u2014 pulls encrypted bytes from the network BIO\n// (these are bytes SSL wants to send out to the peer). Returns a\n// Uint8Array, possibly empty.\nstatic bool JsBioRead(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"bioRead: connId\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    int32_t max = 16384;\n    if (args.length() >= 2 && !JS::ToInt32(cx, args[1], &max)) return false;\n    if (max <= 0 || max > (1 << 20)) max = 16384;\n\n    std::string buf; buf.resize(max);\n    int n = BIO_read(c->netBio, &buf[0], max);\n    if (n <= 0) {\n        if (BIO_should_retry(c->netBio)) n = 0;\n        else n = 0;\n    }\n    JS::RootedObject u8(cx, JS_NewUint8Array(cx, (uint32_t)n));\n    if (!u8) return false;\n    if (n > 0) {\n        JS::AutoCheckCannotGC nogc;\n        bool shared;\n        uint8_t* dst = JS_GetUint8ArrayData(u8, &shared, nogc);\n        if (!dst) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"bioRead: alloc\"); return false; }\n        memcpy(dst, buf.data(), (size_t)n);\n    }\n    args.rval().setObject(*u8);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic bool JsBioPending(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"bioPending: connId\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    args.rval().setInt32((int32_t)BIO_pending(c->netBio));\n    return true;\n}\n\n// --- SSL read/write ------------------------------------------------\n\nstatic bool JsSslWrite(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 2) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"sslWrite: connId, data\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    std::string data;\n    if (!ExtractUint8(cx, args[1], &data)) return false;\n    if (data.empty()) { args.rval().setInt32(0); return true; }\n    int n = SSL_write(c->ssl, data.data(), (int)data.size());\n    if (n <= 0) {\n        int err = SSL_get_error(c->ssl, n);\n        if (err == SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ || err == SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE) {\n            args.rval().setInt32(0); return true;\n        }\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"SSL_write: %s\", DrainErrors().c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    args.rval().setInt32(n);\n    return true;\n}\n\n// sslRead(connId, max) -> { bytes:Uint8Array(may be 0-length), eof:bool, wantRead:bool }\nstatic bool JsSslRead(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"sslRead: connId\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    int32_t max = 16384;\n    if (args.length() >= 2 && !JS::ToInt32(cx, args[1], &max)) return false;\n    if (max <= 0 || max > (1 << 20)) max = 16384;\n\n    std::string buf; buf.resize(max);\n    int n = SSL_read(c->ssl, &buf[0], max);\n\n    JS::RootedObject out(cx, JS_NewPlainObject(cx));\n    if (!out) return false;\n    bool eof = false, wantRead = false;\n    int gotN = 0;\n    if (n > 0) {\n        gotN = n;\n    } else {\n        int err = SSL_get_error(c->ssl, n);\n        if (err == SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ || err == SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE) {\n            wantRead = true;\n        } else if (err == SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN) {\n            eof = true;\n        } else if (err == SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL && n == 0) {\n            // Peer closed without close_notify \u2014 treat as eof.\n            eof = true;\n        } else {\n            std::string e = DrainErrors();\n            JS_ReportError(cx, \"SSL_read: %s\", e.empty() ? \"unknown\" : e.c_str());\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    JS::RootedObject u8(cx, JS_NewUint8Array(cx, (uint32_t)gotN));\n    if (!u8) return false;\n    if (gotN > 0) {\n        JS::AutoCheckCannotGC nogc;\n        bool shared;\n        uint8_t* dst = JS_GetUint8ArrayData(u8, &shared, nogc);\n        if (!dst) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"sslRead: alloc\"); return false; }\n        memcpy(dst, buf.data(), (size_t)gotN);\n    }\n    JS::RootedValue v(cx);\n    v.setObject(*u8);    JS_DefineProperty(cx, out, \"bytes\",    v, JSPROP_ENUMERATE);\n    v.setBoolean(eof);   JS_DefineProperty(cx, out, \"eof\",      v, JSPROP_ENUMERATE);\n    v.setBoolean(wantRead); JS_DefineProperty(cx, out, \"wantRead\", v, JSPROP_ENUMERATE);\n    args.rval().setObject(*out);\n    return true;\n}\n\n// --- shutdown ------------------------------------------------------\n\nstatic bool JsShutdownConn(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"shutdownConn: connId\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    int r = SSL_shutdown(c->ssl);\n    const char* state;\n    if (r >= 1) state = \"done\";\n    else if (r == 0) state = \"want_read\";   // we sent close_notify; peer hasn't yet\n    else {\n        int err = SSL_get_error(c->ssl, r);\n        if (err == SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ)  state = \"want_read\";\n        else if (err == SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE) state = \"want_write\";\n        else state = \"done\";  // best-effort: don't error on shutdown\n    }\n    JS::RootedString s(cx, JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, state));\n    if (!s) return false;\n    args.rval().setString(s);\n    return true;\n}\n\n// --- introspection -------------------------------------------------\n\nstatic JSString* MakeAsn1String(JSContext* cx, const ASN1_STRING* s) {\n    if (!s) return JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, \"\");\n    unsigned char* utf8 = nullptr;\n    int len = ASN1_STRING_to_UTF8(&utf8, const_cast<ASN1_STRING*>(s));\n    if (len < 0 || !utf8) return JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, \"\");\n    JSString* out = JS_NewStringCopyN(cx, reinterpret_cast<const char*>(utf8), len);\n    OPENSSL_free(utf8);\n    return out;\n}\n\nstatic JSString* MakeX509NameString(JSContext* cx, X509_NAME* name) {\n    if (!name) return JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, \"\");\n    char* dn = X509_NAME_oneline(name, nullptr, 0);\n    if (!dn) return JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, \"\");\n    JSString* s = JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, dn);\n    OPENSSL_free(dn);\n    return s;\n}\n\nstatic JSString* MakeAsn1TimeString(JSContext* cx, const ASN1_TIME* t) {\n    if (!t) return JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, \"\");\n    BIO* b = BIO_new(BIO_s_mem());\n    if (!b) return JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, \"\");\n    ASN1_TIME_print(b, t);\n    char* data = nullptr;\n    long n = BIO_get_mem_data(b, &data);\n    JSString* s = (n > 0 && data)\n        ? JS_NewStringCopyN(cx, data, (size_t)n)\n        : JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, \"\");\n    BIO_free(b);\n    return s;\n}\n\nstatic bool JsGetPeerCert(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"getPeerCert: connId\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    X509* peer = SSL_get_peer_certificate(c->ssl);\n    if (!peer) { args.rval().setNull(); return true; }\n\n    JS::RootedObject o(cx, JS_NewPlainObject(cx));\n    if (!o) { X509_free(peer); return false; }\n\n    JS::RootedString sub(cx, MakeX509NameString(cx, X509_get_subject_name(peer)));\n    JS::RootedValue subv(cx, JS::StringValue(sub));\n    JS_DefineProperty(cx, o, \"subject\", subv, JSPROP_ENUMERATE);\n\n    JS::RootedString iss(cx, MakeX509NameString(cx, X509_get_issuer_name(peer)));\n    JS::RootedValue issv(cx, JS::StringValue(iss));\n    JS_DefineProperty(cx, o, \"issuer\", issv, JSPROP_ENUMERATE);\n\n    JS::RootedString vfrom(cx, MakeAsn1TimeString(cx, X509_get0_notBefore(peer)));\n    JS::RootedValue vfv(cx, JS::StringValue(vfrom));\n    JS_DefineProperty(cx, o, \"valid_from\", vfv, JSPROP_ENUMERATE);\n\n    JS::RootedString vto(cx, MakeAsn1TimeString(cx, X509_get0_notAfter(peer)));\n    JS::RootedValue vtv(cx, JS::StringValue(vto));\n    JS_DefineProperty(cx, o, \"valid_to\", vtv, JSPROP_ENUMERATE);\n\n    X509_free(peer);\n    args.rval().setObject(*o);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic bool JsGetCipher(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"getCipher: connId\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    const char* name = SSL_get_cipher(c->ssl);\n    JS::RootedString s(cx, JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, name ? name : \"\"));\n    if (!s) return false;\n    args.rval().setString(s);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic bool JsGetProtocol(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    if (args.length() < 1) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"getProtocol: connId\"); return false; }\n    TlsConn* c = GetConn(cx, args[0]);\n    if (!c) return false;\n    const char* name = SSL_get_version(c->ssl);\n    JS::RootedString s(cx, JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, name ? name : \"\"));\n    if (!s) return false;\n    args.rval().setString(s);\n    return true;\n}\n\nstatic bool JsVersionText(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    JS::RootedString s(cx, JS_NewStringCopyZ(cx, OPENSSL_VERSION_TEXT));\n    if (!s) return false;\n    args.rval().setString(s);\n    return true;\n}\n\n// --- self-signed cert helper for demos / tests ---------------------\n// Generates an RSA-2048 keypair + self-signed cert valid for `days`.\n// Returns { keyPem, certPem }. Slow on a G3 \u2014 about 8-15 seconds.\nstatic bool JsGenerateSelfSigned(JSContext* cx, unsigned argc, JS::Value* vp) {\n    JS::CallArgs args = JS::CallArgsFromVp(argc, vp);\n    EnsureInit();\n\n    std::string commonName = \"localhost\";\n    int days = 365;\n    if (args.length() >= 1 && args[0].isString()) {\n        JSAutoByteString bs;\n        if (!TlsEncodeStrUtf8(cx, args[0].toString(), &bs)) return false;\n        commonName = bs.ptr();\n    }\n    if (args.length() >= 2) {\n        int32_t d = days;\n        if (JS::ToInt32(cx, args[1], &d)) days = d;\n    }\n\n    EVP_PKEY* pkey = EVP_PKEY_new();\n    if (!pkey) { JS_ReportError(cx, \"EVP_PKEY_new\"); return false; }\n\n    BIGNUM* bne = BN_new();\n    BN_set_word(bne, RSA_F4);\n    RSA* rsa = RSA_new();\n    if (!RSA_generate_key_ex(rsa, 2048, bne, nullptr)) {\n        std::string e = DrainErrors();\n        BN_free(bne); RSA_free(rsa); EVP_PKEY_free(pkey);\n        JS_ReportError(cx, \"RSA_generate_key_ex: %s\", e.c_str());\n        return false;\n    }\n    BN_free(bne);\n    EVP_PKEY_assign_RSA(pkey, rsa);  // pkey owns rsa now\n\n    X509* x = X509_new();\n    if (!x) { EVP_PKEY_free(pkey); JS_ReportError(cx, \"X509_new\"); return false; }\n    ASN1_INTEGER_set(X509_get_serialNumber(x), 1);\n    X509_gmtime_adj(X509_getm_notBefore(x), 0);\n    X509_gmtime_adj(X509_getm_notAfter(x), 60L * 60L * 24L * days);\n    X509_set_pubkey(x, pkey);\n    X509_NAME* name = X509_get_subject_name(x);\n    X509_NAME_add_entry_by_txt(name, \"CN\", MBSTRING_ASC,\n                               (const unsigned char*)commonName.c_str(), -1, -1, 0);\n    X509_set_issuer_name(x, name);\n    if (!X509_sign(x, pkey, EVP_sha256())) {\n        std::string e = DrainErrors();\n        X509_free(x); Exits 0\n// on success.\n\nvar tls = require('tls');\nvar assert = require('assert');\n\nvar checks = 0;\nvar t0 = Date.now();\n\nvar sock = tls.connect({\n    host: 'example.com',\n    port: 443,\n    servername: 'example.com'\n}, function () {\n    checks++;\n    console.log('ok: secureConnect fired');\n\n    var proto = sock.getProtocol();\n    console.log('ok: protocol = ' + proto);\n    assert(proto === 'TLSv1.2' || proto === 'TLSv1.3', 'expected TLS 1.2 or 1.3');\n    checks++;\n\n    var cipher = sock.getCipher();\n    console.log('ok: cipher = ' + (cipher && cipher.name));\n    assert(cipher && cipher.name && cipher.name.length > 0, 'cipher name empty');\n    checks++;\n\n    var cert = sock.getPeerCertificate();\n    assert(cert && cert.subject, 'no peer cert');\n    console.log('ok: peer subject = ' + cert.subject);\n    console.log('ok: peer issuer  = ' + cert.issuer);\n    console.log('ok: valid_from   = ' + cert.valid_from);\n    console.log('ok: valid_to     = ' + cert.valid_to);\n    checks++;\n\n    sock.write('GET / HTTP/1.0\\r\\nHost: example.com\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n');\n});\n\nvar bodyChunks = [];\nvar totalBytes = 0;\n\nsock.on('data', function (chunk) {\n    totalBytes += chunk.length;\n    bodyChunks.push(chunk);\n});\n\nsock.on('end', function () {\n    var body = Buffer.concat(bodyChunks).toString('utf8');\n    assert(body.indexOf('HTTP/1') === 0, 'expected HTTP response, got: ' + body.slice(0, 80));\n    console.log('ok: status line = ' + body.split('\\r\\n')[0]);\n    checks++;\n    assert(totalBytes > 100, 'expected >100 bytes, got ' + totalBytes);\n    console.log('ok: total bytes received = ' + totalBytes);\n    checks++;\n\n    var dt = Date.now() - t0;\n    console.log('tls smoke: ok (' + checks + ' checks, ' + dt + ' ms)');\n});\n\nsock.on('error', function (e) {\n    console.error('tls error:', e && e.message ? e.message : e);\n    process.exit(1);\n});\n"

## 🤖 Claude

Found the bug. In `_pumpRead`, after emitting `'data'`, the user's handler may call `sock.destroy()` which sets `_connId = -1`. The next loop iteration calls `sslRead(-1)` which errors. The functional path works (we got the 200 response), but a stray "tls conn not found: -1" error fires after.

This is a pre-existing `_Socket.end()` bug — calling `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` immediately after `write()` to a remote socket loses the buffered data on Tiger. With a 50ms delay it works fine. Let me apply a `setImmediate` fix.

## 🤖 Claude

TCP_NODELAY fixes it! Let me revert the setImmediate change and instead set NoDelay by default in `_onConnected`. That's the conservative fix and matches what most HTTP clients do.

## 🤖 Claude

`setTimeout(0)` works, `setImmediate` doesn't — likely because setTimeout enters `select()` once, giving the kernel time to flush. Let me apply that as the fix.

  "content": "// demos/https/client.js \u2014 minimal HTTPS client.\n//\n// Fetches a URL over HTTPS and prints the response + TLS metadata.\n//\n//   ./node demos/https/client.js [URL]\n//\n// Defaults to https://127.0.0.1:8443/info (paired with server.js).\n// Pass any HTTPS URL to fetch from the public web \u2014 example.com,\n// httpbin.org/ip, etc. With -k it will skip cert validation, useful\n// when hitting the demo server's self-signed cert.\n\nvar https = require('https');\nvar url   = require('url');\n\nvar args = process.argv.slice(2);\nvar insecure = false;\nvar target = null;\nfor (var i = 0; i < args.length; ++i) {\n    if (args[i] === '-k' || args[i] === '--insecure') insecure = true;\n    else if (target === null) target = args[i];\n}\nif (!target) target = 'https://127.0.0.1:8443/info';\n\nvar u = url.parse(target);\nif (u.protocol !== 'https:') {\n    console.error('client: only https:// URLs are supported');\n    process.exit(2);\n}\n\n// Default to insecure when hitting the local demo server (self-signed\n// cert), but require -k for any other host.\nif (!insecure && (u.hostname === '127.0.0.1' || u.hostname === 'localhost')) {\n    insecure = true;\n}\n\nvar t0 = Date.now();\n\nconsole.error('GET ' + target + (insecure ? '   (-k: skipping cert validation)' : ''));\n\nvar req = https.get({\n    hostname: u.hostname,\n    port:     parseInt(u.port || 443, 10),\n    path:     u.path || '/',\n    rejectUnauthorized: !insecure,\n    headers: {\n        'User-Agent': 'ionpower-https-demo-client',\n        'Accept':     'application/json, text/html, */*'\n    }\n}, function (res) {\n    console.error('< HTTP/' + res.httpVersion + ' ' + res.statusCode + ' ' + (res.statusMessage || ''));\n\n    // Print headers in the order received.\n    Object.keys(res.headers).forEach(function (k) {\n        console.error('< ' + k + ': ' + res.headers[k]);\n    });\n\n    var sock = res.socket;\n    if (sock) {\n        var proto  = sock.getProtocol ? sock.getProtocol() : null;\n        var cipher = sock.getCipher   ? sock.getCipher()   : null;\n        var cert   = sock.getPeerCertificate ? sock.getPeerCertificate() : null;\n        console.error('');\n        console.error('---- TLS info ----');\n        console.error('  protocol: ' + proto);\n        console.error('  cipher:   ' + (cipher && cipher.name));\n        if (cert && cert.subject) {\n            console.error('  peer cert subject: ' + cert.subject);\n            console.error('  peer cert issuer:  ' + cert.issuer);\n            console.error('  valid_from: ' + cert.valid_from);\n            console.error('  valid_to:   ' + cert.valid_to);\n        }\n        console.error('------------------');\n    }\n\n    var bodyChunks = [];\n    res.on('data', function (c) { bodyChunks.push(c); });\n    res.on('end', function () {\n        var body = Buffer.concat(bodyChunks).toString('utf8');\n        var dt = Date.now() - t0;\n        // Pretty-print JSON; pass HTML/text through.\n        var ct = (res.headers['content-type'] || '').toLowerCase();\n        if (ct.indexOf('json') >= 0) {\n            try { body = JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(body), null, 2); } catch (e) {}\n        }\n        process.stdout.write(body);\n        if (body.length && body.charAt(body.length - 1) !== '\\n') process.stdout.write('\\n');\n        console.error('\\n(' + body.length + ' bytes, ' + dt + ' ms)');\n    });\n});\n\nreq.on('error', function (e) {\n    console.error('error: ' + (e && e.message ? e.message : e));\n    process.exit(1);\n});\n"

  "file_path": "/Users/cell/claude/ionpower-node/demos/https/README.md",
  "content": "# demos/https \u2014 TLS-secured HTTP server + client\n\nA minimal showcase of the `tls` and `https` modules added in v0.83.\n\n- **`server.js`** \u2014 HTTPS server with a self-signed cert generated at\n  startup. Three routes: `/`, `/info`, `/echo?msg=`.\n- **`client.js`** \u2014 CLI HTTPS client. Fetches a URL, prints headers,\n  TLS metadata (protocol, cipher, peer cert), and the response body.\n  Defaults to talking to the local server but accepts any HTTPS URL.\n\n## Run\n\nIn one terminal:\n\n```bash\n./node demos/https/server.js\n# generating self-signed RSA-2048 cert (slow on G3 ~6 s)...\n# cert generated in 5837 ms\n# listening on https://0.0.0.0:8443/\n```\n\nIn a second terminal:\n\n```bash\n# Hit the local server (auto-skips cert validation since it's self-signed):\n./node demos/https/client.js\n# < HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n# < content-type: application/json\n# ...\n# ---- TLS info ----\n#   protocol: TLSv1.3\n#   cipher:   TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384\n#   peer cert subject: /CN=ionpower-https-demo\n#   ...\n\n# Or any public HTTPS URL:\n./node demos/https/client.js https://example.com/\n./node demos/https/client.js https://httpbin.org/ip\n\n# Pass -k to skip cert validation against a non-localhost host:\n./node demos/https/client.js -k https://self-signed.badssl.com/\n```\n\nIn a browser, open `https://<host>:8443/`. Accept the self-signed cert\nwarning to see a small status page with TLS details.\n\n## What this demonstrates\n\nThe `tls` and `https` modules in ionpower-node are real \u2014 they link\nagainst OpenSSL 1.1.1t and use the same TLS state machine that\nproduction Node uses. From your code's perspective:\n\n```javascript\nvar https = require('https');\nhttps.get('https://example.com/', function (res) {\n    res.on('data', ...);  // decrypted bytes\n    res.on('end',  ...);\n});\n```\n\nThe client demo also reaches into `socket.getProtocol()`,\n`socket.getCipher()`, and `socket.getPeerCertificate()` \u2014 all\nimplemented on top of OpenSSL's `SSL_get_version`, `SSL_get_cipher`,\nand `SSL_get_peer_certificate`.\n\nThe server demo uses `tls.generateSelfSigned(commonName, days)`, an\nionpower-node helper that wraps OpenSSL's keygen + X.509 signing for\nno-fuss demos. For real deployments you'd point `cert` and `key` at\nPEM files (or paths to PEM files) on disk:\n\n```javascript\nhttps.createServer({\n    cert: fs.readFileSync('/etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem'),\n    key:  fs.readFileSync('/etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem')\n}, handler).listen(443);\n```\n\n## Notes\n\n- The server uses a fresh self-signed cert on every restart. Browsers\n  will keep warning unless you click through.\n- TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 are both supported; 1.3 is preferred by default.\n- The HTTPS request and response framing (chunked / Content-Length /\n  keep-alive) reuses the existing `http` parser. Only the socket type\n  is different.\n- See [`BUILDING.md`](../../BUILDING.md) for the OpenSSL prerequisite.\n"
}

  "new_string": "## Documentation as I go\n\nWill write running log here as I make decisions, hit dead ends, or\nroll things back.\n\n## Running log\n\n### Recon (Explore agent)\n\nArchitecture map back from the agent: native modules expose\n`__name_native__` to JS, all JS shims live in a single 8900-line\n`kBootstrapJS` C string in `globals.cpp`, the JS-level `net.Socket`\nwraps `__net_native__` + `__child_process_native__.{readFd,writeFd}`,\nand the http parser is pure JS. No async/await, must respect\n`-fno-exceptions -fno-rtti`. node-forge has a TLS impl but it's\npure-JS and would be unbearably slow on a G3. Native OpenSSL is the\nright call.\n\n### OpenSSL pre-flight\n\nAll three triad hosts (`ibookg37`, `emac`, `pmacg5`) have OpenSSL\n1.1.1t installed at `/opt/openssl-1.1.1t/` with both `.a` and\n`.dylib` libs, headers, and `/opt/ca-certificates-20230110/share/cacert.pem`.\n\nSmoke-compiled a 50-line C TLS client on ibookg37 \u2014 TLS 1.3 with\nAES-256-GCM-SHA384 to example.com:443, 798 bytes back. Linker\nwarning about `-mlong-branch` in Apple's stock crt1.o is benign.\nDep is sound.\n\n### Native binding (`src/node_compat/tls.cpp`, ~530 LOC)\n\nDesign: opaque integer ctx/conn IDs (stored in `std::map`), memory\nBIO pair so the JS side fully drives I/O.  Key API:\n\n- `createClientCtx(opts)` / `createServerCtx(opts)` / `freeCtx`\n- `createConn(ctxId, isServer)` / `freeConn` \u2014 allocates `SSL` + `BIO_pair`\n- `setServername` (SNI)\n- `handshake` \u2014 drives `SSL_do_handshake`, returns\n  `'connected' | 'want_read' | 'want_write' | 'error'`\n- `bioWrite` (push encrypted bytes from network),\n  `bioRead` (pull encrypted bytes to send to network)\n- `sslWrite` (push plaintext app bytes \u2014 encrypted into BIO),\n  `sslRead` (pull decrypted plaintext)\n- `shutdownConn`, `getPeerCert`, `getCipher`, `getProtocol`,\n  `versionText`, `generateSelfSigned`\n\nCompiled cleanly on G3 first try (the Explore agent's pattern guide\nsaved a lot of time).\n\n### JS layer (kBootstrapJS additions, ~280 lines)\n\n`_TLSSocket` extends EventEmitter, owns an inner raw `_Socket`. On\nraw 'data' it `bioWrite`s, then either drives the handshake or\npumps `sslRead`+`sslWrite`. `connect()` mirrors `_Socket.connect`\nshape; emits `'secureConnect'` after handshake. `tls.connect` and\n`tls.createServer` follow the Node API.\n\nFor HTTPS I refactored `_ClientRequest` to accept an optional\n`opts.createConnection(opts, onReady)` factory \u2014 minimal change,\ndefault branch unchanged. `_httpsRequest` plugs in a TLS-backed\nfactory; `_httpsCreateServer` builds on `_tlsCreateServer` + the\nexisting http parser.\n\n### Bugs hit + fixes\n\n1. **`'end'` event firing twice.** SSL's `SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN` and\n   the underlying raw socket's `'end'` both triggered our `'end'`\n   emit. Added `_emitEndOnce` guard.\n\n2. **`tls conn not found: -1` errors after destroy.** In `_pumpRead`,\n   after we emitted `'data'` the listener could synchronously call\n   `sock.destroy()` (e.g. `_ClientRequest`'s `feedBody` does this on\n   Content-Length completion). The next loop iteration would call\n   `sslRead(-1)` and throw. Moved the destroyed check into the loop\n   condition itself.\n\n3. **The big one \u2014 `http.request` to remote servers silently\n   returning no response.** Initially I thought this was a TLS bug,\n   but reproduced with plain `net.createConnection + write + end`.\n   Bisected: with a 50ms `setTimeout` between `write` and `end`,\n   data arrives; without, the server FINs without responding.\n\n   Root cause: on Tiger PPC's BSD TCP stack, `shutdown(SHUT_WR)`\n   called in the same tick as `write()` to a non-blocking remote\n   socket can drop the in-flight bytes \u2014 the peer receives FIN\n   with no data and treats the request as malformed. (Pre-existing\n   bug, not from my refactor; `http_async_smoke` only worked\n   because it talks to a local server, where the loopback socket\n   doesn't have this race.)\n\n   Fixed in two places:\n   - `_Socket._onConnected`: `setNoDelay(true)` by default. Disables\n     Nagle so write isn't coalesced. (Mostly cosmetic \u2014 doesn't fix\n     the bug on its own but reduces the timing window.)\n   - `_Socket.end`: defer the actual `shutdown()` syscall by one\n     timer tick (`setTimeout(0)`). Routes through the timer wheel,\n     which enters `select()` once, giving the kernel a chance to\n     transmit before the half-close request arrives. `setImmediate`\n     is **not** sufficient \u2014 it doesn't wait for select.\n\n   With both fixes, `http.request` to example.com works reliably,\n   and so does `https.request` (which goes through the same path).\n\n### Smokes\n\nThree new smokes wired into `make test-libs`:\n\n- `test/tls_smoke.js` \u2014 `tls.connect` to example.com:443; checks\n  protocol, cipher, peer cert, GET round-trip (~800ms on G3).\n- `test/https_get_smoke.js` \u2014 `https.get` to example.com; checks\n  status, headers, body, \"Example Domain\" content (~800ms).\n- `test/https_server_smoke.js` \u2014 `tls.generateSelfSigned` \u2192\n  `https.createServer` \u2192 `https.get` to self \u2192 JSON round-trip\n  (~6.5s on G3, RSA keygen dominates).\n\n### Demo (`demos/https/`)\n\n- `server.js` \u2014 Self-signed HTTPS server with three routes (`/`,\n  `/info`, `/echo`). Browser-friendly status page with TLS\n  metadata; JSON inspection endpoint.\n- `client.js` \u2014 CLI HTTPS client. Auto-`-k` for localhost, `-k`\n  flag for explicit insecure mode. Prints headers, TLS info,\n  body. Default URL targets the local server.\n- `README.md` \u2014 usage walkthrough.\n\n### Still to do\n\n- Triad-build G4 + G5; cut v0.83 release.\n- Update README front-page to mention HTTPS."
}

## 🤖 Claude


🔧 Using tool: Write
Input: {
  "file_path": "/Users/cell/claude/ionpower-node/docs/sessions/2026-04-30-session-1-https/release-notes/v0.83.md",
  "content": "# ionpower-node v0.83\n\n**HTTPS support is real.** This release adds the `tls` and `https`\nmodules, linked against OpenSSL 1.1.1t, with a TLSSocket that wraps\n`net.Socket` and pumps bytes through a memory BIO pair. From your\ncode's point of view, `https.request` and `https.createServer` work\nexactly like Node's:\n\n```javascript\nvar https = require('https');\nhttps.get('https://example.com/', function (res) {\n    res.on('data', chunk => /* decrypted bytes */);\n});\n```\n\n`fetch('https://...')` no longer falls back to a sync curl shim \u2014 it\nuses the same async TLS path as `https.request`.\n\n## What's new\n\n- **`tls` module**: `tls.connect`, `tls.createServer`, `tls.TLSSocket`,\n  `tls.createSecureContext`, `tls.generateSelfSigned`. SNI, TLS 1.2 +\n  1.3, peer cert verification against the bundled CA bundle at\n  `/opt/ca-certificates-20230110/share/cacert.pem`.\n- **`https` module**: real async `https.request` / `https.get` /\n  `https.createServer` over `tls.TLSSocket` + the same HTTP/1.1\n  parser as `http`.\n- **`fetch()`** now uses `https.request` for `https://` URLs (was\n  falling back to sync curl).\n- **`process.versions.openssl`** populated from the linked OpenSSL.\n- **TLS introspection**: `socket.getProtocol()`, `getCipher()`,\n  `getPeerCertificate()` on `TLSSocket`.\n- **`tls.generateSelfSigned(commonName, days)`** \u2014 RSA-2048 keygen +\n  X.509 self-sign helper for demos and testing.\n\n## New demo\n\n`demos/https/` \u2014 minimal HTTPS server (self-signed cert, three routes)\n+ CLI client (auto-`-k` for localhost; works against any public HTTPS\nURL). See [`demos/https/README.md`](https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/blob/main/demos/https/README.md).\n\n## Bug fixes\n\n- **`_Socket.end()` race on Tiger PPC.** Calling `shutdown(SHUT_WR)`\n  in the same event-loop tick as `write()` to a remote socket dropped\n  in-flight bytes \u2014 the peer received FIN with no data and returned\n  no response. `http.request` to remote servers was silently failing\n  because of this. Fix: defer the shutdown by one timer tick\n  (`setTimeout(0)`), enabling the kernel to actually transmit the\n  buffered data first. Also enabled `TCP_NODELAY` by default in\n  `_Socket._onConnected`. Locally-talking code (`http_async_smoke`,\n  the chat / paste / express-chat demos) was unaffected because\n  loopback doesn't have this race.\n\n## Prerequisite\n\nOpenSSL 1.1.1t must be installed at `/opt/openssl-1.1.1t/` and the\ndefault trust bundle at `/opt/ca-certificates-20230110/share/cacert.pem`.\nTwo ways to install:\n\n```bash\n# Option 1: tiger.sh (project-friendly Tiger PPC pkg manager)\ntiger.sh install openssl-1.1.1t\n\n# Option 2: leopard.sh tarballs (G3 example; swap g3 -> g4 / g5 as needed)\ncd /opt\ncurl http://leopard.sh/dist/ca-certificates-20230110.tar.gz | gunzip | tar x\ncurl http://leopard.sh/binpkgs/openssl-1.1.1t.tiger.g3.tar.gz | gunzip | tar x\n```\n\nSee [`BUILDING.md`](https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/blob/main/BUILDING.md)\nfor the full install walkthrough.\n\n## Smokes\n\nThree new smokes wired into `make test-all`:\n\n- `test/tls_smoke.js` \u2014 `tls.connect` to example.com:443; verifies\n  protocol, cipher, peer cert, GET round-trip.\n- `test/https_get_smoke.js` \u2014 `https.get` round-trip with HTTP body\n  parsing.\n- `test/https_server_smoke.js` \u2014 generates a self-signed cert,\n  brings up an HTTPS server, makes a self-loop request through it.\n\n## Library count\n\nSame as v0.82 (no new third-party libs vendored this release).\n\n## Tarballs\n\n```\nionpower-node-0.83-g3-ppc.tar.gz\nionpower-node-0.83-g4-ppc.tar.gz\nionpower-node-0.83-g5-ppc.tar.gz\n```\n\nDrop in alongside `/opt/mozjs-45-ionpower-{g3,g4,g5}/` +\n`/opt/openssl-1.1.1t/` + `/opt/ca-certificates-20230110/`. See\n[`BUILDING.md`](https://github.com/cellularmitosis/ionpower-node/blob/main/BUILDING.md)\nfor the full layout.\n"
}
